# Multi-source SI network — Plan S3-C1: stage-3 P1 verified object-store backups and the restore-and-gate library Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Give every SI owner on devnet2 verified, incremental backups of its `hg_safe` in a versioned GCS bucket, written with a key that is confined to that owner's prefix and cannot delete, readable with read-only restore keys, and prove each one with a restore drill that gates the restored parts against the published manifest the backup names; land, now, the restore-and-gate library and the pure §8.5 install gate that Plan S3-C2's si-member reuses unchanged; and do all of it without a consensus change and without restarting any ClickHouse, host pod, verifier or voter (spec §16 P1: "tracks paused: none").

**Architecture:** housegate adds the replay helpers stage 3 needs from P1 on: `replay.OwnerEntry`, the exported ledger check `payloadexec.VerifyLedger` and `payloadexec.SumPartRowLtHashes`, `chexec.ScanAllParts` over every active part of a scratch, `chexec.NewMaterializerIn` (named database and prefix) and additive `chexec.NewMaterializerInWithStoragePolicy` (explicit member-disk policy; both older constructors unchanged) and `sitable.CopyTable`, releases `HG_TAG_P1`, and writes the stage-3 ledger tool `s3-ledger.py` (Task 22). arbiter-core pins `HG_TAG_P1`, extracts the partition helpers of the SNode into `dataplane/chparts` with `snode` delegating (applied on top of Plan S3-A Task 5's owner audit), and adds the pure gate `member/gate` (plan, scratch classifier, arithmetic closure) (Task 23); then `dataplane/objstore`: `S3()` builders, the backup index object, the chained full/incremental `Backuper`, `RestoreAndGate`, the restore `Drill` and its verdict, a manifest reader that applies the §8.4 accept rule, and mechanics M12–M14 against MinIO in the mechanics script (incremental BACKUP/RESTORE to an S3 endpoint keeps `hash_of_all_files`; what BACKUP needs to delete; secret masking), released as `CORE_TAG_P1` with the measured delete right `P1_BACKUP_DELETE` (Task 24). sentio-node pins both and adds `sentio-node storage-integrity backup` and `storage-integrity restore-drill`, which read a job config that needs no node identity and take every key and password from the environment, and releases `SN_COMMIT_P1` / `SN_DIGEST_P1` (Task 25). production adds the replica bucket, its no-delete backup service accounts (each confined to its prefix by a managed folder, K25) and read-only restore service accounts in Terraform, the installation-wide `si_backup` ClickHouse user (literal hash, users.d reload, grant-probe rows), a P1 staging installation with the staging-only `si_restore`, the `charts/sentio-node` `siBackup` CronJob outside the host checksum, the backup alerts, the users' key and login scripts and render tests (Task 26), and the P1 runbook and PR (Task 27). On devnet2 the user applies the Terraform and creates the keys; then the staging installation, the mechanics on GCS with the deployed image, `si_backup` on every installation, a drill table on indexer-b, one CronJob per owner with a full and an incremental backup each, one confirmed restore drill per owner, the backup alerts, and the P1 record (Task 28).

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.26; Bazel 9.1.0 + Bzlmod + gazelle (housegate, arbiter-core, sentio-node); ClickHouse 26.3 (`clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3.37.3` in CI and the release gate, `us-west1-docker.pkg.dev/sentio-352722/sentio/clickhouse-server:26.3-lts-decimal512-release-2026-09-16` on devnet2 and for the manual run, S3-A K9); MinIO `bitnamilegacy/minio:2024.12.18-debian-12-r1@sha256:c0ede65eb88e47138470202c517bacf55ab3c27df848030b7b46e69d34b7d192` with its bundled `mc` as the S3 endpoint of the mechanics pair; Google Cloud Storage through its S3-compatible XML API with HMAC keys, IAM custom roles and IAM Conditions; Terraform (backend Terraform Cloud `prod`, applied by the user with `-target`); Helm charts with `test_render.py` (Python 3, PyYAML), `helm lint --strict` and helmfile; the Altinity clickhouse-operator 0.27.2 (`devnet2-operator`, frozen, S3-B K22); kube-state-metrics, VictoriaMetrics VMRule and the Grafana delivery of S3-B K13; `kubectl`, `gcloud`, the runbook helpers and throwaway local tools (live steps); Python 3 for the ledger tool.

**Spec:** housegate `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-multi-source-si-stage3-database-groups-design.md` (on `main` since housegate#236, `fb83a97`, the text of the reviewed commit `a815dd0` with every review fix; its §8.2 `hg_rstage` rights as amended on the plans branch `urwt/claude/ms-si-stage3-plans-cf` by the stage-3 plans PR, decision D36) — binding: §16 row P1 and its exit criterion; §2's ClickHouse mechanics bullet for `BACKUP … PARTITIONS` with `base_backup` and `RESTORE … AS <staging> PARTITIONS`; §8.2's `hg_rstage` rights as amended (explicit `SELECT`, `INSERT`, `ALTER`, `CREATE TABLE`, `DROP TABLE`, `TRUNCATE` and `OPTIMIZE`, never `ALL`), which the staging-only `si_restore` holds as a member's restore does (D36); §8.4's accept rule for a manifest (as the drill applies it); §8.5 steps 1–6 and its last paragraph (as a pure gate and a database-and-prefix materializer); §8.6's object-store restore bullet; §13.1's promotion budget for drills; §14's lockdown rules for every new ClickHouse user; §15's housegate `pkg/replay` helpers, arbiter-core install-gate share and production bucket and backup jobs; §17's data-plane cases for the gate and the restore source — as clarified by Plan S3-A's K1–K10, Plan S3-B's K11–K22, K23–K28 below and the cross-plan decisions D25–D40 where they touch this plan (D25, D26, D32, D34, D35 and D36, each stated where it applies; contract §19 lists all sixteen). **Prerequisites:** Plan S3-A (`2026-10-14-multi-source-si-s3a-p0-guards.md`, Tasks 1–11, contract §0–§6) and Plan S3-B (`2026-10-14-multi-source-si-s3b-p0-hosts-rollout.md`, Tasks 12–21, contract §7–§15): their Global Constraints, clarifications and Appendix A apply here unchanged, this plan's Appendix A continues them (§16–§19), and Tasks 22–28 consume their release ledger and records verbatim. ## Global Constraints

- **Signed worktrees and retained URWT paths (procedural reconciliation).** Codex-created local worktrees use runtime `codex`; this does not rename D34's fixed `origin/urwt/claude/ms-si-stage3-plans-cf`, historical execution evidence, or any existing stack branch. Every creation persists the complete returned JSON (`action` and exact absolute `path`, preserving symlink spelling), refuses malformed/empty/nonabsolute output and unexpected reuse, and subsequent tasks restore that producer's path rather than assuming the template. Code JSON state is `$HOME/.cache/s3-worktrees/s3c1-{housegate,arbiter-core,sentio-node,production}.json` for Tasks22/23/25/26, `$HOME/.cache/s3-worktrees/s3c2-{arbiter-core,sentio-node}.json` for Tasks29/35; Task28 additionally retains `s3c1-production-live.json`. A ledger R1 retains its actual raw JSON beside the existing `record-<plan>-<N>` state as `.urwt.json`, while preserving that state's path/ref interface. Reuse tasks consume their owning producer:23→24,26→27,29→30–34. Before a first real commit every worktree explicitly sets worktree `commit.gpgsign=true` with the poetry identity. Each commit must fail closed on commit/signing failure, produce a new HEAD, and verify `poetry <chen@sentio.xyz> G` plus `git verify-commit HEAD` before publishing. A cancellation preserves staged work and asks the user to unlock that repository's actual signing key; no unsigned fallback. Scratch-only synthetic fixture commits remain explicitly unsigned and unpublished. Existing canonical Claude trailers and paginated REST primary-author/head/coauthor semantics are unchanged.

- **Plans S3-A and S3-B apply.** Every Global Constraint and clarification of Plans S3-A and S3-B applies, and through them those of Plans S1-A, S1-B, S2-A and S2-B (strict decoder, request-only signatures, signed claims, tracks, quarantine, golden files, worktrees, commits, remote actions, the production rule, the runbook conventions, passwords).
- **Activation model (contract §16):** no Raft command, Raft tag, Raft-reachable field, snapshot version (it stays 20), header byte or feature string changes, and `arbiter.LocalNodeFeatures()` is unchanged; no voter, verifier or host image changes in this plan (only the backup and drill Jobs run `SN_DIGEST_P1`); every component stays rollback-able and P1 holds no consensus state.
- **No track pauses (spec §16 P1):** nothing restarts an SI ClickHouse, a host pod, a verifier or a voter: `si_backup` is a users.d reload, the CronJob and its ConfigMap stay outside the host checksum (the `checksum/config` annotation in `charts/sentio-node/templates/node.yaml`), and every live block that changes an installation or a release records the pods' UIDs and restart counts before and after and stops on a difference.
- **Ordering:** 22 → 23 → 24 → 25 → 26 → 27 → 28; per installation indexer-b → indexer-c → network (indexer-a); keys and logins before any user, users before any job, a full backup before the incremental one, both before the drill, the drill before the monitoring commit.
- **Irreversible steps:** the replica bucket (`prevent_destroy`, versioned) and every object written to it (no key in this plan deletes, K24); the on-chain `CREATE TABLE devuser1.s3_p1` and its two INSERTs (a registry incarnation and four promotions that stay in consensus state); each is preceded by `Confirm before running.` and marked irreversible in the runbook. HMAC keys and Secrets are revocable (runbook §15.3).
- **Object-store access is ClickHouse-side only (K23):** every `BACKUP`, `RESTORE` and index read or write is a ClickHouse statement naming the bucket with `S3(...)` / `s3(...)`; no repository gains a Go S3 or GCS client; no ClickHouse config file changes.
- **Keys and passwords (S3-B K16, extended):** HMAC keys are created only by the user's terminal with `scripts/storage-integrity/make-si-backup-keys.sh`, ClickHouse logins only with `make-clickhouse-logins.sh`; plaintext lives only in Kubernetes Secrets; git and the CHIs carry only SHA-256 hashes; agents never print, echo, log or pass a key or password on argv; SQL that carries a key is built by Go from the environment or inside the pod from stdin (`si_s3_sql`, contract §19); keys never appear in chat.
- **Production rule (S3-B, unchanged):** one P1 PR carries Tasks 26–27, inert on merge (render-and-cmp of every `charts/sentio-node` release and `storage-integrity-si-v2` against `origin/main`; Terraform is applied only by the user after merge); the `si_backup` user per installation, `siBackup.enabled` per host and the monitoring list are single-service commits pushed to `main` after the PR merged; CHI manifests go through `kubectl apply --dry-run=server` then `kubectl apply`; the P1 outcome record is a docs-only PR; every live mutation needs explicit user confirmation in chat, for that step only.
- **Runbook conventions (S3-B, unchanged):** bash blocks run in one dedicated session (`set -eo pipefail`) from a production checkout at `origin/main`, by a live agent from block files after sourcing the helpers (D24); `Confirm before running.` before every mutating block; every cross-block value under `$si_backup` (`$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p1`, mode 700, created fresh); read-only checks in their own re-runnable blocks that `tee` into `$si_backup`; writes never re-run; one stage per window; values disjoint from every earlier runbook (D19); all helpers in the first bash block of §0 (D20); commands handed to the user in fish.
- **Security:** the commented YAML in production `k8s-sea/clickhouse/clickhouse-extra.yaml` and `k8s-sea/clickhouse/clickhouse.yaml` (a GCP service-account key and a ClickHouse password; the user rotates them) is never read, copied or quoted; the `sentio-clickhouse-backup` service account and the `sentio-clickhouse` bucket are never reused.
- **Cross-plan boundary:** Plan S3-C2 consumes contract §16–§18 verbatim; `member/gate` is the install gate it reuses unchanged; this plan defines no `dataplane.Client.GetSafeWatermark` or `GetManifest` (Plan S3-C2 Task 29 owns them) and no member id, si-member process or `si_member` user.
- **Never edit** any golden or vector file listed by Plans S2-A and S3-A, `pre_tracks_golden.json`, the `l3_track_golden_test.go` constants or `conformance/stage3_reads_test.go` (decision D25 lets only Plans S3-D and S3-E1 change that file's count literals; this plan does not touch it); this plan adds no frozen fixture.
- **Repository commands, worktrees, commits, releases, the ledger:** contract §19 and Plan S3-A's contract §6; Plan S3-B's record procedure (D23) through `s3-ledger.py`; remote and live actions require explicit user confirmation in chat; commands handed to the user are fish.
- **Ledger copy (decision D34):** the plans branch `urwt/claude/ms-si-stage3-plans-cf` is aligned with `main`, which holds Plans S3-A and S3-B since housegate#237; this plan's ledger copy is `origin/urwt/claude/ms-si-stage3-plans-cf` until the stage-3 plans PR merges, then `origin/main`, and Plans S3-A's and S3-B's is `origin/main`. A recording task whose `s3-ledger.py ref` finds no `s3c1` on origin (the plans branch not pushed yet) stops and asks; nothing is ever recorded into, or read from, a local checkout.
- **Hunks are anchored on the base revisions.** Tasks were drafted in parallel; S3-A and S3-B are now merged: when a hunk overlaps an earlier task's edit, a Plan S3-A or S3-B change, or an earlier stage-3 plan's change (`snode/*.go` after S3-A Task 5, `clickhouse-mechanics.sh` after S3-A Task 6, `test_render.py`, `charts/sentio-node` and the devnet2 overlays after S3-B Tasks 13, 16 and 19), apply the later intent on top of the earlier change. The contract and the named tests are binding; line anchors are guidance.
- **References.** `contract §N` points to Appendix A of Plan S3-A for §0–§6, of Plan S3-B for §7–§15 and of this plan for §16–§19; a task's "Facts" point to Appendix B below; Appendix C records this plan's ledger values and run records as they are made.

## Plan clarifications (binding)

The spec and Plans S3-A and S3-B leave these P1 details open; each is resolved here and binding for Plan S3-C1 and for every later plan that consumes its names.

- **K23 — The backup destination is `S3()` per statement with keys from the job's environment (spec §16 P1 "tracks paused: none", §8.6).** Gap: the spec names an object-store backup but not how ClickHouse reaches the bucket; a config-defined backup disk or named collection would keep keys out of SQL but is a server config change, and operator 0.27.2 restarts a ClickHouse on any config change (S3-B K22). Resolution: every `BACKUP`, `RESTORE` and index read or write names the bucket inline — `S3('<url>', '<access key id>', '<secret>')` for BACKUP and RESTORE, `s3(...)` for the index object — rendered only by arbiter-core `objstore` from `objstore.Credentials`, which sentio-node reads only from `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` (Secret env), or by the runbook's `si_s3_sql` inside the pod from stdin; the ClickHouse login is a new installation-wide user `si_backup` holding exactly `SI_BACKUP_GRANTS` and, on the P1 staging installation only, `si_restore` holding `SI_RESTORE_GRANTS` (contract §18), both measured by M13 on `26.3.37.3` and by the grant probe on staging. Why: nothing restarts; the key travels in query text inside the namespace, so M14 measures its masking in `system.query_log`, `system.backups`, `system.processes` and the server log before any real key exists, and the plaintext native protocol stays a recorded residual until P4's policies.
- **K24 — "Not delete" is measured, and its only possible exception is each backup's own lock file (spec §16 P1).** Gap: ClickHouse's BACKUP writes `<backup>/.lock` and removes it when it finishes, a failed upload may leave parts, and GCS needs `storage.objects.delete` for any removal or overwrite. Resolution: Task 24's M13 (`TestMechanics_S3BackupWithAKeyThatCannotDelete`) backs up to MinIO with a key that may not delete (`mech-nodelete`) and with one that may delete only `*/.lock` (`mech-lockdelete`); the ledger value `P1_BACKUP_DELETE` is `none` when the first completes and `lock` when only the second does; with `none` no backup key holds any delete; with `lock` the plan stops before Task 26 (Task 25 does not depend on it) until the user amends spec §16 P1 to "not delete, except the backup's own `.lock`", and Task 26 then adds the `siDevnet2SiV2BackupLockRemover` binding conditioned on the owner's prefix and the `/.lock` suffix; if neither key completes, the plan stops and the user decides (the scoping fallback, delete on the own prefix with versioning and retention, is never taken without that decision). Backup names are never reused (an overwrite needs delete): `objstore` refuses an existing name and ClickHouse refuses an existing `.backup`. Multipart uploads may be created, listed and aborted (`storage.multipartUploads.*` deletes no object), and a bucket lifecycle rule aborts incomplete uploads after 7 days. Task 28 §5 proves the same on GCS with the deployed image: an overwrite of a backup object is refused and the lock removal behaves as recorded. Why: a prefix-wide delete would let a leaked backup key erase its owner's backups, which the spec's "not delete" exists to prevent; the lock-only exception keeps every data and metadata object immutable.
- **K25 — List confinement is one managed folder per writer prefix, proved live (spec §16 P1 "list … on their own prefix"; user decision, the conservative default).** The scoping reports disagree on whether a list can be prefix-scoped. Gap: GCS checks `storage.objects.list` on the bucket, and an IAM Condition of a bucket binding may use only the resource name, the resource type and the date and time: Cloud Storage's API attributes, the list prefix among them, are supported only in Credential Access Boundaries (IAM attribute reference, "Cloud Storage API attributes"), so a conditional bucket binding can confine a create or a read to a prefix but never a list (it refuses every list, the writer's own included, which stops `Backuper.Run` in `ReadIndexes`). Resolution: each writer prefix (`owner-0/`, `owner-1/`, `owner-<INDEXER_C_ID>/`, `mechanics/`) is a managed folder of the bucket of the same name (`google_storage_managed_folder`; the bucket has uniform bucket-level access, which managed folders require), and each backup service account holds the writer role `siDevnet2SiV2BackupWriter` on its own managed folder only (`google_storage_managed_folder_iam_member`, no condition) and nothing on the bucket but, with `lock`, K24's `/.lock` remover. A role granted on a managed folder covers every object whose name starts with the folder's name and a list whose prefix lies in the folder (Cloud Storage "List objects": a principal with a role on one managed folder lists it with `prefix=<folder>/`), so `ReadIndexes` (`ListObjectsV2` with the prefix `owner-<id>/`) and the name check (the prefix `owner-<id>/<name>/`) work, while a list of another prefix or of the whole bucket and a read outside the folder are refused. The bucket, the prefixes, the roles, the service accounts and the Secrets that Plans S3-C2, S3-C3 and S3-D consume keep their names. The documentation shows the managed-folder list with the JSON API; Task 28 §5 proves it on GCS with HMAC keys through the XML API, which ClickHouse uses: the mechanics key lists `mechanics/<stamp>-full/` (a prefix inside its folder) and is refused a list and a read of `owner-0/`; each owner's key lists and reads its own prefix and is refused a list and a read of another owner's prefix and a write to `mechanics/`. A row that differs stops P1 before any owner's data reaches the bucket (contract §19: §5 passes only when every row does); no residual is accepted, because §2's bucket verdict proves that no writer holds a list right on the bucket, so a granted cross-prefix list would mean the layout does not confine, and the user then decides another one (one bucket per owner, which renames the bucket the later plans read). Restore keys read and list the whole bucket (`roles/storage.objectViewer` on the bucket), which is what "read-only" asks. Why: a managed folder is the GCS IAM mechanism that scopes a list to a prefix, and it keeps every bucket and object name.
- **K26 — Granularity, naming and cadence.** Prefix `owner-<indexer_id>/` (the contract-assigned id, which no signer change alters); one backup service account per owner (`si-devnet2-si-v2-backup-0`, `-1`, `-<INDEXER_C_ID>`), one restore service account per member host for Plan S3-C2 (`si-devnet2-si-v2-restore-a`, `-b`, `-c`), one restore service account for drills (`-restore-drill`) and one writer confined to `mechanics/` (`-backup-mech`); each a separately revocable HMAC key. A backup is `BACKUP DATABASE hg_safe` named `<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ>-<full|incr>` with its index object `<name>.index.json` beside it under the owner's prefix; a chain is one full backup and at most `max_chain_links − 1` incremental ones on it (default 7: a weekly full); one CronJob per owner, daily at `17 3 * * *`, `47 3 * * *` and `17 4 * * *` UTC for indexer-a, -b and -c. Why: a database backup needs no per-table bookkeeping and restores any single table; lexicographic names order the chain; per-key revocation never touches another owner.
- **K27 — A drill gates against the manifest its backup names, on a staging installation (spec §16 P1 exit, §8.4, §8.5).** Resolution: the index object names S, the latest published manifest when the backup started, with its `track_frontiers[O]`; `restore-drill` fetches S through `objstore.NewArbiterManifests` (the existing `GetSafeWatermark` and `GetManifest` RPCs; S is accepted only when its id equals the requested id and its recomputed `ManifestRoot`, `Validate` passes and `payloadexec.VerifyLedger` holds — the §8.4 rule) and, for every partition of every backed-up table S lists, restores it into `hg_rstage` of the P1 staging installation `storage-integrity-si-v2-p1-staging` and runs `objstore.RestoreAndGate` with an empty local copy: Need = M(S), kept parts satisfy it exactly once, unneeded parts (a backup ahead of publication) are dropped inside the scratch, and closure Σ(kept) = R must hold. Each table's schema is read from the owner host's `sentio_getStorageIntegrityTableStatus` and must hash (`payloadexec.TableSchemaHash`) to S's `schema_hash`. A verdict passes only with at least one verified table and every backed-up table that S lists verified; the runbook compares the verified set with the owner's Active tables in the registry. `member/gate` is the gate Plan S3-C2 reuses unchanged. Why it is sound: after S is published the owner's `hg_safe` only grows (promotions append, `REPLACE PARTITION` keeps every part's bytes, `hash_of_all_files` and rows, merges are pinned off, and the owner audit drops only unacknowledged twins), so M(S) is a sub-multiset of every later backup; the schema source is untrusted but checked against the manifest's committed hash; the manifest reader stays inside `objstore`, so Plan S3-C2 Task 29 keeps `Client.GetSafeWatermark` / `GetManifest`.
- **K28 — The promotion budget is quadratic (spec §13.1, S3-B defect D1).** Every stage-3 runbook from P1 on computes its budget with the quadratic estimate of Plan S3-B's P0 runbook §13.4 (as fixed in housegate#237). P1 writes two statements (`devuser1.s3_p1`, rows 5101–5104 over two partitions), at most four promotions; backups and drills make none; runbook §1.3 runs that §13.4 procedure (the leader's newest finished snapshot and the live promotion sequence) and refuses to start §7 unless the budget is at least 16 promotions. Why: the earlier linear estimate overstated the budget about fourfold, and P2's devnet2 soak (K38) runs within half of whatever budget P1 leaves.

## Review Focus

1. **A backup key that could delete, overwrite or read beyond its owner.** ClickHouse's BACKUP writes and removes `<backup>/.lock`, a retried name would overwrite, and a list is a bucket-level permission that no IAM Condition of a bucket binding can scope to a prefix (K25). Expected: the writer role holds no `storage.objects.delete` and is granted only on the writer's own managed folder (`owner-<id>/` or `mechanics/`), never on the bucket; the only possible exception is the lock-remover binding, present exactly when `P1_BACKUP_DELETE` is `lock` and conditioned on the owner's prefix and the `/.lock` suffix; no backup name is reused (objstore refuses an existing index or backup, ClickHouse an existing `.backup`); on GCS an overwrite of a backup object is refused, the mechanics key lists inside `mechanics/` and is refused a list of `owner-0/`, and each owner key lists its own prefix and is refused a list and read of another owner's prefix (any other outcome stops P1, K25); restore keys only read. Tests: Task 24 `TestMechanics_S3BackupWithAKeyThatCannotDelete`, `TestS3_BackuperNeverReusesABackupName`, `TestNextBackupStartsAFullBackupAfterMaxChainLinks`; Task 26 `test_replica_bucket_terraform_follows_the_p1_contract`; checks: runbook §5 rows of `mechanics-gcs.tsv`, including forced multipart upload/readback through `mechanics/`.
2. **A backup ahead of its manifest, or a promotion during the backup.** hg_safe holds promotions the latest published manifest does not list yet, and a `REPLACE PARTITION` may rename parts between S and BACKUP. Expected: the index names the manifest that was latest when the backup started; the drill gates against exactly that manifest, keeps each needed row hash once, drops every unneeded part inside the scratch (never calls it Foreign), and passes only when closure Σ(kept) = R holds for every partition; a backup that lacks a needed part fails `need_unsatisfied`, never silently. Tests: Task 23 `TestPlanPartitionNeedIsManifestMinusLocal`, `TestClassifyRestoreKeepsOnlyNeededPartsAndDropsTheRest`, `TestClosureIsArithmetic`; Task 24 `TestS3_RestoreAndGateKeepsOnlyTheManifestsPartsFromABackupAheadOfPublication`, `TestS3_RestoreAndGateReportsANeedTheBackupCannotMeet`, `TestS3_DrillVerifiesABackupAgainstTheManifestItsIndexNames`, `TestMechanics_S3IncrementalBackupRestoreKeepsHashOfAllFiles`.
3. **A key or a password that leaks.** The HMAC secret travels in query text (K23) and the jobs hold three secrets. Expected: the secret argument shows as `[HIDDEN]` in `system.query_log`, `system.backups`, `system.processes` and the server log on 26.3.37.3 and on the deployed image; `Credentials` never prints the secret; no YAML key, ConfigMap, argv or log carries a key or password; the CronJob takes exactly three Secret env vars; the runbook builds key-bearing SQL inside the pod from stdin. Tests: Task 24 `TestMechanics_S3SecretsAreMaskedInLogsAndSystemTables` (and the runner's server-log grep), `TestCredentialsRedactTheSecret`; Task 25 `TestDecodeConfigYAMLRefusesStorageIntegrityBackupKeys`, `TestStorageIntegrityS3CredentialsComeOnlyFromTheEnvironment`; Task 26 `test_backup_job_takes_keys_and_password_only_from_secrets`, `test_backup_job_config_carries_no_secret`, `test_si_clickhouse_users_carry_only_literal_hashes`.
4. **A restart sneaks into P1.** P1 must pause no track (spec §16 P1). Expected: `siBackup` changes no host StatefulSet byte (it is outside the checksum at the `checksum/config` annotation in `templates/node.yaml`); `si_backup` arrives as a users.d reload; no ClickHouse config file changes; every installation and release step records pod UIDs and restart counts before and after and stops on a difference; the backup's load runs on the owner's ClickHouse as a separate login, never inside the host pod. Tests: Task 26 `test_backup_job_never_changes_the_host_pod`, `test_backup_job_renders_only_a_cronjob_and_its_config`, `test_si_backup_user_follows_the_rollout`, `test_default_renders_no_backup_job`; checks: `render-inertness.sh` on the P1 PR, runbook §6 and §8 `host-pods-<x>-{before,after}.txt`.
5. **A drill that passes against the wrong reference, or vacuously.** The drill must not trust the host for schemas, the arbiter for an unverified manifest, or an owner with nothing to restore. Expected: S is accepted only when its id equals the requested id and its recomputed root, `Validate` passes and `VerifyLedger` holds; each table's schema from the owner's status RPC must hash to S's `schema_hash`; the verdict passes only with at least one verified table and every backed-up table that S lists verified; `restore-drill` exits non-zero otherwise; indexer-b gets the drill table `devuser1.s3_p1` before its drill, and the runbook compares each verified set with the owner's Active registry tables. Tests: Task 24 `TestCheckManifestRefusesAWrongIDRootOrLedger`, `TestS3_DrillFailsWhenNoTableOfTheOwnerIsVerified`, `TestS3_DrillRefusesASchemaWhoseHashIsNotTheManifests`, `TestDrillVerdictPassRule`; Task 25 `TestStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillExitsNonZeroUnlessTheVerdictPasses`, `TestStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillTakesSchemasFromTheOwnersStatusRPC`, `TestStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillRefusesATableWithoutASchema`; checks: runbook §10.
6. **A restore user with more than a member's restore rights.** The drill's `si_restore` stands in for a member's restore on staging, and `ALL ON hg_rstage.*` would add dictionary, `SYSTEM` and definer rights the spec withholds (§8.2 as amended, D36). Expected: `SI_RESTORE_GRANTS` names spec §8.2's explicit `hg_rstage` list, never `ALL`; `si_restore` is refused a `CREATE DICTIONARY` and a `SYSTEM STOP MERGES` in `hg_rstage` and a view that names another definer, and exists only on the P1 staging installation; every right it holds is exercised by a positive probe row. Tests: Task 24 `TestMechanics_S3BackupWithAKeyThatCannotDelete` (M13's `si_restore` refusals); Task 26 `test_si_restore_exists_only_on_the_p1_staging_installation`, `test_grant_probe_covers_every_protocol_grant`; checks: runbook §4 `staging-grant-probe.tsv`.

7. **A failed commit accepted as an older signed HEAD, or a different checkout restored as the worktree.** Expected: Tasks22/23/25/26 create and retain their own actual Codex URWT JSON; Tasks24/27 consume the exact producer state, and Task28 retains its separate live JSON and session path. Creation checks the expected branch/base/common repository and refuses unexpected reuse; later restoration preserves the absolute JSON path spelling. Every real commit explicitly enables worktree signing, stops on stage/commit/read failure, creates a new HEAD and requires `poetry <chen@sentio.xyz> G` plus `git verify-commit HEAD` before publication. Ledger restoration checks the raw JSON against its retained path/ref state and the expected branch/common repository. Checks: the explicit gates in Tasks22–28 and the scoped workflow verification recorded in Appendix B; these do not authorize a live action or replace its confirmation.

Task 22's first record, and every later one, needs this plan's ledger copy on origin: the plans branch `urwt/claude/ms-si-stage3-plans-cf` pushed (aligned with `main` after housegate#237) until the stage-3 plans PR merges, then `main` (D34); without it R1's `ref` stops and the task asks. ## Follow-ups (not in this plan)

- Plan S3-C2 Task 29's `dataplane.Client.GetSafeWatermark` and `GetManifest` may replace the internals of `objstore.NewArbiterManifests`; the accept rule (`CheckManifest`) stays one function.
- The bucket grows forever: no key of this plan deletes, so expiring old chains needs an administrator action and a retention decision (versions, chain age) before storage cost matters.
- The HMAC secret crosses the namespace in the plaintext native protocol (K23); P4's policies narrow who can observe it (the CronJob pods to their owner's ClickHouse on 9000, the ClickHouse pods to `storage.googleapis.com:443`), and native-protocol TLS is a separate change. Plan S3-D's ingress policies must admit the backup CronJobs and the drill Jobs.
- `si_backup` is installation-wide, so it is valid on the network CHI's verifier hosts too (their `hg_safe` is empty): a K18-style residual, recorded in runbook §15.5.
- If GCS ever refuses a writer's list of its own managed folder through the XML API, or grants a list outside it (K25, runbook §5), P1 stops: the remaining layout, one bucket per owner, renames the bucket that Plans S3-C2, S3-C3 and S3-D read and is the user's decision.
- With `P1_BACKUP_DELETE` = `lock`, spec §16 P1 is amended by the user to admit the backup's own `.lock` removal.
- The drill reads table schemas from the owner host's status RPC; Plan S3-C2's members need their own schema source for the gate (registry plus the genesis schemas).
- HMAC key rotation is documented (runbook §15.3) but not drilled.
- ClickHouse grants `CREATE VIEW` and `DROP VIEW` implicitly with `CREATE TABLE` and `DROP TABLE` (Plan S3-B's measured `role_atoms`), so `si_restore` can create a plain view in `hg_rstage` on the P1 staging installation; spec §8.2's "no view right" (D36) is enforced here for definer views only, and whether `table_engines_require_grant` closes plain views for `si_member` from P2 on is for Plan S3-C2's confinement suite to measure.
- Plan S3-B's single `monitoring.runbookURL` is joined here by `monitoring.backups.runbookURL`; the later groups follow this per-group pattern (Plan S3-C3 `monitoring.members.runbookURL`, Plan S3-C4 `monitoring.replicaReads.runbookURL`, Plan S3-E4 `monitoring.stage3Consensus.runbookURL`, Plan S3-F `monitoring.stage3.p6RunbookURL`).
- The commented GCP service-account key and ClickHouse password in `k8s-sea/clickhouse/clickhouse-extra.yaml` and `k8s-sea/clickhouse/clickhouse.yaml` must be rotated and purged from history by the user (never read by this plan).
- A CI job for the mechanics suite on the deployed image still needs a read-only registry secret (S3-A K9).
- Members, their users, the P2 restart window and everything else of stage 3 beyond P1: Plans S3-C2 to S3-F.

Notes:
- **No behaviour change for existing callers.** `ScanParts` keeps its query byte for byte (``SELECT _part, _hg_row_id, … FROM `db`.`t` WHERE _part IN (?, …)``, pinned by `TestScanAllPartsScansEveryActivePartWithScanPartsRefusals`), its refusals and its order of checks (the empty-names refusal first). `NewMaterializer`'s four statements (``CREATE TABLE `_hg_replay_scratch_<n>` (…)``, `INSERT INTO …`, `SELECT _hg_row_id, … FROM …`, `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS …`) and its error text `create scratch table _hg_replay_scratch_<n>: …` are unchanged, pinned without ClickHouse by `TestMaterializerScratchStatementsNameTheirTable` and against ClickHouse by `TestChexecMaterializer_DefaultScratchIsUnchanged`. `verifyLedger`'s three callers are untouched. No `json` tag of a type `replay.proto` mirrors changes (`pkg/replay/AGENTS.md`), no reserved database, no plugin; housegate keeps arbiter-proto `v0.11.0`, and `go.mod` does not change.
- **`ScanAllParts` sees parts through their rows.** It reads the `_part` virtual column, so a part without rows cannot appear. Measured on `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3` (26.3.51.7) while drafting: `ALTER TABLE … DROP PART` of a plain MergeTree part writes an empty covering part that is not active, and `TRUNCATE` leaves no active part, so on a scratch `ScanAllParts` and `system.parts WHERE active` agree on every part that holds rows. MergeTree `SELECT` reads only active parts, which `TestChexecScanAllParts_MatchesScanPartsOverEveryActivePart` checks across a merge.
- **The materializer database is not created here.** `NewMaterializerIn` interpolates both names into SQL, so it validates them (`[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*` and `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,96}`, which admit every member id of Plan S3-C2 K29 and `shadow.ReplayPrefix`), and a missing database fails the CREATE with ClickHouse code 81, never falling back to the default database; the caller creates `hg_rstage` (`CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS hg_rstage`, without `ENGINE`, spec §8.2).
- **Integration tests without the FFI library.** The original four new `pkg/integration` tests use `openDirectCH` and call no rewriter. The fifth, `TestChexecMaterializerInWithStoragePolicyUsesMemberDisk`, starts an additional pinned `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3.37.3` with two logical disk paths and inspects the actual replay parts. None needs `POLYGLOT_SQL_FFI_PATH`; the shared package `TestMain` still starts its usual ClickHouse container. The PR's `Integration (ClickHouse)` job runs the whole target with the FFI library, on `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:25.8` (`pkg/integration/testenv/clickhouse.go:22`). testcontainers reaches Docker through `DOCKER_HOST` or `/var/run/docker.sock`; where that socket is not the active Docker context's (on the user's Mac it points at Docker Desktop while OrbStack is the active context, and the run fails with `rootless Docker not found`), pass `--test_env=DOCKER_HOST=<the output of docker context inspect --format '{{.Endpoints.docker.Host}}'>` to `bazel test` (or set `DOCKER_HOST` for `go test`). testcontainers also starts its reaper `testcontainers/ryuk`, pulled when it is not local (a remote read under the same confirmation as the ClickHouse image); `--test_env=TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true` avoids it, and `TestMain` still terminates its container.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the ledger tool and read the ledger**

The ledger lives in Appendix C of the plan files on their ledger copies, never in a local checkout or a pending PR (contract §19, decision D23). Run `mkdir -p -m 700 "$HOME/.cache/s3-ledger"` and write `$HOME/.cache/s3-ledger/s3-ledger.py` with the Write tool: the ledger tool at the end of contract §19 (this plan's Appendix A), verbatim, ending with one newline after `    main(sys.argv[1:])`; an existing copy is overwritten. Remote read (housegate fetch), then local reads: needs explicit user confirmation in chat before running.

```bash
h=/Users/uranuswch/Dev/projects/sentio-network/housegate; L="$HOME/.cache/s3-ledger"
git -C "$h" fetch -q origin --tags
ref="$(python3 -I "$L/s3-ledger.py" ref "$h" s3c1)" || exit 1
echo "$ref"
python3 -I "$L/s3-ledger.py" show "$h" s3c1 | python3 -I -c '
import sys
lines = sys.stdin.read().split("\n")
marker = "The ledger tool `$HOME/.cache/s3-ledger/s3-ledger.py` (contract §19, decision D23 generalized), verbatim:"
hits = [i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if line == marker]
if len(hits) != 1:
    sys.exit(f"expected one contract §19 ledger-tool line, found {len(hits)}")
i = hits[0] + 1
while i < len(lines) and lines[i] == "":
    i += 1
if i >= len(lines) or lines[i] != "```python":
    sys.exit("contract §19: no python block after the ledger-tool line")
end = lines.index("```", i + 1)
sys.stdout.write("\n".join(lines[i + 1:end]) + "\n")
' > "$L/s3-ledger.py.plan" || exit 1
cmp "$L/s3-ledger.py" "$L/s3-ledger.py.plan" && echo "s3-ledger.py is contract §19 of $ref"
shasum -a 256 "$L/s3-ledger.py"
python3 -I "$L/s3-ledger.py" plans "$h"
python3 -I "$L/s3-ledger.py" get "$h" HG_TAG PROTO_TAG CORE_TAG ARBITER_TAG
python3 -I "$L/s3-ledger.py" empty "$h" HG_TAG_P1
```

Expected: the ledger copy of this plan, `origin/urwt/claude/ms-si-stage3-plans-cf` until the stage-3 plans PR merges and `origin/main` afterwards; `s3-ledger.py is contract §19 of <that ref>`; one `shasum` line; `plans` prints one line per plan file (never one for the s3cf status, scoping or names-index files), `s3a origin/main docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-14-multi-source-si-s3a-p0-guards.md HG_TAG,PROTO_TAG,CORE_TAG,ARBITER_TAG,ARBITER_DIGEST`, `s3b origin/main docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-14-multi-source-si-s3b-p0-hosts-rollout.md SN_COMMIT,SN_DIGEST,…`, `s3c1 <ref> docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-15-multi-source-si-s3c1-p1-backups.md HG_TAG_P1,CORE_TAG_P1,P1_BACKUP_DELETE,SN_COMMIT_P1,SN_DIGEST_P1,P1_PR,P1_MECHANICS,P1_END` and one line for each other stage-3 plan file on origin; then `HG_TAG=v…`, `PROTO_TAG=v…`, `CORE_TAG=v…`, `ARBITER_TAG=v…` (Plan S3-A's Appendix C on `origin/main`); and `s3-ledger: HG_TAG_P1 not recorded yet in <ref>:docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-15-multi-source-si-s3c1-p1-backups.md`. If `ref` stops with `no plan 's3c1'`, the plans branch is not on origin: stop and ask the user to push it (decision D34); nothing is read from or recorded into a local checkout. ```go
package payloadexec

import (
	"encoding/hex"
	"errors"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/lthash"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"
)

// ledgerManifest replays two blocks into a table partitioned by shard, so one
// partition holds two parts and the other one (spec 2026-10-14 §8.5 step 1: M
// is the multiset of part row hashes S lists for (T, p), R its root).
func ledgerManifest(t *testing.T) replay.SafeSnapshotManifest {
	t.Helper()
	e := New(testNetwork, TableSchema{
		TableID:     testTable,
		PartitionBy: "shard",
		Columns: []lthash.Column{
			{Name: "shard", Type: "String"},
			{Name: "name", Type: "String"},
			{Name: "balance", Type: "UInt64"},
		},
	})
	snap := genesis(t, e)
	snap, _ = applyInsert(t, e, snap, "stmt-1", "p1", "shard,name,balance\na,alice,10\nb,bob,20\n")
	snap, _ = applyInsert(t, e, snap, "stmt-2", "p2", "shard,name,balance\na,carol,30\n")
	if len(snap.Tables) != 1 || len(snap.Tables[0].PartitionRoots) != 2 || len(snap.Tables[0].ActiveParts) != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("ledger manifest has %d tables, want one table with 2 partition roots and 3 parts: %+v", len(snap.Tables), snap.Tables)
	}
	return snap
}

// copyLedgerManifest copies the table slices a test mutates, so a mutation
// never reaches the replayed manifest.
func copyLedgerManifest(m replay.SafeSnapshotManifest) replay.SafeSnapshotManifest {
	m.Tables = slices.Clone(m.Tables)
	for i := range m.Tables {
		m.Tables[i].PartitionRoots = slices.Clone(m.Tables[i].PartitionRoots)
		m.Tables[i].ActiveParts = slices.Clone(m.Tables[i].ActiveParts)
	}
	return m
}

// TestVerifyLedgerIsTheExecutorsLedgerCheck pins the exported ledger check of
// spec 2026-10-14 §8.4 ("every partition root equals the sum of its listed
// part row hashes"): it accepts what the executor replays and refuses, with
// the executor's own texts, a root that is not its parts' sum, an orphan part
// and a part hash that is not hex; the unexported check the executor applies
// to every previous snapshot answers exactly the same.
func TestVerifyLedgerIsTheExecutorsLedgerCheck(t *testing.T) {
	good := ledgerManifest(t)
	if err := VerifyLedger(good); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("VerifyLedger(replayed manifest) = %v", err)
	}
	if err := verifyLedger(good); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("verifyLedger(replayed manifest) = %v", err)
	}
	table := good.Tables[0]
	single := ""
	counts := map[string]int{}
	for _, p := range table.ActiveParts {
		counts[p.PartitionID]++
	}
	for id, n := range counts {
		if n == 1 {
			single = id
		}
	}
	if single == "" {
		t.Fatalf("no single-part partition in %+v", table.ActiveParts)
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		mutate func(*replay.TableManifest)
		want   string
	}{
		{
			name:   "a root that is not its parts' sum",
			mutate: func(tm *replay.TableManifest) { tm.PartitionRoots[0].Root = lthashHex(lthash.New()) },
			want:   "table " + testTable + " partition " + table.PartitionRoots[0].PartitionID + ": parts sum != root",
		},
		{
			name: "a part whose partition declares no root",
			mutate: func(tm *replay.TableManifest) {
				tm.PartitionRoots = slices.DeleteFunc(tm.PartitionRoots, func(pc replay.PartitionCommitment) bool { return pc.PartitionID == single })
			},
			want: "table " + testTable + " partition " + single + ": active parts present with no partition root",
		},
		{
			name:   "a part hash that is not hex",
			mutate: func(tm *replay.TableManifest) { tm.ActiveParts[0].PartRowLtHash = "0xzz" },
			want:   "table " + testTable + " part " + table.ActiveParts[0].PartName + ": decode lthash hex: encoding/hex: invalid byte: U+007A 'z'",
		},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			m := copyLedgerManifest(good)
			tc.mutate(&m.Tables[0])
			err := VerifyLedger(m)
			if err == nil || err.Error() != tc.want {
				t.Fatalf("VerifyLedger = %v, want %q", err, tc.want)
			}
			if inner := verifyLedger(m); inner == nil || inner.Error() != err.Error() {
				t.Fatalf("verifyLedger = %v, want the exported check's %q", inner, err)
			}
		})
	}
	if err := VerifyLedger(good); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a refused copy changed the replayed manifest: %v", err)
	}
}

// TestSumPartRowLtHashesEqualsThePartitionRoot is spec 2026-10-14 §8.5 step 6's
// arithmetic: the sum of the part row hashes a manifest lists for a partition
// is its root, in any order, and a repeated hash counts once per occurrence.
func TestSumPartRowLtHashesEqualsThePartitionRoot(t *testing.T) {
	table := ledgerManifest(t).Tables[0]
	byPartition := map[string][]string{}
	for _, p := range table.ActiveParts {
		byPartition[p.PartitionID] = append(byPartition[p.PartitionID], p.PartRowLtHash)
	}
	sawTwoParts := false
	for _, pc := range table.PartitionRoots {
		hashes := byPartition[pc.PartitionID]
		got, err := SumPartRowLtHashes(hashes)
		if err != nil || got != pc.Root {
			t.Fatalf("SumPartRowLtHashes(partition %s, %d parts) = %q, %v; want the root %q", pc.PartitionID, len(hashes), got, err, pc.Root)
		}
		reversed := slices.Clone(hashes)
		slices.Reverse(reversed)
		if again, err := SumPartRowLtHashes(reversed); err != nil || again != pc.Root {
			t.Fatalf("SumPartRowLtHashes(reversed partition %s) = %q, %v; the order must not matter", pc.PartitionID, again, err)
		}
		sawTwoParts = sawTwoParts || len(hashes) == 2
	}
	if !sawTwoParts {
		t.Fatalf("want a partition with two parts, got %v", byPartition)
	}

	h := table.ActiveParts[0].PartRowLtHash
	once, err := SumPartRowLtHashes([]string{h})
	if err != nil || once != h {
		t.Fatalf("SumPartRowLtHashes([h]) = %q, %v; want h itself", once, err)
	}
	if !strings.HasPrefix(once, "0x") || len(once) != 2+2*lthash.Size || strings.ToLower(once) != once {
		t.Fatalf("SumPartRowLtHashes form = %.20q… (len %d), want 0x and %d lowercase hex digits", once, len(once), 2*lthash.Size)
	}
	twice, err := SumPartRowLtHashes([]string{h, h})
	if err != nil || twice == once {
		t.Fatalf("SumPartRowLtHashes([h, h]) = %.20q…, %v; a repeated part must count twice", twice, err)
	}
	upper, err := SumPartRowLtHashes([]string{"0x" + strings.ToUpper(h[2:])})
	if err != nil || upper != once {
		t.Fatalf("SumPartRowLtHashes(uppercase h) = %.20q…, %v; want the lowercase form of h", upper, err)
	}
}

// TestSumPartRowLtHashesOfNothingIsTheEmptyRoot pins the sum of no parts: the
// zero accumulator, which is the root VerifyLedger accepts for a declared
// partition that has no part.
func TestSumPartRowLtHashesOfNothingIsTheEmptyRoot(t *testing.T) {
	zero := lthashHex(lthash.New())
	for _, in := range [][]string{nil, {}} {
		got, err := SumPartRowLtHashes(in)
		if err != nil || got != zero {
			t.Fatalf("SumPartRowLtHashes(%#v) = %.20q…, %v; want the zero accumulator", in, got, err)
		}
	}
	m := replay.SafeSnapshotManifest{Tables: []replay.TableManifest{{
		TableID:        testTable,
		PartitionRoots: []replay.PartitionCommitment{{TableID: testTable, PartitionID: "all", Root: zero}},
	}}}
	if err := VerifyLedger(m); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("VerifyLedger(a declared partition without parts, root = the empty sum) = %v", err)
	}
}

// TestSumPartRowLtHashesRefusesBadHex: a hash that is not an accumulator names
// its position and wraps the executor's decode error, so a caller can still
// match the hex error underneath; nothing is summed.
func TestSumPartRowLtHashesRefusesBadHex(t *testing.T) {
	good := ledgerManifest(t).Tables[0].ActiveParts[0].PartRowLtHash
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		in    []string
		want  string
		wraps error
	}{
		{[]string{good, "0xzz"}, "part row lthash 1: decode lthash hex: encoding/hex: invalid byte: U+007A 'z'", hex.InvalidByteError('z')},
		{[]string{"0xabc"}, "part row lthash 0: decode lthash hex: encoding/hex: odd length hex string", hex.ErrLength},
		{[]string{good, good, "0x00"}, "part row lthash 2: lthash: accumulator must be exactly 2048 bytes", nil},
	} {
		got, err := SumPartRowLtHashes(tc.in)
		if err == nil || err.Error() != tc.want || got != "" {
			t.Errorf("SumPartRowLtHashes(%d hashes) = %q, %v; want \"\" and %q", len(tc.in), got, err, tc.want)
		}
		if tc.wraps != nil && !errors.Is(err, tc.wraps) {
			t.Errorf("SumPartRowLtHashes(%d hashes) = %v, which does not wrap %v", len(tc.in), err, tc.wraps)
		}
	}
}

Create `pkg/replay/owner_entry.go`:

```go
package replay

// OwnerEntry returns track_frontiers[O] of manifest m: the TrackFrontier whose
// IndexerID is indexerID (spec 2026-10-14 §8.4, §8.5 step 7: a member keys
// its installs and checkpoints on the owner's entry). It returns false when m
// carries no frontiers (a manifest published before the tracks activation) or
// does not list that indexer. It reads the list as it is and does not check
// its order; Validate does.
func OwnerEntry(m SafeSnapshotManifest, indexerID uint64) (TrackFrontier, bool) {
	for _, f := range m.TrackFrontiers {
		if f.IndexerID == indexerID {
			return f, true
		}
	}
	return TrackFrontier{}, false
}
```

Replace `pkg/replay/payloadexec/exports.go` with (the first four exports are unchanged; `VerifyLedger`'s body is `verifyLedger`'s, `executor.go:567-601`, moved with its error texts):

```go
package payloadexec

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/lthash"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"
)

// RowIDProfileID names the _hg_row_id derivation profile (§5.2). Envelope v2
// signs it as row_id_profile_id; verifiers reject any other value.
const RowIDProfileID = rowIDDomain

// PayloadFormatCSVWithNames is the legacy/test wire encoding decoded by
// DecodeCSV. Production storage-integrity payloads are Native
// (pkg/replay/nativepayload.PayloadFormat).
const PayloadFormatCSVWithNames = "csv-with-names-v1"

// RowElementHash exposes the executor's canonical per-row LtHash element. Data
// plane scanners call this instead of reimplementing row identity or row
// encoding.
func RowElementHash(sch TableSchema, rowID []byte, values []any) (*lthash.Hash, error) {
	return rowElementHash(sch, rowID, values)
}

// SchemaRoot exposes the deployment schema-root derivation used by replay
// manifests and Arbiter genesis checks.
func SchemaRoot(networkID string, schemas []TableSchema) string {
	return schemaRoot(networkID, schemas)
}

// TableSchemaHash exposes the per-table schema digest used in table manifests.
func TableSchemaHash(networkID string, t TableSchema) string {
	return tableSchemaHash(networkID, t)
}

// SchemaRootFromHashes derives the schema root from table ids and their
// TableSchemaHash values. It is byte-identical to SchemaRoot over the schemas
// those hashes were computed from, so a party that holds only committed hashes
// (the arbiter FSM, a manifest) derives the root a verifier derives from full
// schemas.
func SchemaRootFromHashes(schemaHashes map[string]string) string {
	return schemaRootFromHashes(schemaHashes)
}

// VerifyLedger is the executor's partition-ledger check (§5.4), exported for
// the stage-3 manifest reader and install gate (spec 2026-10-14 §8.4: a
// manifest is accepted only if every partition root equals the sum of its
// listed part row hashes). For every table, the LtHash sum of the
// PartRowLtHash of its active parts in a partition must equal that
// partition's declared root (a declared partition without parts has the zero
// accumulator as its root), and every partition with active parts must
// declare a root. The executor applies the same check to every previous
// snapshot it replays from.
func VerifyLedger(m replay.SafeSnapshotManifest) error {
	for _, t := range m.Tables {
		sums := map[string]*lthash.Hash{}
		for _, p := range t.ActiveParts {
			h, err := lthashFromHex(p.PartRowLtHash)
			if err != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("table %s part %s: %w", t.TableID, p.PartName, err)
			}
			if sums[p.PartitionID] == nil {
				sums[p.PartitionID] = lthash.New()
			}
			sums[p.PartitionID].AddHash(h)
		}
		declared := make(map[string]struct{}, len(t.PartitionRoots))
		for _, pc := range t.PartitionRoots {
			declared[pc.PartitionID] = struct{}{}
			got := sums[pc.PartitionID]
			if got == nil {
				got = lthash.New()
			}
			if lthashHex(got) != pc.Root {
				return fmt.Errorf("table %s partition %s: parts sum != root", t.TableID, pc.PartitionID)
			}
		}
		// The invariant is bijective: a partition with active parts must also
		// declare a commitment, else an orphan part contributes data summed into
		// no partition root (§5.4 / "Registration arithmetic").
		for partitionID := range sums {
			if _, ok := declared[partitionID]; !ok {
				return fmt.Errorf("table %s partition %s: active parts present with no partition root", t.TableID, partitionID)
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// SumPartRowLtHashes returns the LtHash sum of part row accumulators in the
// executor's form ("0x" + lowercase hex of the 2048-byte accumulator), the
// arithmetic of the install gate (spec 2026-10-14 §8.5 steps 1 and 6: Σ(M) =
// R, Σ(L) + Σ(kept) = R). Each element is a 0x-prefixed hex accumulator as a
// manifest's PartRowLtHash or chexec's PartScanResult.RowLtHash holds it.
// Repeats count, order does not, and the sum of no element is the zero
// accumulator, the root of a partition without parts. An element that is not
// an accumulator fails with its position.
func SumPartRowLtHashes(hashes []string) (string, error) {
	sum := lthash.New()
	for i, s := range hashes {
		h, err := lthashFromHex(s)
		if err != nil {
			return "", fmt.Errorf("part row lthash %d: %w", i, err)
		}
		sum.AddHash(h)
	}
	return lthashHex(sum), nil
}
```

In `pkg/replay/payloadexec/executor.go` replace `verifyLedger` and its doc (`:565-601`, from `// verifyLedger enforces §5.4: for every partition the sum of its part` through the function's closing brace) with:

```go
// verifyLedger enforces §5.4 on the previous snapshot of every replay: for
// every partition the sum of its part accumulators must equal the recorded
// partition root. It is VerifyLedger, which the stage-3 manifest reader and
// install gate share (spec 2026-10-14 §8.4).
func verifyLedger(m replay.SafeSnapshotManifest) error {
	return VerifyLedger(m)
}

// TestScanAllPartsScansEveryActivePartWithScanPartsRefusals pins, without
// ClickHouse, what ScanAllParts sends and refuses (spec 2026-10-14 §8.5 step
// 4): ScanParts's query without the _part filter, so every active part of the
// table is read; ScanParts's refusals, before any query; and an empty answer
// is an empty slice, not an error (the rename-race signal). ScanParts's own
// query is unchanged.
func TestScanAllPartsScansEveryActivePartWithScanPartsRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	schema := payloadexec.TableSchema{TableID: "db.t", PartitionBy: "p", Columns: []lthash.Column{{Name: "p", Type: "String"}, {Name: "v", Type: "UInt64"}}}

	conn := &recordingConn{}

	if err != nil || got == nil || len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("ScanAllParts(empty table) = %#v, %v; want an empty slice and no error", got, err)
	}
	if _, err := ScanParts(ctx, conn, "hg_rstage.s_1", schema, []string{"all_1_1_0", "all_2_2_0"}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("ScanParts of parts an empty table lacks must fail")
	}
	want := []string{
		"SELECT _part, _hg_row_id, `p`, `v` FROM `hg_rstage`.`s_1`",
		"SELECT _part, _hg_row_id, `p`, `v` FROM `hg_rstage`.`s_1` WHERE _part IN (?, ?)",
	}
	if !slices.Equal(conn.queries, want) {
		t.Fatalf("queries = %q, want %q", conn.queries, want)
	}

	for _, tc := range []struct {
		table  string
		schema payloadexec.TableSchema
		want   string
	}{
		{"s_1", schema, `chexec: qualifiedTable must be db.table, got "s_1"`},
		{"hg_rstage.s_1", payloadexec.TableSchema{TableID: "db.t", Columns: []lthash.Column{{Name: "v", Type: "Array(UInt64)"}}}, `chexec: unsupported column type "Array(UInt64)" for part scan (column "v")`},
	} {
		if got, err := ScanAllParts(ctx, panicConn{}, tc.table, tc.schema); err == nil || err.Error() != tc.want || got != nil {
			t.Errorf("ScanAllParts(%q) = %v, %v; want nil, %q", tc.table, got, err, tc.want)
		}
		if _, err := ScanParts(ctx, panicConn{}, tc.table, tc.schema, []string{"all_1_1_0"}); err == nil || err.Error() != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("ScanParts(%q) = %v, want the same refusal %q", tc.table, err, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

```go
// TestChexecScanAllParts_MatchesScanPartsOverEveryActivePart pins the full
// partition scan of spec 2026-10-14 §8.5 step 4 (a restore scratch is scanned
// without knowing its part names): ScanAllParts equals ScanParts over the
// names of every active part, sorted by part name, and after a merge it reads
// only the merged part, whose rows still sum to the same accumulator.
func TestChexecScanAllParts_MatchesScanPartsOverEveryActivePart(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	conn := openDirectCH(t)
	db := "hg_scan_all_test"
	table := uniqueTable(t)
	qualified := db + "." + table

	mustExec(t, conn, "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS "+db)
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		_ = conn.Exec(context.Background(), "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "+db)
	})
	mustExec(t, conn, fmt.Sprintf(`
		CREATE TABLE %s (
			_hg_row_id FixedString(32),
			p String,
			v UInt64
		) ENGINE = MergeTree
		PARTITION BY p
		ORDER BY tuple()`, qualified))
	mustExec(t, conn, "SYSTEM STOP MERGES "+qualified)

	sch := payloadexec.TableSchema{
		TableID:     "db.scan_all_t",
		PartitionBy: "p",
		Columns:     []lthash.Column{{Name: "p", Type: "String"}, {Name: "v", Type: "UInt64"}},
	}
	rid := func(ordinal uint64) []byte { return payloadexec.RowID("net-1", "db.scan_all_t", "acct/1/n", ordinal) }
	insertScanRows(t, conn, qualified, scanRow{rid: rid(0), p: "p0", v: 1}, scanRow{rid: rid(1), p: "p0", v: 2})
	insertScanRows(t, conn, qualified, scanRow{rid: rid(2), p: "p0", v: 3})
	insertScanRows(t, conn, qualified, scanRow{rid: rid(3), p: "p1", v: 4})

	scanAll := func(wantParts int) []chexec.PartScanResult {
		t.Helper()
		names := activePartNames(t, ctx, conn, db, table)
		if len(names) != wantParts {
			t.Fatalf("active parts = %v, want %d", names, wantParts)
		}
		all, err := chexec.ScanAllParts(ctx, conn, qualified, sch)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("ScanAllParts: %v", err)
		}
		named, err := chexec.ScanParts(ctx, conn, qualified, sch, names)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("ScanParts(%v): %v", names, err)
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(all, named) {
			t.Fatalf("ScanAllParts = %+v, ScanParts over every active part = %+v", all, named)
		}
		got := make([]string, len(all))
		var rows uint64
		for i, part := range all {
			got[i] = part.PartName
			rows += part.RowCount
		}
		if !slices.Equal(got, names) || !slices.IsSorted(got) || rows != 4 {
			t.Fatalf("ScanAllParts parts = %v (%d rows), want the active parts %v sorted by name with 4 rows", got, rows, names)
		}
		return all
	}
	sum := func(parts []chexec.PartScanResult) string {
		t.Helper()
		hashes := make([]string, len(parts))
		for i, part := range parts {
			hashes[i] = part.RowLtHash
		}
		total, err := payloadexec.SumPartRowLtHashes(hashes)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("SumPartRowLtHashes: %v", err)
		}
		return total
	}

	before := sum(scanAll(3))

	// A merge retires both parts of p0; only the merged part stays active.
	mustExec(t, conn, "SYSTEM START MERGES "+qualified)
	mustExec(t, conn, "OPTIMIZE TABLE "+qualified+" PARTITION 'p0' FINAL")
	mustExec(t, conn, "SYSTEM STOP MERGES "+qualified)
	if after := sum(scanAll(2)); after != before {
		t.Fatalf("the rows' accumulator changed across a merge: %.20s… != %.20s…", after, before)
	}
}

// TestChexecScanAllParts_EmptyTableIsEmpty: a table without rows, never
// written or emptied, scans to an empty slice and no error, which is how a
// caller sees a rename race (spec 2026-10-14 §8.5 step 4).
func TestChexecScanAllParts_EmptyTableIsEmpty(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	conn := openDirectCH(t)
	db := "hg_scan_all_test"
	table := uniqueTable(t)
	qualified := db + "." + table

	mustExec(t, conn, "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS "+db)
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		_ = conn.Exec(context.Background(), "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "+db)
	})
	mustExec(t, conn, "CREATE TABLE "+qualified+" (_hg_row_id FixedString(32), v UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple()")
	sch := payloadexec.TableSchema{TableID: "db.scan_all_empty", Columns: []lthash.Column{{Name: "v", Type: "UInt64"}}}

	got, err := chexec.ScanAllParts(ctx, conn, qualified, sch)
	if err != nil || len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("ScanAllParts(new table) = %+v, %v; want no part and no error", got, err)
	}
	rid := payloadexec.RowID("net-1", "db.scan_all_empty", "acct/1/n", 0)
	batch, err := conn.PrepareBatch(ctx, "INSERT INTO "+qualified)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("PrepareBatch: %v", err)
	}
	if err := batch.Append(rid, uint64(1)); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("batch.Append: %v", err)
	}
	if err := batch.Send(); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("batch.Send: %v", err)
	}
	if got, err := chexec.ScanAllParts(ctx, conn, qualified, sch); err != nil || len(got) != 1 || got[0].RowCount != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("ScanAllParts(one row) = %+v, %v; want one part of one row", got, err)
	}
	mustExec(t, conn, "TRUNCATE TABLE "+qualified)
	if got, err := chexec.ScanAllParts(ctx, conn, qualified, sch); err != nil || len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("ScanAllParts(truncated table) = %+v, %v; want no part and no error", got, err)
	}
}

- [ ] **Step 9: Scan every active part**

Replace `pkg/replay/chexec/scan.go` with (`ScanParts` keeps its signature, its empty-names refusal and its query; the scan loop moves into `scanTable`, shared with `ScanAllParts`; `scanPartRow` and `scanResults` are unchanged):

```go
package chexec

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"strings"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/lthash"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"
)

// PartScanResult is one real ClickHouse part's row-content commitment.
type PartScanResult struct {
	PartName  string
	RowLtHash string
	RowCount  uint64
}

// ScanParts recomputes row LtHash commitments from named active parts of a real
// ClickHouse table. It folds rows through payloadexec.RowElementHash so byte-side
// scans and replay execution use the same row identity and encoding.
func ScanParts(ctx context.Context, conn clickhouse.Conn, qualifiedTable string, schema payloadexec.TableSchema, partNames []string) ([]PartScanResult, error) {
	if len(partNames) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("chexec: ScanParts requires at least one part name")
	}
	byPart, err := scanTable(ctx, conn, qualifiedTable, schema, partNames)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return scanResults(qualifiedTable, partNames, byPart)
}

// ScanAllParts is ScanParts over every active part of the table: the same row
// derivation and refusals without the _part filter, sorted by part name. It is
// the install gate's scan of a scratch whose part names the caller does not
// know (spec 2026-10-14 §8.5 step 4). A part holds at least one row to be
// seen, so a table without rows gives an empty slice and no error, which is
// how a caller sees a rename race. It reads the whole table: only scratch
// tables and the rate-limited self-audit call it.
func ScanAllParts(ctx context.Context, conn clickhouse.Conn, qualifiedTable string, schema payloadexec.TableSchema) ([]PartScanResult, error) {
	byPart, err := scanTable(ctx, conn, qualifiedTable, schema, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	names := make([]string, 0, len(byPart))
	for name := range byPart {
		names = append(names, name)
	}
	// scanResults sorts by part name.
	return scanResults(qualifiedTable, names, byPart)
}

// scanTable folds the rows of qualifiedTable into one accumulator per part:
// of the named parts, or of every active part when partNames is nil.
func scanTable(ctx context.Context, conn clickhouse.Conn, qualifiedTable string, schema payloadexec.TableSchema, partNames []string) (map[string]*partAccumulator, error) {
	db, table, ok := strings.Cut(qualifiedTable, ".")
	if !ok {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("chexec: qualifiedTable must be db.table, got %q", qualifiedTable)
	}
	for _, c := range schema.Columns {
		if !supportedColumnType(c.Type) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("chexec: unsupported column type %q for part scan (column %q)", c.Type, c.Name)
		}
	}

	query, args := scanPartsQuery(db, table, schema, partNames)
	rows, err := conn.Query(ctx, query, args...)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("part scan query: %w", err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()

	byPart := map[string]*partAccumulator{}
	for rows.Next() {
		part, rowHash, err := scanPartRow(rows, schema)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		acc := byPart[part]
		if acc == nil {
			acc = &partAccumulator{hash: lthash.New()}
			byPart[part] = acc
		}
		acc.hash.AddHash(rowHash)
		acc.count++
	}
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("part scan rows: %w", err)
	}
	return byPart, nil
}

type partAccumulator struct {
	hash  *lthash.Hash
	count uint64
}

// scanPartsQuery selects the rows of the named parts, or of every active part
// when partNames is nil (ScanAllParts).
func scanPartsQuery(db, table string, schema payloadexec.TableSchema, partNames []string) (string, []any) {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("SELECT _part, ")
	b.WriteString(rowIDColumn)
	for _, c := range schema.Columns {
		b.WriteString(", ")
		b.WriteString(quoteIdent(c.Name))
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, " FROM %s.%s", quoteIdent(db), quoteIdent(table))
	if partNames == nil {
		return b.String(), nil
	}
	b.WriteString(" WHERE _part IN (")

	args := make([]any, 0, len(partNames))
	for i, name := range partNames {
		if i > 0 {
			b.WriteString(", ")
		}
		b.WriteString("?")
		args = append(args, name)
	}
	b.WriteString(")")
	return b.String(), args
}

type rowScanner interface {
	Scan(...any) error
}

func scanPartRow(rows rowScanner, schema payloadexec.TableSchema) (string, *lthash.Hash, error) {
	var part string
	var rid []byte
	dests := make([]any, len(schema.Columns)+2)
	dests[0] = &part
	dests[1] = &rid
	holders := make([]any, len(schema.Columns))
	for i, c := range schema.Columns {
		dest, err := newScanDest(c.Type)
		if err != nil {
			return "", nil, err
		}
		dests[i+2] = dest
		holders[i] = dest
	}
	if err := rows.Scan(dests...); err != nil {
		return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("part scan row: %w", err)
	}

	values := make([]any, len(schema.Columns))
	for i := range schema.Columns {
		value, err := derefScan(schema.Columns[i].Type, holders[i])
		if err != nil {
			return "", nil, err
		}
		values[i] = value
	}
	h, err := payloadexec.RowElementHash(schema, append([]byte(nil), rid...), values)
	if err != nil {
		return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("part %s: %w", part, err)
	}
	return part, h, nil
}

func scanResults(qualifiedTable string, partNames []string, byPart map[string]*partAccumulator) ([]PartScanResult, error) {
	out := make([]PartScanResult, 0, len(partNames))
	for _, name := range partNames {
		acc, ok := byPart[name]
		if !ok {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("part %q not found (or empty) in %s", name, qualifiedTable)
		}
		out = append(out, PartScanResult{
			PartName:  name,
			RowLtHash: "0x" + hex.EncodeToString(acc.hash.Bytes()),
			RowCount:  acc.count,
		})
	}
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].PartName < out[j].PartName })
	return out, nil
}
```

package chexec

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	clickhouse "github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"

	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/lthash"

// TestNewMaterializerInRefusesABadDatabaseOrPrefix pins the two refusals of
// the database-and-prefix materializer (spec 2026-10-14 §8.5, last paragraph):
// the database must be a plain lowercase ClickHouse name and the prefix a
// bounded token, because both are interpolated into every scratch statement.
// The database is checked first.
func TestNewMaterializerInRefusesABadDatabaseOrPrefix(t *testing.T) {
	for _, database := range []string{"", "Hg_rstage", "1db", "hg-rstage", "hg.rstage", "hg`x", "hg_rstage\n", "hg rstage"} {
		m, err := NewMaterializerIn("net-1", panicConn{}, database, "")
		want := fmt.Sprintf("chexec: materializer database %q must match [a-z_][a-z0-9_]*", database)
		if m != nil || err == nil || err.Error() != want {
			t.Errorf("NewMaterializerIn(database %q) = %v, %v; want nil, %q", database, m, err, want)
		}
	}
	for _, prefix := range []string{"", strings.Repeat("a", 97), "a.b", "a`b", "a b", "a/b", "m1_\n", "é"} {
		m, err := NewMaterializerIn("net-1", panicConn{}, "hg_rstage", prefix)
		want := fmt.Sprintf("chexec: materializer prefix %q must match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,96}", prefix)
		if m != nil || err == nil || err.Error() != want {
			t.Errorf("NewMaterializerIn(prefix %q) = %v, %v; want nil, %q", prefix, m, err, want)
		}
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct{ database, prefix string }{
		{"hg_rstage", "m-1_boot_"},
		{"_x", strings.Repeat("Z", 96)},
		{"hg_rstage", "-"},
	} {
		if m, err := NewMaterializerIn("net-1", panicConn{}, tc.database, tc.prefix); err != nil || m == nil {
			t.Errorf("NewMaterializerIn(%q, %q) = %v, %v; want a materializer", tc.database, tc.prefix, m, err)
		}
	}
}

// refusingCreateConn records every Exec like recordingConn and refuses each
// CREATE TABLE, so a test sees the scratch name in the materializer's error.
type refusingCreateConn struct{ recordingConn }

func (c *refusingCreateConn) Exec(_ context.Context, query string, _ ...any) error {
	c.execs = append(c.execs, query)
	if strings.HasPrefix(query, "CREATE TABLE ") {
		return errors.New("refused")
	}
	return nil
}

// TestMaterializerScratchStatementsNameTheirTable pins, without ClickHouse,
// the scratch table every statement of a materializer names: NewMaterializer
// keeps today's unqualified _hg_replay_scratch_<n> in the connection's default
// database byte for byte (statements and error texts), and NewMaterializerIn
// qualifies `<database>`.`<prefix>replay_<n>`; n counts per materializer, and
// the scratch is dropped on exit when the INSERT or the CREATE fails.
func TestMaterializerScratchStatementsNameTheirTable(t *testing.T) {
	schema := payloadexec.TableSchema{TableID: "db.t", Columns: []lthash.Column{{Name: "v", Type: "UInt64"}}}
	st := replay.PreparedStatement{
		Statement: replay.Statement{StatementID: "0xabc:1:n", TargetTableID: "db.t", PayloadFormat: payloadexec.PayloadFormatCSVWithNames},
		Payload:   []byte("v\n1\n"),
	}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name     string
		database string   // "" builds NewMaterializer
		refs     []string // the scratch of the first and second statement, as SQL names it
		first    string   // the first scratch, as an error names it
	}{
		{"NewMaterializer", "", []string{"`_hg_replay_scratch_1`", "`_hg_replay_scratch_2`"}, "_hg_replay_scratch_1"},
		{"NewMaterializerIn", "hg_rstage", []string{"`hg_rstage`.`m-1_replay_1`", "`hg_rstage`.`m-1_replay_2`"}, "hg_rstage.m-1_replay_1"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			materializer := func(conn clickhouse.Conn) *Materializer {
				if tc.database == "" {
					return NewMaterializer("net-1", conn)
				}
				m, err := NewMaterializerIn("net-1", conn, tc.database, "m-1_")
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("NewMaterializerIn: %v", err)
				}
				return m
			}
			conn := &recordingConn{}
			m := materializer(conn)
			var want []string
			for i, ref := range tc.refs {
				// recordingConn refuses every batch, so each Materialize stops at
				// the INSERT after its CREATE and still drops its scratch.
				if _, err := m.Materialize(context.Background(), schema, st); err == nil || err.Error() != "prepare insert batch: unused" {
					t.Fatalf("Materialize %d = %v, want the recording connection's batch refusal", i+1, err)
				}
				want = append(want,
					"CREATE TABLE "+ref+" (_hg_row_id FixedString(32), `v` UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple()",
					"DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "+ref)
			}
			if !slices.Equal(conn.execs, want) {
				t.Fatalf("statements = %q, want %q", conn.execs, want)
			}

			refusing := &refusingCreateConn{}
			_, err := materializer(refusing).Materialize(context.Background(), schema, st)
			if wantErr := "create scratch table " + tc.first + ": refused"; err == nil || err.Error() != wantErr {
				t.Fatalf("Materialize with a refused CREATE = %v, want %q", err, wantErr)
			}
			if last := refusing.execs[len(refusing.execs)-1]; last != "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "+tc.refs[0] {
				t.Fatalf("last statement after a refused CREATE = %q, want the drop of %s", last, tc.refs[0])
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestNewMaterializerInWithStoragePolicyRefusesUnsafeNames keeps policy text
// out of SQL unless it is a bounded identifier; the legacy name checks run first.
func TestNewMaterializerInWithStoragePolicyRefusesUnsafeNames(t *testing.T) {
	for _, policy := range []string{"", "1member", "a-b", "a.b", "a'b", "a`b", "a\\b", "a\nb", strings.Repeat("a", 129), "成员"} {
		m, err := NewMaterializerInWithStoragePolicy("net-1", panicConn{}, "hg_rstage", "m1_", policy)
		want := fmt.Sprintf("chexec: materializer storage policy %q must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,127}", policy)
		if m != nil || err == nil || err.Error() != want {
			t.Fatalf("policy %q: got %v, %v; want nil, %q", policy, m, err, want)
		}
	}
	for _, policy := range []string{"member", "_member", "Member_1", strings.Repeat("a", 128)} {
		if m, err := NewMaterializerInWithStoragePolicy("net-1", panicConn{}, "hg_rstage", "m1_", policy); m == nil || err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("policy %q: %v, %v", policy, m, err)
		}
	}
	if _, err := NewMaterializerInWithStoragePolicy("net-1", panicConn{}, "Bad", "m1_", "member"); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "materializer database") {
		t.Fatalf("database validation: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := NewMaterializerInWithStoragePolicy("net-1", panicConn{}, "hg_rstage", "", "member"); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "materializer prefix") {
		t.Fatalf("prefix validation: %v", err)
	}
}

// TestMaterializerStoragePolicyIsExplicitOnlyForTheNewConstructor pins all
// legacy CREATE bytes while requiring the new constructor's explicit policy.
func TestMaterializerStoragePolicyIsExplicitOnlyForTheNewConstructor(t *testing.T) {
	schema := payloadexec.TableSchema{TableID: "db.t", Columns: []lthash.Column{{Name: "v", Type: "UInt64"}}}
	st := replay.PreparedStatement{Statement: replay.Statement{StatementID: "0xabc:1:n", TargetTableID: "db.t", PayloadFormat: payloadexec.PayloadFormatCSVWithNames}, Payload: []byte("v\n1\n")}
	for _, tc := range []struct{ name, policy, ref string }{
		{"legacy", "", "`_hg_replay_scratch_1`"}, {"named", "", "`hg_rstage`.`m1_replay_1`"}, {"policy", "member", "`hg_rstage`.`m1_replay_1`"},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			conn := &recordingConn{}
			var m *Materializer
			var err error
			switch tc.name {
			case "legacy":
				m = NewMaterializer("net-1", conn)
			case "named":
				m, err = NewMaterializerIn("net-1", conn, "hg_rstage", "m1_")
			default:
				m, err = NewMaterializerInWithStoragePolicy("net-1", conn, "hg_rstage", "m1_", tc.policy)
			}
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if _, err = m.Materialize(context.Background(), schema, st); err == nil || err.Error() != "prepare insert batch: unused" {
				t.Fatalf("Materialize = %v", err)
			}
			want := "CREATE TABLE " + tc.ref + " (_hg_row_id FixedString(32), `v` UInt64) ENGINE = MergeTree ORDER BY tuple()"
			if tc.policy != "" {
				want += " SETTINGS storage_policy = '" + tc.policy + "'"
			}
			if !slices.Equal(conn.execs, []string{want, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS " + tc.ref}) {
				t.Fatalf("SQL = %q, want CREATE %q and exact DROP", conn.execs, want)
			}
		})
	}
}
