```go
// TestDecodeConfigYAMLRefusesStorageIntegrityBackupKeys pins the refusal of an
// object-store key in a config file (Plan S3-C1 contract §18, K23): either
// half, any value (empty and null included), whether or not storage
// integrity is enabled, and through an alias or a merge key.
func TestDecodeConfigYAMLRefusesStorageIntegrityBackupKeys(t *testing.T) {
	const idRefusal = "storage_integrity.backup.access_key_id is not read from the config file; set STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID instead"
	const secretRefusal = "storage_integrity.backup.secret_access_key is not read from the config file; set STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY instead"
	for name, tc := range map[string]struct{ doc, want string }{
		"an access key id":             {"storage_integrity:\n  backup:\n    bucket_url: x\n    access_key_id: GOOG1EXAMPLE\n", idRefusal},
		"a secret":                     {"storage_integrity:\n  backup:\n    secret_access_key: in-the-file\n", secretRefusal},
		"an empty access key id":       {"storage_integrity:\n  backup:\n    access_key_id: \"\"\n", idRefusal},
		"a null secret":                {"storage_integrity:\n  backup:\n    secret_access_key:\n", secretRefusal},
		"both, the id first":           {"storage_integrity:\n  backup:\n    secret_access_key: s\n    access_key_id: i\n", idRefusal},
		"storage integrity enabled":    {"storage_integrity:\n  enabled: true\n  backup:\n    access_key_id: i\n", idRefusal},
		"storage integrity disabled":   {"storage_integrity:\n  enabled: false\n  backup:\n    secret_access_key: s\n", secretRefusal},
		"a backup block through alias": {"b: &b\n  secret_access_key: s\nstorage_integrity:\n  backup: *b\n", secretRefusal},
		"a storage_integrity alias":    {"si: &si\n  backup:\n    access_key_id: i\nstorage_integrity: *si\n", idRefusal},
		"through a merge key":          {"b: &b\n  access_key_id: i\nstorage_integrity:\n  backup:\n    <<: *b\n    bucket_url: x\n", idRefusal},
		"through a merge list":         {"a: &a\n  bucket_url: x\nb: &b\n  secret_access_key: s\nstorage_integrity:\n  backup:\n    <<: [*a, *b]\n", secretRefusal},
	} {
		_, err := decodeConfigYAML([]byte(tc.doc))
		require.EqualErrorf(t, err, tc.want, name)
	}
	for name, doc := range map[string]string{
		"the job config":                 storageIntegrityBackupJobYAML,
		"the keys outside backup":        "storage_integrity:\n  access_key_id: i\n  secret_access_key: s\n",
		"the keys in another block":      "node:\n  backup:\n    access_key_id: i\n",
		"a null backup block":            "storage_integrity:\n  backup:\n",
		"a quoted << key":                "storage_integrity:\n  backup:\n    \"<<\": {access_key_id: i}\n",
		"a scratch prefix and no secret": "storage_integrity:\n  backup:\n    scratch_prefix: p1drill_b_\n",
		"an empty document":              "",
	} {
		_, err := decodeConfigYAML([]byte(doc))
		require.NoErrorf(t, err, name)
	}
}

// TestStorageIntegrityBackupJobValidation pins ValidateBackupJob (Plan S3-C1
// contract §18): the job needs the arbiter, the owner's ClickHouse as a named
// user, the network id, the bucket and the owner; it never reads
// storage_integrity.enabled. The bucket's form is objstore.ParseBucket's,
// which standalone checks before it reads the key or opens anything.
func TestStorageIntegrityBackupJobValidation(t *testing.T) {
	require.NoError(t, validStorageIntegrityBackupJobConfig().ValidateBackupJob(), "owner 0, max_chain_links 0 (the default 7)")
	for _, links := range []uint32{1, 7, 30} {
		cfg := validStorageIntegrityBackupJobConfig()
		cfg.Backup.MaxChainLinks = links
		require.NoErrorf(t, cfg.ValidateBackupJob(), "max_chain_links %d", links)
	}

	for name, tc := range map[string]struct {
		edit func(*StorageIntegrityConfig)
		want string
	}{
		"no arbiter peers":    {func(c *StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.ArbiterPeers = nil }, "storage_integrity.arbiter_peers is required"},
		"a peer without addr": {func(c *StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.ArbiterPeers[0].Addr = "" }, "storage_integrity.arbiter_peers[0].addr is required"},
		"no clickhouse dsn":   {func(c *StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.ClickhouseDSN = "" }, "storage_integrity.clickhouse_dsn is required"},
		"the default user":    {func(c *StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.ClickhouseUsername = "" }, "storage_integrity.clickhouse_username is required: storage-integrity backup and restore-drill never use the passwordless default user"},
		"no network id":       {func(c *StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.SNode.NetworkID = " " }, "storage_integrity.snode.network_id is required"},
		"no bucket":           {func(c *StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.Backup.BucketURL = "" }, "storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url is required"},
		"a blank bucket":      {func(c *StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.Backup.BucketURL = " " }, "storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url is required"},
		"no owner":            {func(c *StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.Backup.OwnerIndexerID = nil }, "storage_integrity.backup.owner_indexer_id is required for storage-integrity backup"},
		"a chain of 31":       {func(c *StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.Backup.MaxChainLinks = 31 }, "storage_integrity.backup.max_chain_links must be between 1 and 30, got 31"},
	} {
		cfg := validStorageIntegrityBackupJobConfig()
		cfg.ArbiterPeers = append([]StorageIntegrityPeer(nil), cfg.ArbiterPeers...)
		tc.edit(&cfg)
		require.ErrorContainsf(t, cfg.ValidateBackupJob(), tc.want, name)
	}

	enabledHost := validStorageIntegrityConfig()
	require.ErrorContains(t, enabledHost.ValidateBackupJob(), "storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url is required", "a host config is not a backup job config")
	all := StorageIntegrityConfig{}.ValidateBackupJob()
	for _, want := range []string{"arbiter_peers", "clickhouse_dsn", "clickhouse_username", "snode.network_id", "backup.bucket_url", "backup.owner_indexer_id"} {
		require.ErrorContains(t, all, want, "every refusal is reported at once")
	}
}

// TestStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillValidation pins ValidateRestoreDrill (Plan
// S3-C1 contract §18): the drill needs what a backup needs except the owner
// (its --owner flag names it) and a scratch prefix for its hg_rstage tables.
func TestStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillValidation(t *testing.T) {
	require.NoError(t, validStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillConfig().ValidateRestoreDrill())
	for _, prefix := range []string{"p1drill_a_", "p1drill_c_", "A-Z_0-9", strings.Repeat("p", 64)} {
		cfg := validStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillConfig()
		cfg.Backup.ScratchPrefix = prefix
		require.NoErrorf(t, cfg.ValidateRestoreDrill(), "scratch prefix %q", prefix)
	}
	for _, prefix := range []string{"", "p1.drill", "p1 drill", "p1`drill", "hg_rstage.p1", strings.Repeat("p", 65)} {
		cfg := validStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillConfig()
		cfg.Backup.ScratchPrefix = prefix
		require.EqualErrorf(t, cfg.ValidateRestoreDrill(),
			fmt.Sprintf("storage_integrity.backup.scratch_prefix must match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}, got %q", prefix), "scratch prefix %q", prefix)
	}
	for name, tc := range map[string]struct {
		edit func(*StorageIntegrityConfig)
		want string
	}{
		"no arbiter peers": {func(c *StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.ArbiterPeers = nil }, "storage_integrity.arbiter_peers is required"},
		"the default user": {func(c *StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.ClickhouseUsername = "" }, "storage_integrity.clickhouse_username is required: storage-integrity backup and restore-drill never use the passwordless default user"},
		"no bucket":        {func(c *StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.Backup.BucketURL = "" }, "storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url is required"},
		"no network id":    {func(c *StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.SNode.NetworkID = "" }, "storage_integrity.snode.network_id is required"},
	} {
		cfg := validStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillConfig()
		tc.edit(&cfg)
		require.ErrorContainsf(t, cfg.ValidateRestoreDrill(), tc.want, name)
	}
	require.ErrorContains(t, validStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillConfig().ValidateBackupJob(),
		"storage_integrity.backup.owner_indexer_id is required for storage-integrity backup", "only a backup needs the owner in its config")
}

// TestStorageIntegrityS3CredentialsComeOnlyFromTheEnvironment pins the key
// source (Plan S3-C1 contract §18, K23): both halves from the environment,
// read when asked, never from a config.
func TestStorageIntegrityS3CredentialsComeOnlyFromTheEnvironment(t *testing.T) {
	const refusal = "STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY must both be set"
	t.Setenv(StorageIntegrityS3AccessKeyIDEnv, "GOOG1EXAMPLEACCESSKEYID")
	t.Setenv(StorageIntegrityS3SecretAccessKeyEnv, "example-secret-from-the-environment")
	id, secret, err := StorageIntegrityS3Credentials()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, "GOOG1EXAMPLEACCESSKEYID", id)
	require.Equal(t, "example-secret-from-the-environment", secret)

	t.Setenv(StorageIntegrityS3SecretAccessKeyEnv, "")
	id, secret, err = StorageIntegrityS3Credentials()
	require.EqualError(t, err, refusal)
	require.Empty(t, id, "nothing is returned with a refusal")
	require.Empty(t, secret)
	require.NotContains(t, err.Error(), "GOOG1EXAMPLEACCESSKEYID", "a refusal never names a key")

	t.Setenv(StorageIntegrityS3AccessKeyIDEnv, "")
	t.Setenv(StorageIntegrityS3SecretAccessKeyEnv, "example-secret-from-the-environment")
	_, _, err = StorageIntegrityS3Credentials()
	require.EqualError(t, err, refusal)
	require.NotContains(t, err.Error(), "example-secret-from-the-environment")

	require.Equal(t, "STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID", StorageIntegrityS3AccessKeyIDEnv)
	require.Equal(t, "STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY", StorageIntegrityS3SecretAccessKeyEnv)
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement the job config**

Create `config/storage_integrity_job.go`:

```go
package config

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"regexp"
	"strings"

	"gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

// StorageIntegrityS3AccessKeyIDEnv and StorageIntegrityS3SecretAccessKeyEnv
// name the only source of the object-store HMAC key of `sentio-node
// storage-integrity backup` and `restore-drill` (housegate spec 2026-10-14
// §16 P1, Plan S3-C1 clarification K23): a Secret's environment, never the
// config file.
const (
	StorageIntegrityS3AccessKeyIDEnv     = "STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID"
	StorageIntegrityS3SecretAccessKeyEnv = "STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"
)

// StorageIntegrityBackup is storage_integrity.backup: where the backup and
// restore-drill jobs find the replica bucket (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §16
// P1). A storage-integrity host never sets it, and
// StorageIntegrityConfig.Validate ignores it.
type StorageIntegrityBackup struct {
	// BucketURL is the bucket's S3 endpoint, http(s)://<host>[:port]/<bucket>
	// (objstore.ParseBucket), for example
	// https://storage.googleapis.com/<bucket>.
	BucketURL string `yaml:"bucket_url"`
	// OwnerIndexerID is the SI indexer whose hg_safe the backup job copies,
	// under the prefix owner-<id>/. A pointer, because 0 is the founding
	// indexer's id; restore-drill takes its owner from --owner instead.
	OwnerIndexerID *uint64 `yaml:"owner_indexer_id"`
	// MaxChainLinks caps a backup chain: one full backup and at most
	// MaxChainLinks-1 incremental ones on it. 0 selects
	// objstore.DefaultMaxChainLinks (7).
	MaxChainLinks uint32 `yaml:"max_chain_links"`
	// ScratchPrefix names restore-drill's scratch tables
	// hg_rstage.<prefix><n>; the backup job does not read it.
	ScratchPrefix string `yaml:"scratch_prefix"`
}

// storageIntegrityScratchPrefixPattern is objstore.NewScratchNamer's rule.
var storageIntegrityScratchPrefixPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`)

// storageIntegrityMaxChainLinksLimit is objstore.MaxChainLinksLimit, restated
// because config gains no arbiter-core import (Plan S3-C1 contract §18);
// standalone's TestStorageIntegrityBackupPrintsOnlyTheIndexLine pins the two
// together.
const storageIntegrityMaxChainLinksLimit = 30

// storageIntegrityBackupKeyRefusals are the storage_integrity.backup keys a
// config file must not carry, each with the variable that holds its value.
var storageIntegrityBackupKeyRefusals = []struct{ key, env string }{
	{key: "access_key_id", env: StorageIntegrityS3AccessKeyIDEnv},
	{key: "secret_access_key", env: StorageIntegrityS3SecretAccessKeyEnv},
}

// LoadStorageIntegrityJobConfig reads the config of `sentio-node
// storage-integrity backup` and `restore-drill`. It decodes with
// decodeConfigYAML, so every refusal of a secret in the file holds, and it
// never calls NodeConfig.LoadAndValidate: a job has no node identity and no
// PRIVATE_KEY. The command validates the result (ValidateBackupJob,
// ValidateRestoreDrill).
func LoadStorageIntegrityJobConfig(path string) (*Config, error) {
	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("read config file: %w", err)
	}
	cfg, err := decodeConfigYAML(data)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unmarshal config: %w", err)
	}
	return &cfg, nil
}

// ValidateBackupJob checks the config of `sentio-node storage-integrity
// backup`. It reports every refusal at once and never reads
// storage_integrity.enabled: the job is not a storage-integrity host.
func (c StorageIntegrityConfig) ValidateBackupJob() error {
	errs := c.validateStorageIntegrityJob()
	if c.Backup.OwnerIndexerID == nil {
		errs = append(errs, errors.New("storage_integrity.backup.owner_indexer_id is required for storage-integrity backup"))
	}
	return errors.Join(errs...)
}

// ValidateRestoreDrill checks the config of `sentio-node storage-integrity
// restore-drill`, whose owner is its --owner flag.
func (c StorageIntegrityConfig) ValidateRestoreDrill() error {
	errs := c.validateStorageIntegrityJob()
	if !storageIntegrityScratchPrefixPattern.MatchString(c.Backup.ScratchPrefix) {
		errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("storage_integrity.backup.scratch_prefix must match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}, got %q", c.Backup.ScratchPrefix))
	}
	return errors.Join(errs...)
}

// validateStorageIntegrityJob holds the refusals both jobs share: the arbiter
// peers (for the manifests), the ClickHouse as a named user (never the
// passwordless default), the network id, the bucket and the chain cap.
func (c StorageIntegrityConfig) validateStorageIntegrityJob() []error {
	var errs []error
	required := func(path, value string) {
		if strings.TrimSpace(value) == "" {
			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("storage_integrity.%s is required", path))
		}
	}
	if len(c.ArbiterPeers) == 0 {
		errs = append(errs, errors.New("storage_integrity.arbiter_peers is required"))
	}
	for i, peer := range c.ArbiterPeers {
		required(fmt.Sprintf("arbiter_peers[%d].id", i), peer.ID)
		required(fmt.Sprintf("arbiter_peers[%d].addr", i), peer.Addr)
	}
	required("clickhouse_dsn", c.ClickhouseDSN)
	if strings.TrimSpace(c.ClickhouseUsername) == "" {
		errs = append(errs, errors.New("storage_integrity.clickhouse_username is required: storage-integrity backup and restore-drill never use the passwordless default user"))
	}
	required("snode.network_id", c.SNode.NetworkID)
	// The bucket's form is objstore.ParseBucket's; standalone checks it.
	required("backup.bucket_url", c.Backup.BucketURL)
	if c.Backup.MaxChainLinks > storageIntegrityMaxChainLinksLimit {
		errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("storage_integrity.backup.max_chain_links must be between 1 and 30, got %d", c.Backup.MaxChainLinks))
	}
	return errs
}

// StorageIntegrityS3Credentials returns the object-store HMAC key from the
// environment, its only source (a Secret's env in the backup CronJob and the
// drill Job). Both halves must be set; a refusal names neither value.
func StorageIntegrityS3Credentials() (accessKeyID, secretAccessKey string, err error) {
	accessKeyID = os.Getenv(StorageIntegrityS3AccessKeyIDEnv)
	secretAccessKey = os.Getenv(StorageIntegrityS3SecretAccessKeyEnv)
	if accessKeyID == "" || secretAccessKey == "" {
		return "", "", fmt.Errorf("%s and %s must both be set", StorageIntegrityS3AccessKeyIDEnv, StorageIntegrityS3SecretAccessKeyEnv)
	}
	return accessKeyID, secretAccessKey, nil
}

// refuseStorageIntegrityBackupKeys refuses a document that sets
// storage_integrity.backup.access_key_id or secret_access_key, whatever the
// value (empty and null included) and whether or not storage integrity is
// enabled: the jobs' ConfigMap must never hold the HMAC key. Like
// refuseStorageIntegrityClickhousePasswordKey it reads the YAML nodes,
// following aliases and merge keys.
func refuseStorageIntegrityBackupKeys(data []byte) error {
	var doc yaml.Node
	if err := yaml.Unmarshal(data, &doc); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if doc.Kind != yaml.DocumentNode || len(doc.Content) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	for _, refusal := range storageIntegrityBackupKeyRefusals {
		for _, block := range yamlMappingValues(doc.Content[0], "storage_integrity") {
			for _, backup := range yamlMappingValues(block, "backup") {
				if len(yamlMappingValues(backup, refusal.key)) > 0 {
					return fmt.Errorf("storage_integrity.backup.%s is not read from the config file; set %s instead", refusal.key, refusal.env)
				}
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}
```

```go
// backupTestRecording is what the backup and restore-drill commands handed

type backupTestRecording struct {

	drills    []objstore.Drill
	closed    []string

// backupTestConn is the fake ClickHouse connection: the fake runs never query

type backupTestConn struct {
	clickhouse.Conn
	rec *backupTestRecording

func (c *backupTestConn) Close() error {
	c.rec.closed = append(c.rec.closed, "clickhouse")
	return nil

// backupTestManifests is the fake arbiter; the fake runs never read it.
type backupTestManifests struct{ objstore.ManifestSource }

// backupTestDeps records the seams' inputs and answers backup and drill runs
// with backup and drill.
func backupTestDeps(
	rec *backupTestRecording,
	conn *backupTestConn,
	manifests objstore.ManifestSource,
	backup func(*objstore.Backuper) (objstore.BackupIndex, error),
	drill func(context.Context, *objstore.Drill) (objstore.DrillVerdict, error),
) storageIntegrityBackupDeps {
	return storageIntegrityBackupDeps{
		openClickHouse: func(opts *clickhouse.Options) (clickhouse.Conn, error) {
			rec.options = append(rec.options, *opts)
			return conn, nil
		},
		openManifests: func(peers []dataplane.Peer) (objstore.ManifestSource, func(), error) {
			rec.peers = append(rec.peers, peers)
			return manifests, func() { rec.closed = append(rec.closed, "arbiter") }, nil
		},
		runBackup: func(_ context.Context, b *objstore.Backuper) (objstore.BackupIndex, error) {
			rec.backupers = append(rec.backupers, *b)
			return backup(b)
		},
		runDrill: func(ctx context.Context, d *objstore.Drill) (objstore.DrillVerdict, error) {
			rec.drills = append(rec.drills, *d)
			return drill(ctx, d)
		},
	}
}

// requireOneJSONLine returns stdout's only line, decoded into T.
func requireOneJSONLine[T any](t *testing.T, stdout string) T {
	t.Helper()
	line, ok := strings.CutSuffix(stdout, "\n")
	require.True(t, ok, "stdout ends with one newline")
	require.NotContains(t, line, "\n", "stdout holds exactly one line")
	var value T
	decoder := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(line))
	decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()
	require.NoError(t, decoder.Decode(&value))
	return value
}

// TestStorageIntegrityBackupPrintsOnlyTheIndexLine pins Plan S3-C1 contract
// §18: stdout gets exactly one line, the index object's JSON, and never a key
// or a password; a refusal or a failed backup prints nothing there.
func TestStorageIntegrityBackupPrintsOnlyTheIndexLine(t *testing.T) {
	setBackupTestEnv(t)
	rec := &backupTestRecording{}
	conn := &backupTestConn{rec: rec}
	index := backupTestIndex()
	deps := backupTestDeps(rec, conn, &backupTestManifests{},
		func(*objstore.Backuper) (objstore.BackupIndex, error) { return index, nil }, nil)

	var stdout bytes.Buffer
	require.NoError(t, runStorageIntegrityBackup(t.Context(), backupTestConfig(1), &stdout, deps))
	require.Equal(t, index, requireOneJSONLine[objstore.BackupIndex](t, stdout.String()))
	for _, secret := range []string{backupTestSecret, backupTestAccessKeyID, backupTestPassword} {
		require.NotContains(t, stdout.String(), secret)
	}
	want, err := json.Marshal(index)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, string(want)+"\n", stdout.String())

	failing := backupTestDeps(rec, conn, &backupTestManifests{},
		func(*objstore.Backuper) (objstore.BackupIndex, error) {
			return objstore.BackupIndex{}, errors.New("objstore: backup 20261016T034700Z-full of indexer 1 exists already; a backup name is never reused")
		}, nil)
	stdout.Reset()
	err = runStorageIntegrityBackup(t.Context(), backupTestConfig(1), &stdout, failing)
	require.EqualError(t, err, "storage-integrity backup of indexer 1: objstore: backup 20261016T034700Z-full of indexer 1 exists already; a backup name is never reused")
	require.Empty(t, stdout.String(), "a failed backup prints nothing on stdout")

	require.ErrorContains(t, runStorageIntegrityBackup(t.Context(), nil, &stdout, deps), "storage-integrity backup requires a config")
	opened := len(rec.options)
	for name, tc := range map[string]struct {
		edit  func(*config.StorageIntegrityConfig)
		unset string
		want  string
	}{
		"no owner":             {edit: func(c *config.StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.Backup.OwnerIndexerID = nil }, want: "storage_integrity.backup.owner_indexer_id is required for storage-integrity backup"},
		"default login":        {edit: func(c *config.StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.ClickhouseUsername = "" }, want: "storage_integrity.clickhouse_username is required"},
		"no secret":            {unset: config.StorageIntegrityS3SecretAccessKeyEnv, want: "STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY must both be set"},
		"no key id":            {unset: config.StorageIntegrityS3AccessKeyIDEnv, want: "STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY must both be set"},
		"a bucket with a path": {edit: func(c *config.StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.Backup.BucketURL = backupTestBucket + "/owner-1" }, want: `storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url: objstore: bucket "` + backupTestBucket + `/owner-1" must be http(s)://<host>[:port]/<bucket> with no further path, query or trailing slash`},
		"a trailing slash":     {edit: func(c *config.StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.Backup.BucketURL = backupTestBucket + "/" }, want: "storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url: objstore: bucket"},
		"a gs:// bucket": {edit: func(c *config.StorageIntegrityConfig) {
			c.Backup.BucketURL = "gs://sentio-352722-si-devnet2-si-v2-replica"
		}, want: "storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url: objstore: bucket"},
		"a bad bucket, no key": {edit: func(c *config.StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.Backup.BucketURL = "gs://x" }, unset: config.StorageIntegrityS3AccessKeyIDEnv, want: "storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url: objstore: bucket"},
		"objstore's cap + 1": {edit: func(c *config.StorageIntegrityConfig) {
			c.Backup.MaxChainLinks = uint32(objstore.MaxChainLinksLimit) + 1
		}, want: "storage_integrity.backup.max_chain_links must be between 1 and 30, got 31"},
	} {
		setBackupTestEnv(t)
		if tc.unset != "" {
			t.Setenv(tc.unset, "")
		}
		cfg := backupTestConfig(1)
		if tc.edit != nil {
			tc.edit(&cfg.StorageIntegrity)
		}
		stdout.Reset()
		require.ErrorContainsf(t, runStorageIntegrityBackup(t.Context(), cfg, &stdout, deps), tc.want, name)

// TestStorageIntegrityBackupOpensTheClickHouseAsTheConfiguredUser pins the

func TestStorageIntegrityBackupOpensTheClickHouseAsTheConfiguredUser(t *testing.T) {
	setBackupTestEnv(t)
	rec := &backupTestRecording{}
	conn := &backupTestConn{rec: rec}
	manifests := &backupTestManifests{}
	deps := backupTestDeps(rec, conn, manifests,
		func(*objstore.Backuper) (objstore.BackupIndex, error) { return backupTestIndex(), nil }, nil)

	require.NoError(t, runStorageIntegrityBackup(t.Context(), backupTestConfig(0), &stdout, deps))
	require.Equal(t, []clickhouse.Options{{

		Auth: clickhouse.Auth{Username: "si_backup", Password: backupTestPassword},
	}}, rec.options)
	require.Equal(t, [][]dataplane.Peer{{{ID: "storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-0", GRPCAddr: "storage-integrity-si-v2-arbiter-0:7080"}}}, rec.peers)
	require.Len(t, rec.backupers, 1)

	require.True(t, b.Manifests == objstore.ManifestSource(manifests), "the backup reads the arbiter's manifests")
	require.Equal(t, backupTestBucket, b.Bucket.URL())

	require.Equal(t, uint32(7), b.MaxChainLinks)

// TestStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillExitsNonZeroUnlessTheVerdictPasses pins the
// drill's outcome (Plan S3-C1 contract §18, K27): stdout gets exactly one
// line, the verdict's JSON, whether or not it passes, and the command fails
// with ErrStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillFailed unless it passes; a drill that
// cannot run prints nothing on stdout.
func TestStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillExitsNonZeroUnlessTheVerdictPasses(t *testing.T) {
	setBackupTestEnv(t)
	owner := httptest.NewServer(nil)
	t.Cleanup(owner.Close)
	opts := StorageIntegrityRestoreDrillOptions{Owner: 1, OwnerRPC: owner.URL, Backup: "20261017T034700Z-incr"}

	for _, pass := range []bool{true, false} {
		rec := &backupTestRecording{}
		conn := &backupTestConn{rec: rec}
		manifests := &backupTestManifests{}
		verdict := drillTestVerdict(pass)
		deps := backupTestDeps(rec, conn, manifests, nil,
			func(context.Context, *objstore.Drill) (objstore.DrillVerdict, error) { return verdict, nil })
		var stdout bytes.Buffer
		err := runStorageIntegrityRestoreDrill(t.Context(), restoreDrillTestConfig(), opts, &stdout, deps)
		if pass {
			require.NoError(t, err)
		} else {
			require.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillFailed)
			require.EqualError(t, err, "storage-integrity restore drill: the verdict is not pass")
		}
		require.Equal(t, verdict, requireOneJSONLine[objstore.DrillVerdict](t, stdout.String()), "pass %v: the verdict is printed either way", pass)
		require.NotContains(t, stdout.String(), backupTestSecret)

		require.Equal(t, []clickhouse.Options{{
			Addr: []string{"storage-integrity-si-v2-p1-staging-source:9000"},
			Auth: clickhouse.Auth{Username: "si_restore", Password: backupTestPassword},
		}}, rec.options, "the drill restores into the staging installation as si_restore")
		require.Len(t, rec.drills, 1)
		d := rec.drills[0]
		require.True(t, d.Conn == clickhouse.Conn(conn))
		require.True(t, d.Manifests == objstore.ManifestSource(manifests))
		require.NotNil(t, d.Schemas, "schemas come from the owner's host")
		require.Equal(t, backupTestBucket, d.Bucket.URL())
		require.Equal(t, uint64(1), d.Owner, "the owner is --owner")
		require.Equal(t, "devnet2", d.NetworkID)
		require.Equal(t, objstore.Credentials{AccessKeyID: backupTestAccessKeyID, SecretAccessKey: backupTestSecret}, d.Credentials)
		require.Equal(t, "20261017T034700Z-incr", d.Backup)
		require.NotNil(t, d.Scratch)
		require.Equal(t, objstore.Scratch{Database: "hg_rstage", Table: "p1drill_b_1"}, d.Scratch.Next(), "scratch tables carry storage_integrity.backup.scratch_prefix")
		require.ElementsMatch(t, []string{"clickhouse", "arbiter"}, rec.closed)
	}

	rec := &backupTestRecording{}
	deps := backupTestDeps(rec, &backupTestConn{rec: rec}, &backupTestManifests{}, nil,
		func(context.Context, *objstore.Drill) (objstore.DrillVerdict, error) {
			return objstore.DrillVerdict{}, errors.New("objstore: no backup of indexer 1 under " + backupTestBucket + "/owner-1/")
		})
	var stdout bytes.Buffer
	err := runStorageIntegrityRestoreDrill(t.Context(), restoreDrillTestConfig(), opts, &stdout, deps)
	require.EqualError(t, err, "storage-integrity restore drill of indexer 1: objstore: no backup of indexer 1 under "+backupTestBucket+"/owner-1/")
	require.NotErrorIs(t, err, ErrStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillFailed)
	require.Empty(t, stdout.String(), "a drill that did not run prints no verdict")

	stdout.Reset()
	require.ErrorContains(t, runStorageIntegrityRestoreDrill(t.Context(), nil, opts, &stdout, deps), "storage-integrity restore-drill requires a config")
	founder := uint64(0)
	for name, tc := range map[string]struct {
		edit   func(*config.StorageIntegrityConfig)
		rpcURL string
		want   string
	}{
		"no scratch prefix":           {edit: func(c *config.StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.Backup.ScratchPrefix = "" }, rpcURL: opts.OwnerRPC, want: `storage_integrity.backup.scratch_prefix must match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}, got ""`},
		"another owner in the config": {edit: func(c *config.StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.Backup.OwnerIndexerID = &founder }, rpcURL: opts.OwnerRPC, want: "storage-integrity restore-drill --owner 1 is not storage_integrity.backup.owner_indexer_id 0"},
		"no owner RPC":                {want: "storage-integrity restore-drill requires --owner-rpc: the owner host's storage RPC URL, which serves each table's schema"},
		"an owner RPC without scheme": {rpcURL: "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-b:33003", want: `storage-integrity restore-drill --owner-rpc "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-b:33003" must be an http(s) URL`},
		"a bucket with a query":       {edit: func(c *config.StorageIntegrityConfig) { c.Backup.BucketURL = backupTestBucket + "?x=1" }, rpcURL: opts.OwnerRPC, want: "storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url: objstore: bucket"},
	} {
		cfg := restoreDrillTestConfig()
		if tc.edit != nil {
			tc.edit(&cfg.StorageIntegrity)
		}
		stdout.Reset()
		err := runStorageIntegrityRestoreDrill(t.Context(), cfg, StorageIntegrityRestoreDrillOptions{Owner: 1, OwnerRPC: tc.rpcURL}, &stdout, deps)
		require.ErrorContainsf(t, err, tc.want, name)
		require.Emptyf(t, stdout.String(), "%s: a refusal prints nothing on stdout", name)
	}
	require.Len(t, rec.options, 1, "a refusal opens no ClickHouse connection")
}

// fixedOwnerStatuses is the owner host's table state as its status RPC
// serves it; it records each [database, table] it was asked for.
type fixedOwnerStatuses struct {
	mu       sync.Mutex
	statuses map[string]hgregistry.TableStatus
	asked    []string
}

func (f *fixedOwnerStatuses) StorageIntegrityTableStatus(database, table string) hgregistry.TableStatus {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	f.asked = append(f.asked, database+"|"+table)
	if status, ok := f.statuses[database+"."+table]; ok {
		return status
	}
	return hgregistry.TableStatus{Status: hgregistry.TableStatusPending}
}

// startOwnerStatusRPC serves sentio_getStorageIntegrityTableStatus from
// statuses on sentio-node's own storage RPC server and returns its URL.
func startOwnerStatusRPC(t *testing.T, statuses *fixedOwnerStatuses) string {
	t.Helper()
	server, err := rpc.NewStorageNodeRPCServer(nil, nil, rpc.WithStorageIntegrityTableStatus(statuses))
	require.NoError(t, err)
	httpServer := httptest.NewServer(server.Handler)
	t.Cleanup(httpServer.Close)
	return httpServer.URL
}

// drillTestSchemaJSON is backupTestSchemaJSON for another table id.
func drillTestSchemaJSON(tableID string) string {
	return strings.Replace(backupTestSchemaJSON, "devuser1.s3_p1", tableID, 1)
}

// TestStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillTakesSchemasFromTheOwnersStatusRPC pins the
// drill's schema source (Plan S3-C1 contract §18, K27): each table's schema
// is sentio_getStorageIntegrityTableStatus [database, table] on --owner-rpc,
// taken from any answer that carries schema_json (an Active table, a held
// Pending one, a quarantined host's Refused one, a Gone one) and decoded as
// the registry's schema; its hash is objstore's to check against the
// manifest, so the answer's schema_hash is not trusted here.
func TestStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillTakesSchemasFromTheOwnersStatusRPC(t *testing.T) {
	setBackupTestEnv(t)
	statuses := &fixedOwnerStatuses{statuses: map[string]hgregistry.TableStatus{
		"devuser1.s3_p1":      {Status: hgregistry.TableStatusActive, SchemaJSON: backupTestSchemaJSON, SchemaHash: "0xnot-checked-here", RegistryVersion: 41},
		"devuser1.held":       {Status: hgregistry.TableStatusPending, SchemaJSON: drillTestSchemaJSON("devuser1.held"), RegistryVersion: 41},
		"devuser1.quarantine": {Status: hgregistry.TableStatusRefused, RefusedCode: "indexer_quarantined", RefusedReason: "storage-integrity indexer 1 is quarantined", SchemaJSON: drillTestSchemaJSON("devuser1.quarantine"), RegistryVersion: 41},
		"devuser1.gone":       {Status: hgregistry.TableStatusGone, SchemaJSON: drillTestSchemaJSON("devuser1.gone"), RegistryVersion: 42},
	}}
	ownerRPC := startOwnerStatusRPC(t, statuses)
	tableIDs := []string{"devuser1.s3_p1", "devuser1.held", "devuser1.quarantine", "devuser1.gone"}

	rec := &backupTestRecording{}
	got := map[string]payloadexec.TableSchema{}
	deps := backupTestDeps(rec, &backupTestConn{rec: rec}, &backupTestManifests{}, nil,
		func(ctx context.Context, d *objstore.Drill) (objstore.DrillVerdict, error) {
			for _, id := range tableIDs {
				schema, err := d.Schemas.TableSchema(ctx, id)
				if err != nil {
					return objstore.DrillVerdict{}, err
				}
				got[id] = schema
			}
			return drillTestVerdict(true), nil
		})
	var stdout bytes.Buffer
	require.NoError(t, runStorageIntegrityRestoreDrill(t.Context(), restoreDrillTestConfig(),
		StorageIntegrityRestoreDrillOptions{Owner: 1, OwnerRPC: ownerRPC}, &stdout, deps))
	for _, id := range tableIDs {
		want, err := payloadexec.DecodeTableSchemaJSON(id, drillTestSchemaJSON(id))
		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.Equal(t, want, got[id], id)
	}
	require.Equal(t, []string{"devuser1|s3_p1", "devuser1|held", "devuser1|quarantine", "devuser1|gone"}, statuses.asked,
		"one status call per table, with the database and the table as its two parameters")
}

// TestStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillRefusesATableWithoutASchema pins the
// refusal of a status answer without schema_json (Plan S3-C1 contract §18):
// an ordinary or schema-less Pending or Refused table has nothing to gate
// against, and neither has a schema that names another table or a table id
// that is not <database>.<table>.
func TestStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillRefusesATableWithoutASchema(t *testing.T) {
	setBackupTestEnv(t)
	statuses := &fixedOwnerStatuses{statuses: map[string]hgregistry.TableStatus{
		"devuser1.ordinary": {Status: hgregistry.TableStatusOrdinary},
		"devuser1.refused":  {Status: hgregistry.TableStatusRefused, RefusedCode: "column_type", RefusedReason: `column "v" has unsupported type "Decimal(18, 4)"`, RegistryVersion: 41},
		"devuser1.renamed":  {Status: hgregistry.TableStatusActive, SchemaJSON: backupTestSchemaJSON, RegistryVersion: 41},
	}}
	ownerRPC := startOwnerStatusRPC(t, statuses)
	for tableID, want := range map[string]string{
		"devuser1.ordinary": `table devuser1.ordinary has no schema on its owner's host (status "ordinary")`,
		"devuser1.refused":  `table devuser1.refused has no schema on its owner's host (status "refused")`,
		"devuser1.unknown":  `table devuser1.unknown has no schema on its owner's host (status "pending")`,
		"devuser1.renamed":  `table devuser1.renamed: schema_json names table "devuser1.s3_p1"`,
		"no_database":       `table id "no_database" is not <database>.<table>`,
	} {
		rec := &backupTestRecording{}
		deps := backupTestDeps(rec, &backupTestConn{rec: rec}, &backupTestManifests{}, nil,
			func(ctx context.Context, d *objstore.Drill) (objstore.DrillVerdict, error) {
				_, err := d.Schemas.TableSchema(ctx, tableID)
				return objstore.DrillVerdict{}, err
			})
		var stdout bytes.Buffer
		err := runStorageIntegrityRestoreDrill(t.Context(), restoreDrillTestConfig(),
			StorageIntegrityRestoreDrillOptions{Owner: 1, OwnerRPC: ownerRPC}, &stdout, deps)
		require.ErrorContainsf(t, err, want, tableID)
		require.Emptyf(t, stdout.String(), "%s: no verdict without a schema", tableID)
	}

	rec := &backupTestRecording{}
	deps := backupTestDeps(rec, &backupTestConn{rec: rec}, &backupTestManifests{}, nil,
		func(ctx context.Context, d *objstore.Drill) (objstore.DrillVerdict, error) {
			_, err := d.Schemas.TableSchema(ctx, "devuser1.s3_p1")
			return objstore.DrillVerdict{}, err
		})
	unreachable := httptest.NewServer(nil)
	unreachable.Close()
	err := runStorageIntegrityRestoreDrill(t.Context(), restoreDrillTestConfig(),
		StorageIntegrityRestoreDrillOptions{Owner: 1, OwnerRPC: unreachable.URL}, &bytes.Buffer{}, deps)
	require.ErrorContains(t, err, "table devuser1.s3_p1: sentio_getStorageIntegrityTableStatus on "+unreachable.URL+":")
}

// blockingManifests answers no manifest until its context ends, as
// dataplane.Client.WithLeaderRetry does while every arbiter peer is
// unavailable.
type blockingManifests struct{}

func (blockingManifests) Latest(ctx context.Context) (replay.SafeSnapshotManifest, error) {
	<-ctx.Done()
	return replay.SafeSnapshotManifest{}, ctx.Err()
}

func (blockingManifests) Manifest(ctx context.Context, _ string) (replay.SafeSnapshotManifest, error) {
	<-ctx.Done()
	return replay.SafeSnapshotManifest{}, ctx.Err()
}

// answeringManifests answers at once with its manifest and its error.
type answeringManifests struct {
	manifest replay.SafeSnapshotManifest
	err      error
}

func (a answeringManifests) Latest(context.Context) (replay.SafeSnapshotManifest, error) {
	return a.manifest, a.err
}

func (a answeringManifests) Manifest(context.Context, string) (replay.SafeSnapshotManifest, error) {
	return a.manifest, a.err
}

// TestStorageIntegrityArbiterManifestReadsAreBounded pins the deadline of
// every manifest read of backup and restore-drill (Plan S3-C1 Task 25,
// Appendix B): WithLeaderRetry retries an unavailable arbiter until its
// context ends, so without a bound an arbiter outage would hold the Job
// until its activeDeadlineSeconds.
func TestStorageIntegrityArbiterManifestReadsAreBounded(t *testing.T) {
	require.Equal(t, 5*time.Minute, storageIntegrityArbiterReadTimeout)
	snapshotID := "0x" + strings.Repeat("ab", 32)

	blocked := storageIntegrityBoundedManifests{source: blockingManifests{}, timeout: 20 * time.Millisecond}
	_, err := blocked.Latest(t.Context())
	require.ErrorIs(t, err, context.DeadlineExceeded)
	require.EqualError(t, err, "storage integrity arbiter: reading the latest manifest took longer than 20ms: context deadline exceeded")
	_, err = blocked.Manifest(t.Context(), snapshotID)
	require.EqualError(t, err, "storage integrity arbiter: reading manifest "+snapshotID+" took longer than 20ms: context deadline exceeded")

	want := replay.SafeSnapshotManifest{SnapshotID: snapshotID}
	got, err := storageIntegrityBoundedManifests{source: answeringManifests{manifest: want}, timeout: time.Minute}.Manifest(t.Context(), snapshotID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, want, got, "an answer in time passes through unchanged")
	refused := errors.New("objstore: manifest " + snapshotID + " is not its own root 0x00")
	_, err = storageIntegrityBoundedManifests{source: answeringManifests{err: refused}, timeout: time.Minute}.Latest(t.Context())
	require.Same(t, refused, err, "an error in time is not rewrapped")

	// The arbiter client the commands open, against a peer nothing listens on.
	listener, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	addr := listener.Addr().String()
	require.NoError(t, listener.Close())
	manifests, closeManifests, err := openStorageIntegrityArbiterManifests([]dataplane.Peer{{ID: "arb-1", GRPCAddr: addr}})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	t.Cleanup(closeManifests)
	bounded, ok := manifests.(storageIntegrityBoundedManifests)
	require.True(t, ok, "the commands read the arbiter through the bound")
	require.Equal(t, storageIntegrityArbiterReadTimeout, bounded.timeout)
	bounded.timeout = 200 * time.Millisecond
	started := time.Now()
	_, err = bounded.Latest(t.Context())
	require.ErrorContains(t, err, "storage integrity arbiter: reading the latest manifest took longer than 200ms: ")
	require.Less(t, time.Since(started), 10*time.Second, "the bound ends WithLeaderRetry's retries")
}
```

```go
package standalone

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"compute-network-node/config"
	"sentioxyz/sentio-core/common/log"

	"github.com/ClickHouse/clickhouse-go/v2"
	gethrpc "github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/rpc"
	hgregistry "github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/registry"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay"
	"github.com/housegate/housegate/pkg/replay/payloadexec"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane"
	"github.com/sentioxyz/arbiter-core/dataplane/objstore"
)

// ErrStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillFailed is restore-drill's error when the
// verdict it printed is not pass, so the process exits non-zero.
var ErrStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillFailed = errors.New("storage-integrity restore drill: the verdict is not pass")

// StorageIntegrityRestoreDrillOptions are restore-drill's flags.
type StorageIntegrityRestoreDrillOptions struct {
	// Owner is the SI indexer whose backup the drill restores (--owner).
	Owner uint64
	// OwnerRPC is that indexer's storage RPC URL (--owner-rpc), which serves
	// each backed-up table's schema.
	OwnerRPC string
	// Backup names the backup; empty is the owner's latest (--backup).
	Backup string
}

const (
	// storageIntegrityOwnerStatusMethod is the owner host's table status
	// method, params [database, table]
	// (rpc.StorageNodeService.GetStorageIntegrityTableStatus).
	storageIntegrityOwnerStatusMethod = "sentio_getStorageIntegrityTableStatus"
	// storageIntegrityOwnerStatusTimeout bounds one status call.
	storageIntegrityOwnerStatusTimeout = 30 * time.Second
	// storageIntegrityArbiterReadTimeout bounds one manifest read from the
	// arbiter peers. dataplane.Client.WithLeaderRetry retries an unavailable
	// arbiter until its context ends and the commands' context has no
	// deadline, so without it an arbiter outage would hold a backup or a
	// drill until its Job's deadline.
	storageIntegrityArbiterReadTimeout = 5 * time.Minute
)

// storageIntegrityBackupDeps are the seams of backup and restore-drill; tests
// replace them with fakes.
type storageIntegrityBackupDeps struct {
	openClickHouse func(*clickhouse.Options) (clickhouse.Conn, error)
	openManifests  func([]dataplane.Peer) (objstore.ManifestSource, func(), error)
	runBackup      func(context.Context, *objstore.Backuper) (objstore.BackupIndex, error)
	runDrill       func(context.Context, *objstore.Drill) (objstore.DrillVerdict, error)
}

func defaultStorageIntegrityBackupDeps() storageIntegrityBackupDeps {
	return storageIntegrityBackupDeps{
		openClickHouse: clickhouse.Open,
		openManifests:  openStorageIntegrityArbiterManifests,
		runBackup: func(ctx context.Context, b *objstore.Backuper) (objstore.BackupIndex, error) {
			return b.Run(ctx)
		},
		runDrill: func(ctx context.Context, d *objstore.Drill) (objstore.DrillVerdict, error) {
			return d.Run(ctx)
		},
	}
}

// openStorageIntegrityArbiterManifests reads published manifests from the
// arbiter peers through the existing SafeState RPCs, every answer checked by
// objstore's accept rule (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §8.4), each read bounded
// by storageIntegrityArbiterReadTimeout. dataplane.New does not dial.
func openStorageIntegrityArbiterManifests(peers []dataplane.Peer) (objstore.ManifestSource, func(), error) {
	client, err := dataplane.New(dataplane.Config{Peers: peers})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("storage integrity arbiter client: %w", err)
	}
	manifests := storageIntegrityBoundedManifests{
		source:  objstore.NewArbiterManifests(client),
		timeout: storageIntegrityArbiterReadTimeout,
	}
	return manifests, client.Close, nil
}

// storageIntegrityBoundedManifests gives every manifest read of source its
// own deadline.
type storageIntegrityBoundedManifests struct {
	source  objstore.ManifestSource
	timeout time.Duration
}

func (m storageIntegrityBoundedManifests) Latest(ctx context.Context) (replay.SafeSnapshotManifest, error) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, m.timeout)
	defer cancel()
	manifest, err := m.source.Latest(ctx)
	return manifest, m.explain(ctx, "the latest manifest", err)
}

func (m storageIntegrityBoundedManifests) Manifest(ctx context.Context, snapshotID string) (replay.SafeSnapshotManifest, error) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, m.timeout)
	defer cancel()
	manifest, err := m.source.Manifest(ctx, snapshotID)
	return manifest, m.explain(ctx, "manifest "+snapshotID, err)
}

// explain names the bound when a read failed because it ran out of time;
// any other error stays as it is.
func (m storageIntegrityBoundedManifests) explain(ctx context.Context, what string, err error) error {
	if err != nil && errors.Is(ctx.Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded) {
		return fmt.Errorf("storage integrity arbiter: reading %s took longer than %s: %w", what, m.timeout, err)
	}
	return err
}

// RunStorageIntegrityBackup is `sentio-node storage-integrity backup` (Plan
// S3-C1 contract §18): one full or incremental backup of
// storage_integrity.backup.owner_indexer_id's hg_safe to the replica bucket
// (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §16 P1), as objstore.Backuper decides. stdout
// gets exactly one line, the backup's index object as JSON; logs go to
// stderr. The ClickHouse login is storage_integrity.clickhouse_username with
// STORAGE_INTEGRITY_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD, the bucket key comes only from the
// environment, and neither is ever printed.
func RunStorageIntegrityBackup(ctx context.Context, cfg *config.Config, out io.Writer) error {
	return runStorageIntegrityBackup(ctx, cfg, out, defaultStorageIntegrityBackupDeps())
}

func runStorageIntegrityBackup(ctx context.Context, cfg *config.Config, out io.Writer, deps storageIntegrityBackupDeps) error {
	if cfg == nil {
		return errors.New("storage-integrity backup requires a config")
	}
	si := cfg.StorageIntegrity
	if err := si.ValidateBackupJob(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	owner := *si.Backup.OwnerIndexerID
	job, err := openStorageIntegrityBackupJob(si, deps)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer job.close()
	links := si.Backup.MaxChainLinks
	if links == 0 {
		links = uint32(objstore.DefaultMaxChainLinks)
	}
	ctx, logger := log.FromContext(ctx, "component", "storage-integrity-backup")
	logger.Infow("backing up hg_safe to the replica bucket",
		"owner_indexer_id", owner, "bucket", job.bucket.URL(), "clickhouse_dsn", si.ClickhouseDSN,
		"clickhouse_user", si.ClickhouseUsername, "max_chain_links", links)
	index, err := deps.runBackup(ctx, &objstore.Backuper{
		Conn:          job.conn,
		Manifests:     job.manifests,
		Bucket:        job.bucket,
		Owner:         owner,
		NetworkID:     si.SNode.NetworkID,
		Credentials:   job.credentials,
		MaxChainLinks: si.Backup.MaxChainLinks,
	})
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("storage-integrity backup of indexer %d: %w", owner, err)
	}
	logger.Infow("backed up hg_safe",
		"name", index.Name, "kind", index.Kind, "base", index.Base, "chain_length", index.ChainLength,
		"snapshot_id", index.SnapshotID, "tables", len(index.Tables))
	return writeStorageIntegrityJSONLine(out, index)
}

// RunStorageIntegrityRestoreDrill is `sentio-node storage-integrity
// restore-drill` (Plan S3-C1 contract §18, clarification K27): it restores
// every partition the manifest named by opts.Owner's backup index lists into
// hg_rstage scratch tables and gates each against that manifest
// (objstore.Drill). Each table's schema comes from the owner host's status
// RPC at opts.OwnerRPC and is untrusted until objstore checks its hash against
// the manifest. stdout gets exactly one line, the verdict as JSON; logs go to
// stderr. It returns ErrStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillFailed unless the verdict
// passes, and prints nothing on stdout when the drill cannot run.
func RunStorageIntegrityRestoreDrill(ctx context.Context, cfg *config.Config, opts StorageIntegrityRestoreDrillOptions, out io.Writer) error {
	return runStorageIntegrityRestoreDrill(ctx, cfg, opts, out, defaultStorageIntegrityBackupDeps())
}

func runStorageIntegrityRestoreDrill(ctx context.Context, cfg *config.Config, opts StorageIntegrityRestoreDrillOptions, out io.Writer, deps storageIntegrityBackupDeps) error {
	if cfg == nil {
		return errors.New("storage-integrity restore-drill requires a config")
	}
	si := cfg.StorageIntegrity
	if err := si.ValidateRestoreDrill(); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if id := si.Backup.OwnerIndexerID; id != nil && *id != opts.Owner {
		return fmt.Errorf("storage-integrity restore-drill --owner %d is not storage_integrity.backup.owner_indexer_id %d", opts.Owner, *id)
	}
	if opts.OwnerRPC == "" {
		return errors.New("storage-integrity restore-drill requires --owner-rpc: the owner host's storage RPC URL, which serves each table's schema")
	}
	if u, err := url.Parse(opts.OwnerRPC); err != nil || (u.Scheme != "http" && u.Scheme != "https") || u.Host == "" {
		return fmt.Errorf("storage-integrity restore-drill --owner-rpc %q must be an http(s) URL", opts.OwnerRPC)
	}
	scratch, err := objstore.NewScratchNamer(si.Backup.ScratchPrefix)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	job, err := openStorageIntegrityBackupJob(si, deps)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer job.close()
	schemas, err := newStorageIntegrityOwnerSchemas(ctx, opts.OwnerRPC)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer schemas.client.Close()
	ctx, logger := log.FromContext(ctx, "component", "storage-integrity-restore-drill")
	logger.Infow("restoring a backup into hg_rstage and gating it against the manifest its index names",
		"owner_indexer_id", opts.Owner, "backup", opts.Backup, "bucket", job.bucket.URL(),
		"owner_rpc", opts.OwnerRPC, "clickhouse_dsn", si.ClickhouseDSN, "clickhouse_user", si.ClickhouseUsername,
		"scratch_prefix", si.Backup.ScratchPrefix)
	verdict, err := deps.runDrill(ctx, &objstore.Drill{
		Conn:        job.conn,
		Manifests:   job.manifests,
		Schemas:     schemas,
		Bucket:      job.bucket,
		Owner:       opts.Owner,
		NetworkID:   si.SNode.NetworkID,
		Credentials: job.credentials,
		Backup:      opts.Backup,
		Scratch:     scratch,
	})
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("storage-integrity restore drill of indexer %d: %w", opts.Owner, err)
	}
	if err := writeStorageIntegrityJSONLine(out, verdict); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	logger.Infow("restore drill finished",
		"backup", verdict.Backup, "snapshot_id", verdict.SnapshotID, "tables", len(verdict.Tables), "pass", verdict.Pass)
	if !verdict.Pass {
		return ErrStorageIntegrityRestoreDrillFailed
	}
	return nil
}

// storageIntegrityBackupJob holds what backup and restore-drill open: the
// bucket, its key, the ClickHouse connection and the arbiter's manifests.
type storageIntegrityBackupJob struct {
	bucket      objstore.Bucket
	credentials objstore.Credentials
	conn        clickhouse.Conn
	manifests   objstore.ManifestSource
	closers     []func()
}

// openStorageIntegrityBackupJob checks the bucket's form and reads the key
// from the environment before it opens anything; neither clickhouse.Open nor
// dataplane.New dials.
func openStorageIntegrityBackupJob(si config.StorageIntegrityConfig, deps storageIntegrityBackupDeps) (*storageIntegrityBackupJob, error) {
	bucket, err := objstore.ParseBucket(si.Backup.BucketURL)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url: %w", err)
	}
	accessKeyID, secretAccessKey, err := config.StorageIntegrityS3Credentials()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	job := &storageIntegrityBackupJob{
		bucket:      bucket,
		credentials: objstore.Credentials{AccessKeyID: accessKeyID, SecretAccessKey: secretAccessKey},
	}
	job.conn, err = deps.openClickHouse(si.ClickhouseOptions())
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("storage integrity clickhouse: %w", err)
	}
	job.closers = append(job.closers, func() { _ = job.conn.Close() })
	peers := make([]dataplane.Peer, 0, len(si.ArbiterPeers))
	for _, peer := range si.ArbiterPeers {
		peers = append(peers, dataplane.Peer{ID: peer.ID, GRPCAddr: peer.Addr})
	}
	manifests, closeManifests, err := deps.openManifests(peers)
	if err != nil {
		job.close()
		return nil, err
	}
	job.manifests = manifests
	job.closers = append(job.closers, closeManifests)
	return job, nil
}

func (j *storageIntegrityBackupJob) close() {
	for i := len(j.closers) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		j.closers[i]()
	}
}

// storageIntegrityOwnerSchemas is restore-drill's objstore.SchemaSource: the
// owner host's sentio_getStorageIntegrityTableStatus. Any answer that carries
// schema_json is taken (Active, a held Pending table, a quarantined host's
// Refused table, Gone); its schema_hash is not, because objstore recomputes
// the hash and checks it against the manifest.
type storageIntegrityOwnerSchemas struct {
	rpcURL string
	client *gethrpc.Client
}

func newStorageIntegrityOwnerSchemas(ctx context.Context, rpcURL string) (*storageIntegrityOwnerSchemas, error) {
	client, err := gethrpc.DialOptions(ctx, rpcURL, gethrpc.WithHTTPClient(&http.Client{Timeout: storageIntegrityOwnerStatusTimeout}))
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("storage-integrity restore-drill --owner-rpc %s: %w", rpcURL, err)
	}
	return &storageIntegrityOwnerSchemas{rpcURL: rpcURL, client: client}, nil
}

func (s *storageIntegrityOwnerSchemas) TableSchema(ctx context.Context, tableID string) (payloadexec.TableSchema, error) {
	database, table, ok := strings.Cut(tableID, ".")
	if !ok || database == "" || table == "" {
		return payloadexec.TableSchema{}, fmt.Errorf("table id %q is not <database>.<table>", tableID)
	}
	var status hgregistry.TableStatus
	if err := s.client.CallContext(ctx, &status, storageIntegrityOwnerStatusMethod, database, table); err != nil {
		return payloadexec.TableSchema{}, fmt.Errorf("table %s: %s on %s: %w", tableID, storageIntegrityOwnerStatusMethod, s.rpcURL, err)
	}
	if status.SchemaJSON == "" {
		return payloadexec.TableSchema{}, fmt.Errorf("table %s has no schema on its owner's host (status %q)", tableID, status.Status)
	}
	return payloadexec.DecodeTableSchemaJSON(tableID, status.SchemaJSON)
}

// writeStorageIntegrityJSONLine writes v as one line of JSON: the only output
// backup and restore-drill write to stdout.
func writeStorageIntegrityJSONLine(out io.Writer, v any) error {
	line, err := json.Marshal(v)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	_, err = fmt.Fprintf(out, "%s\n", line)
	return err
}
```

```go
// TestStorageIntegrityCommandListsBackupAndRestoreDrill pins Plan S3-C1
// contract §18: `storage-integrity backup` takes no arguments,
// `storage-integrity restore-drill` requires --owner and --owner-rpc and takes
// an optional --backup, and both load the global --config-path as a job
// config (no node block, no PRIVATE_KEY) before they validate it.
func TestStorageIntegrityCommandListsBackupAndRestoreDrill(t *testing.T) {
	// A job config without its bucket: LoadConfig would refuse it for its
	// missing node block first, so the bucket refusal shows the job loader.
	const jobWithoutBucket = `storage_integrity:
  arbiter_peers:
    - {id: arb-1, addr: "127.0.0.1:7080"}
  clickhouse_dsn: 127.0.0.1:9000
  clickhouse_username: si_backup
  snode:
    network_id: devnet2
  backup:
    owner_indexer_id: 1
    scratch_prefix: p1drill_b_
`
	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "job.yaml")
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(path, []byte(jobWithoutBucket), 0o600))
	t.Setenv("PRIVATE_KEY", "")
	run := func(args ...string) error {
		cmd := NewStorageIntegrityCommand(&path)
		cmd.SetArgs(args)
		cmd.SetOut(io.Discard)
		cmd.SetErr(io.Discard)
		return cmd.Execute()
	}

	cmd := NewStorageIntegrityCommand(&path)
	backup, rest, err := cmd.Find([]string{"backup"})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Empty(t, rest)
	require.Equal(t, "backup", backup.Name())
	require.Error(t, backup.Args(backup, []string{"extra"}), "backup takes no positional arguments")
	require.NoError(t, backup.Args(backup, nil))
	require.EqualError(t, run("backup"), "storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url is required")

	drill, rest, err := cmd.Find([]string{"restore-drill"})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Empty(t, rest)
	require.Equal(t, "restore-drill", drill.Name())
	require.Error(t, drill.Args(drill, []string{"extra"}), "restore-drill takes no positional arguments")
	for name, required := range map[string]bool{"owner": true, "owner-rpc": true, "backup": false} {
		flag := drill.Flags().Lookup(name)
		require.NotNilf(t, flag, "--%s", name)
		_, isRequired := flag.Annotations[cobra.BashCompOneRequiredFlag]
		require.Equalf(t, required, isRequired, "--%s required", name)
	}
	require.Equal(t, "uint64", drill.Flags().Lookup("owner").Value.Type(), "--owner is an indexer id")
	require.EqualError(t, run("restore-drill"), `required flag(s) "owner", "owner-rpc" not set`)
	require.EqualError(t, run("restore-drill", "--owner", "1", "--owner-rpc", "http://sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-b:33003"),
		"storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url is required")
	require.ErrorContains(t, run("restore-drill", "--owner", "-1", "--owner-rpc", "http://127.0.0.1:1"), `invalid argument "-1" for "--owner"`)
}
```

```go
// newBackupCommand runs one backup of an SI owner's hg_safe to the replica
// bucket (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §16 P1, Plan S3-C1 contract §18): the
// command the production chart's siBackup CronJob runs.
func newBackupCommand(configPath *string) *cobra.Command {
	return &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "backup",
		Short: "Back up an SI owner's hg_safe to the replica bucket and print the backup's index object",
		Long: "Backs up hg_safe of storage_integrity.backup.owner_indexer_id from storage_integrity.clickhouse_dsn " +
			"to storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url under owner-<id>/: a full backup, or an incremental one on the " +
			"owner's latest backup until its chain holds max_chain_links backups (default 7). The index object names " +
			"the latest manifest the arbiter peers published when the backup started. The config is a job config: no " +
			"node block and no PRIVATE_KEY. The ClickHouse password comes only from STORAGE_INTEGRITY_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD, " +
			"the bucket key only from STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. " +
			"Only the index object's JSON is written to stdout; logs go to stderr.",
		Args: cobra.NoArgs,
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
			ctx := cmd.Context()
			if ctx == nil {
				ctx = context.Background()
			}
			cfg, err := config.LoadStorageIntegrityJobConfig(*configPath)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			return standalone.RunStorageIntegrityBackup(ctx, cfg, cmd.OutOrStdout())
		},
	}
}

// newRestoreDrillCommand restores one owner's backup into hg_rstage scratch
// tables and gates it against the manifest its index object names (Plan S3-C1
// contract §18, clarification K27).
func newRestoreDrillCommand(configPath *string) *cobra.Command {
	var opts standalone.StorageIntegrityRestoreDrillOptions
	cmd := &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "restore-drill",
		Short: "Restore an SI owner's backup into hg_rstage, gate it against the manifest its index names, and print the verdict",
		Long: "Reads the index object of --owner's backup (--backup, else the latest) from storage_integrity.backup.bucket_url, " +
			"fetches the manifest it names from the arbiter peers and accepts it only by the manifest accept rule, takes each " +
			"table's schema from --owner-rpc's sentio_getStorageIntegrityTableStatus and checks its hash against the manifest, " +
			"restores every partition the manifest lists into hg_rstage.<scratch_prefix><n> on storage_integrity.clickhouse_dsn " +
			"and gates it: the manifest's parts are kept once each, the rest dropped, and the kept parts must sum to the " +
			"partition root. The config is a job config: no node block and no PRIVATE_KEY. The ClickHouse password comes only " +
			"from STORAGE_INTEGRITY_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD, the bucket key only from STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID and " +
			"STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. Only the verdict's JSON is written to stdout; logs go to stderr. The " +
			"command exits non-zero unless the verdict passes.",
		Args: cobra.NoArgs,
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
			ctx := cmd.Context()
			if ctx == nil {
				ctx = context.Background()
			}
			cfg, err := config.LoadStorageIntegrityJobConfig(*configPath)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			return standalone.RunStorageIntegrityRestoreDrill(ctx, cfg, opts, cmd.OutOrStdout())
		},
	}
	cmd.Flags().Uint64Var(&opts.Owner, "owner", 0, "the SI indexer id whose backup is restored (its prefix owner-<id>/)")
	cmd.Flags().StringVar(&opts.OwnerRPC, "owner-rpc", "", "the owner host's storage RPC URL, for example http://sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-b:33003")
	cmd.Flags().StringVar(&opts.Backup, "backup", "", "the backup's name (<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ>-<full|incr>); empty restores the owner's latest backup")
	cobra.CheckErr(cmd.MarkFlagRequired("owner"))
	cobra.CheckErr(cmd.MarkFlagRequired("owner-rpc"))
	return cmd
}
```

````markdown
### Storage-integrity backups and restore drills

Every SI owner keeps verified, incremental backups of its `hg_safe` in a versioned object-store bucket (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §16 P1). Two commands do it, and neither runs in a host: both load the global `--config-path` as a job config, which has no `node` block and needs no `PRIVATE_KEY`, and only `storage_integrity.arbiter_peers`, `clickhouse_dsn`, `clickhouse_username`, `snode.network_id` and `backup` are read from it, as in this `job.yaml`:

```yaml
storage_integrity:
  arbiter_peers:
    - {id: arb-1, addr: "127.0.0.1:7080"}
  clickhouse_dsn: "127.0.0.1:9000"  # backup: the owner's SI ClickHouse; restore-drill: a staging installation
  clickhouse_username: si_backup  # required (si_restore for a drill); its password only from STORAGE_INTEGRITY_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD
  snode:
    network_id: local
  backup:
    bucket_url: "https://storage.googleapis.com/example-si-replica"  # http(s)://<host>[:port]/<bucket>, nothing after the bucket
    owner_indexer_id: 1  # backup only: the SI indexer whose hg_safe is copied, under owner-<id>/
    max_chain_links: 7  # the default: one full backup and up to six incremental ones on it
    scratch_prefix: drill_  # restore-drill only: its scratch tables are hg_rstage.<prefix><n>
```

```bash
/sentio-node --config-path job.yaml storage-integrity backup > index.json
/sentio-node --config-path job.yaml storage-integrity restore-drill --owner 1 --owner-rpc http://127.0.0.1:8081 > verdict.json
```

`backup` runs one `BACKUP DATABASE hg_safe` on the owner's ClickHouse to `owner-<id>/<UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ>-<full|incr>/` in the bucket: a full backup when the owner has none or its latest chain already holds `max_chain_links` backups, else an incremental one on the latest. Beside it, it writes the index object `<name>.index.json`, which names the latest manifest the arbiter published when the backup started and lists every backed-up part, and prints that object as one line of JSON on stdout; logs go to stderr. A backup name is never reused, so no backup object is ever overwritten. The production chart runs it as the `siBackup` CronJob of each SI host's release.

`restore-drill` proves a backup: it takes `--owner`'s latest backup (or `--backup <name>`; `--owner-rpc` is that owner host's storage RPC URL), fetches the manifest its index names from the arbiter and accepts it only when its id, its recomputed root, its validation and its ledger check hold, reads each table's schema from the owner host's `sentio_getStorageIntegrityTableStatus` at `--owner-rpc` and checks its hash against the manifest, restores every partition the manifest lists into an `hg_rstage` scratch table on `clickhouse_dsn` and gates it: each part the manifest needs is kept once, every other part of the backup is dropped from the scratch, and the kept parts must sum to the partition root. It prints the verdict as one line of JSON on stdout and exits non-zero unless the verdict passes, which needs at least one verified table and every backed-up table the manifest lists verified. Run it against a staging installation, never against a live SI ClickHouse.

Both commands log in to ClickHouse as `storage_integrity.clickhouse_username` (required: never the passwordless `default`) with the password from `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD`, and take the bucket's HMAC key only from `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`. A config file that sets `storage_integrity.backup.access_key_id` or `secret_access_key` is refused whatever the value. ClickHouse reaches the bucket itself (`S3(...)` in each statement), so the key travels in the query text to that ClickHouse, which shows the secret argument as `[HIDDEN]` in its logs and system tables (arbiter-core's mechanics M14 measures it); the commands never print it. Each manifest read from the arbiter peers gives up after five minutes, so an arbiter outage fails a command instead of holding it until its Job's deadline.
````

Notes:
- **Inert on merge, and no restart when used.** The bucket and its accounts exist only once the user applies the Terraform (Task 28 §2); no key, key file or Secret is a Terraform resource. `siBackup` is a top-level block of `charts/sentio-node`, so the host's `checksum/config` (which hashes `node.config`, `housegate`, `storageIntegrity` and `housegateSidecar`) never sees it; `test_backup_job_never_changes_the_host_pod` renders all seven `charts/sentio-node` releases with the job on and off and requires every other document byte-identical (a release without storage integrity refuses the job). `si_backup` is a users block change, which the operator applies as a users.d reload; `test_si_backup_user_holds_exactly_its_grants` requires that adding it changes the installation's users and nothing else. The backup alerts render only with a listed CronJob. Step 18's `render-inertness.sh` proves all eight releases render byte-identically to the branch base.
- **Operator inputs are `__TOKEN__`s filled from recorded values (S3-B D19-5's pattern).** `INDEXER_C_ID`, `P1_BACKUP_DELETE` and the backup image are written as `__INDEXER_C_ID__`, `__P1_BACKUP_DELETE__`, `__SN_COMMIT_P1__`, `__SN_DIGEST_P1__` (with `__HG_TAG_P1__` and `__CORE_TAG_P1__` in one comment), and the P1 staging hashes as `__SHA256_P1S_<USER>__`; the local fill tool of Step 2 replaces them right after each step that writes them, from `$P/ledger.env` (the ledger values of Step 1) and the user's staging hashes file, and refuses a missing or malformed value. Every test that reads such a file fails on a token left in it, and Step 18 greps the tree for any.
- **The Terraform follows contract §18 exactly.** No IAM Condition of a bucket binding can scope a list to a prefix: GCS checks `storage.objects.list` on the bucket, and Cloud Storage's API attributes (the list prefix among them) are supported only in Credential Access Boundaries, never in a role binding (K25). So each writer prefix is a managed folder (`google_storage_managed_folder`, `force_destroy = false`; GCS also refuses to delete a managed folder that holds objects), and the writer role is granted, without a condition, on that folder only (`google_storage_managed_folder_iam_member`, the provider's documented form `bucket = <folder>.bucket`, `managed_folder = <folder>.name`); no writer has a binding on the bucket but the lock remover. The lock remover's condition uses `resource.name` only (the prefix and the `/.lock` suffix), which bucket bindings support. The lock remover's two resources are always in the file and gated by `count` and `for_each` on `local.si_v2_backup_delete_right`, so the same file serves both outcomes of M13 and the test checks the gate, not a branch. A `precondition` on the bucket refuses any other value at plan time. The map entries are separated by comments so `terraform fmt` aligns nothing and the filled file is formatted whatever `INDEXER_C_ID`'s width. The expressions were evaluated offline (`terraform plan` of the locals and the gated maps, no provider): four writers, four readers, the lock-remover map empty for `none` and equal to the writers for `lock`.
- **The grant probe rows, measured.** On `clickhouse/clickhouse-server:26.3` (26.3.51.7) the contract's literal rows `BACKUP TABLE hg_safe.<t> TO S3('http://127.0.0.1:1/probe/', 'k', 's')` and `SELECT * FROM s3('http://127.0.0.1:1/probe.json', 'k', 's', 'RawBLOB')` do not answer: `backup_restore_s3_retry_attempts` defaults to 1000 and `s3_retry_attempts` to 500, so each retried a refused connection for more than five minutes; an `INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3(…) VALUES …` is an asynchronous insert (`async_insert` is 1 by default) whose flush retries the same way. The rows therefore end in `SETTINGS backup_restore_s3_retry_attempts = 0` (BACKUP), `SETTINGS s3_retry_attempts = 0` (`s3()` reads) and `SETTINGS async_insert = 0, s3_retry_attempts = 0` before `VALUES` (`s3()` writes); each then answers at once, 499 after a passed access check and 497 before it (recorded in Appendix B as a measured difference from the contract's row text). Also measured: BACKUP checks `BACKUP` on what it backs up before it opens the destination (`si_restore` and a `BACKUP` of `hg_unsafe` by `si_backup` get 497), but no S3 source grant at query time (a user with `BACKUP ON hg_safe.*` and no S3 grant got as far as the connection); `READ ON S3` and `WRITE ON S3` are what the index object's `s3()` read and `INSERT INTO FUNCTION s3` need, so the probe exercises them there, and M13 (Task 24) measures the full BACKUP and RESTORE with real keys. RESTORE checks its access only after it has read the backup's metadata (a user without `CREATE TABLE` on `hg_rstage` got 499, not 497), so no row probes it. `si_backup`'s `CREATE TABLE` in `hg_rstage` answers 497 before the database exists. The whole corpus (143 rows) was run in file order as every role with users made from `SI_PROBE_GRANTS`: 0 mismatches.
- **`si_restore` and the views.** D36's refusals hold as rows: `CREATE DICTIONARY`, `SYSTEM STOP MERGES` and a `CREATE VIEW … DEFINER = default SQL SECURITY DEFINER` in `hg_rstage` answer 497 (the last needs `SET DEFINER`); a plain `CREATE VIEW` there is allowed by ClickHouse's implicit grant with `CREATE TABLE` (measured; `role_atoms` models it), which contract §18 records as not a refusal.
- **The rollout order is enforced.** `test_si_backup_user_follows_the_rollout` and `test_devnet2_backup_jobs_follow_the_rollout` refuse a host's job before its installation has `si_backup`; `test_devnet2_monitoring_follows_the_rollout` refuses a listed CronJob before its job is enabled; every by-role comparison of a CHI manifest renders the network chart with that manifest's own `si_backup` state, so indexer-b's user may come before the network's (decision D10's pattern). Checked by replaying Task 28's commits on a filled copy: indexer-b's user, indexer-c's, the network's, the jobs b, c, a, then the monitoring list, the whole suite passing after each; enabling indexer-b's job first fails with `sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-b backs up as si_backup before storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b has the user`, and listing the CronJobs first fails with `sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a-si-backup is alerted on before its job is enabled`. The S3-B test `test_si_clients_take_clickhouse_passwords_only_from_secrets` keeps the job's password environment apart from the host's (the replay found that an enabled job overwrote the host's entry).
- **The CronJob.** `timeZone: Etc/UTC` makes K26's UTC schedules independent of the controller's zone; `automountServiceAccountToken: false` (the job calls no Kubernetes API); the host's `nodeSelector` and `imagePullSecrets`; pod labels `app.kubernetes.io/{name,instance,component}` = `<fullname>-si-backup`, the release, `si-backup`, which no Service of the chart selects; no `checksum/config` annotation (a CronJob pod reads its ConfigMap at start). The guards run only when `siBackup.enabled`, so the devnet2 overlays (off) are validated by `test_devnet2_backup_jobs_follow_the_rollout`, which renders each with the job turned on. Helm gives `-f` numbers as `float64` and `--set` numbers as `int64`, and the chart default `ownerIndexerID: null` as no value, so the integer guards accept both kinds and owner 0 (measured with `kindOf`).
- **The backup alerts.** `StorageIntegrityBackupStale` fires for a listed CronJob whose last success (`kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time`) is older than `maxAgeSeconds`, for one that never succeeded since its creation (`kube_cronjob_created`) that long ago, and for a listed CronJob that is gone (`absent(kube_cronjob_created{…})` per name); `StorageIntegrityBackupFailed` fires for a failed Job (`kube_job_status_failed > 0`) owned by a listed CronJob (`kube_job_owner{owner_kind="CronJob", owner_name=~…}`), until the Job is removed (the failed history keeps three; runbook §15.2). Both select `namespace` and the listed names, never `job`, and keep `cluster` in every `by`. `MONITORING_ALERTS["backups"]` is a `frozenset` like every other group of Plan S3-B's constant (the contract's parenthesis lists the two names); the test compares sets.
- **Plan S3-B tests extended in place** (beyond the contract's four), each keeping every assertion it had: `test_indexer_b_source_clickhouse_carries_the_network_source_profile`, `test_indexer_c_source_clickhouse_carries_the_network_source_profile_and_a_member_disk` and `test_devnet2_clickhouse_logins_follow_the_rollout` (a manifest's or the overlay's own `si_backup` state), `test_si_clients_take_clickhouse_passwords_only_from_secrets` (the job's password environment), `test_legacy_profile_keeps_its_clickhouse_users` (`backupUser` is refused on the legacy profile), `test_logins_script_writes_only_hashes_and_never_prints_a_password` (through `PLANS["p1-staging"]`), `test_default_renders_no_monitoring`, `test_every_rule_reads_only_this_networks_series`, `test_monitoring_settings_fail_closed` and `test_devnet2_monitoring_follows_the_rollout` (the backups group); `MonitoringTest.MONITORED` lists two probe CronJobs, so every monitoring test renders the group.
- **Contract text adjusted (Appendix B).** The CI paths already hold `scripts/storage-integrity/**` since Plan S3-B Task 16, so Step 18 adds the other three paths only; `make-si-backup-keys.sh` passes `--project=sentio-352722` to `gcloud storage hmac create`, so the key belongs to the bucket's project whatever the user's gcloud default; the probe rows' `SETTINGS` (above); the drill's `hg_rstage` table in the corpus is `hg_rstage.si_grant_probe_restore (v Int64)`, the corpus's own naming, for the contract's `hg_rstage.probe (a UInt8)`.

- [ ] **Step 2: The fill tool (local only, never committed)**

```bash
P="$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p1-prep"
cat > "$P/fill-p1.py" <<'PY'
"""Fill Plan S3-C1 Task 26's recorded inputs into its files, in place.

usage: python3 -I fill-p1.py <ledger.env> [--staging-hashes <hashes-p1-staging.yaml>] <file>...

ledger.env holds the NAME=value lines that s3-ledger.py get printed in Task 26
Step 1 (INDEXER_C_ID, E_END, SN_COMMIT_P1, SN_DIGEST_P1, HG_TAG_P1, CORE_TAG_P1
and P1_BACKUP_DELETE). With --staging-hashes, the passwordSha256 map that
scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh p1-staging wrote fills the
P1 staging installation's __SHA256_P1S_<USER>__ tokens. Every file must
exist. A token of this task without a value, or a value that is not well
formed, is refused, and then nothing is written.
"""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

USAGE = "usage: fill-p1.py <ledger.env> [--staging-hashes <hashes-p1-staging.yaml>] <file>..."
USERS = ("default", "si_snode", "si_gateway", "si_reader", "si_backup", "si_restore")
TOKEN = re.compile(r"__(?:SN_COMMIT_P1|SN_DIGEST_P1|HG_TAG_P1|CORE_TAG_P1|INDEXER_C_ID|P1_BACKUP_DELETE|SHA256_P1S_[A-Z_]+)__")
PATTERNS = {
    "INDEXER_C_ID": r"0|[1-9][0-9]*",
    "SN_COMMIT_P1": r"[0-9a-f]{40}",
    "SN_DIGEST_P1": r"sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}",
    "HG_TAG_P1": r"v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+",
    "CORE_TAG_P1": r"v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+",
    "P1_BACKUP_DELETE": r"none|lock",
}

arguments = sys.argv[1:]
if len(arguments) < 2:
    sys.exit(USAGE)
ledger_path, arguments = arguments[0], arguments[1:]
hashes_path = None
if arguments[:1] == ["--staging-hashes"]:
    if len(arguments) < 3:
        sys.exit(USAGE)
    hashes_path, arguments = arguments[1], arguments[2:]

ledger = {}
for line in Path(ledger_path).read_text().splitlines():
    if line.strip():
        name, _, value = line.partition("=")
        ledger[name.strip()] = value.strip()
for name, pattern in PATTERNS.items():
    if not re.fullmatch(pattern, ledger.get(name, "")):
        sys.exit(f"{ledger_path}: {name} must match {pattern} (s3-ledger.py get), got {ledger.get(name)!r}")
if ledger["INDEXER_C_ID"] in ("0", "1"):
    sys.exit(f"{ledger_path}: INDEXER_C_ID is {ledger['INDEXER_C_ID']}, the id of indexer-a or indexer-b")
tokens = {f"__{name}__": ledger[name] for name in PATTERNS}

if hashes_path is not None:
    # BaseLoader keeps every scalar a string: a hash of digits only stays a hash.
    hashes = (yaml.load(Path(hashes_path).read_text(), Loader=yaml.BaseLoader) or {}).get("passwordSha256")
    if not isinstance(hashes, dict) or sorted(hashes) != sorted(USERS):
        sys.exit(f"{hashes_path}: passwordSha256 must name exactly {', '.join(USERS)}")
    for user, digest in hashes.items():
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", str(digest)):
            sys.exit(f"{hashes_path}: passwordSha256.{user} must be 64 lowercase hex characters")
    if len(set(hashes.values())) != len(hashes):
        sys.exit(f"{hashes_path}: two users share a password hash")
    tokens.update({f"__SHA256_P1S_{user.upper()}__": hashes[user] for user in USERS})

filled = {}
for name in arguments:
    text = Path(name).read_text()
    for token, value in tokens.items():
        text = text.replace(token, value)
    left = sorted(set(TOKEN.findall(text)))
    if left:
        sys.exit(f"{name}: no value for {left}; nothing was written")
    filled[name] = text
for name, text in filled.items():
    Path(name).write_text(text)
    print(f"filled {name}")
PY
chmod 600 "$P/fill-p1.py"
python3 -I "$P/fill-p1.py" 2>&1 || true
printf '%s\n' __INDEXER_C_ID__ __P1_BACKUP_DELETE__ __SN_COMMIT_P1__ > "$P/fill-smoke.txt"
python3 -I "$P/fill-p1.py" "$P/ledger.env" "$P/fill-smoke.txt" && cat "$P/fill-smoke.txt" && rm "$P/fill-smoke.txt"
printf '%s\n' __SHA256_P1S_DEFAULT__ > "$P/fill-smoke.txt"
python3 -I "$P/fill-p1.py" "$P/ledger.env" "$P/fill-smoke.txt"; cat "$P/fill-smoke.txt"; rm "$P/fill-smoke.txt"
```

Expected: the usage line `usage: fill-p1.py <ledger.env> [--staging-hashes <hashes-p1-staging.yaml>] <file>...`; `filled …/fill-smoke.txt` and the three recorded values, one per line: `<INDEXER_C_ID>`, `none` or `lock`, and `<SN_COMMIT_P1>` (40 hex); then `…/fill-smoke.txt: no value for ['__SHA256_P1S_DEFAULT__']; nothing was written` and the unchanged `__SHA256_P1S_DEFAULT__` (a staging token needs `--staging-hashes`). A refusal naming `ledger.env` means Step 1's values are missing or malformed: stop. Remove `$P` at the end of Task 27 (it holds no secret).

```diff
+def terraform_blocks(text):
+    """The top-level blocks of a Terraform file by kind and labels, e.g.
+    ("locals",) or ("resource", <type>, <name>), each with its body."""
+    blocks = {}
+    for match in re.finditer(r'^(resource|data|locals|output|variable|module)((?: "[^"]+")*) \{$', text, re.M):
+        depth = 0
+        for end in range(match.end() - 1, len(text)):
+            if text[end] == "{":
+                depth += 1
+            elif text[end] == "}":
+                depth -= 1
+                if depth == 0:
+                    break
+        key = (match.group(1), *re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', match.group(2)))
+        if key in blocks:
+            raise AssertionError(f"{key} is declared twice")
+        blocks[key] = text[match.end():end]
+    return blocks
+
+
+def terraform_attribute(body, name):
+    """Every expression assigned to name in a block body (nested blocks included), in order."""
+    return [value.strip() for value in re.findall(rf"^\s*{re.escape(name)}\s*=\s*(.+)$", body, re.M)]
+
```
