```hcl
# devnet2-si-v2 replica bucket: verified object-store backups of each SI
# owner's hg_safe (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §16 P1; Plan S3-C1 contract §18;
# docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p1-backups.md §2). ClickHouse writes
# and reads it itself, with BACKUP ... TO S3(...), RESTORE ... FROM S3(...)
# and s3(), through the bucket's S3-compatible XML API and the HMAC keys of
# the service accounts below. The keys are made in the operator's own terminal
# by scripts/storage-integrity/make-si-backup-keys.sh and live only in
# Kubernetes Secrets, so no HMAC key, key file or Secret is a resource here
# (the Terraform Cloud state would hold it).
#
# A backup writer creates, reads and lists objects under its own prefix only,
# through the managed folder of that prefix, and can never delete or overwrite
# one (an overwrite needs storage.objects.delete, which the writer role lacks;
# a backup name is never reused). A restore reader reads the whole bucket.
# Every object version is kept and the bucket is never destroyed by Terraform;
# removing an old backup chain is an administrator's decision.
locals {
  si_v2_replica_bucket = "sentio-352722-si-devnet2-si-v2-replica"

  # One backup writer per SI owner, keyed by the owner's contract-assigned SI
  # indexer id, which names its prefix owner-<id>/ and which no signer change
  # alters (Plan S3-C1 K26), and the P1 runbook's mechanics writer.
  si_v2_backup_writers = {
    # indexer-a, the founding SI indexer
    "0" = "owner-0/"
    # indexer-b
    "1" = "owner-1/"
    # indexer-c (INDEXER_C_ID, Plan S3-B Appendix C)
    "__INDEXER_C_ID__" = "owner-__INDEXER_C_ID__/"
    # the GCS mechanics of the P1 runbook (§5)
    "mech" = "mechanics/"
  }

  # Read-only restore service accounts: one per member host of stage 3 P2
  # (indexer-a, -b, -c) and one for the P1 restore drills.
  si_v2_restore_readers = ["a", "b", "c", "drill"]

  # P1_BACKUP_DELETE of Plan S3-C1 (K24): the delete right a ClickHouse BACKUP
  # needs, as mechanics M13 measured it. "none": no backup key may delete
  # anything. "lock": each writer may also delete the .lock file of a backup
  # under its own prefix (spec §16 P1 as the user amended it), nothing else.
  si_v2_backup_delete_right = "__P1_BACKUP_DELETE__"
}

resource "google_storage_bucket" "storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_replica" {
  name                        = "sentio-352722-si-devnet2-si-v2-replica"
  location                    = var.region
  uniform_bucket_level_access = true
  public_access_prevention    = "enforced"
  force_destroy               = false

  versioning {
    enabled = true
  }

  # ClickHouse uploads large backup files in parts. An upload that a failed
  # backup leaves unfinished is aborted after 7 days; aborting deletes no object.
  lifecycle_rule {
    condition {
      age = 7
    }
    action {
      type = "AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload"
    }
  }

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true

    precondition {
      condition     = contains(["none", "lock"], local.si_v2_backup_delete_right)
      error_message = "si_v2_backup_delete_right must be P1_BACKUP_DELETE of Plan S3-C1: none or lock."
    }
  }
}

resource "google_project_iam_custom_role" "storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_backup_writer" {
  role_id     = "siDevnet2SiV2BackupWriter"
  title       = "Storage Integrity devnet2-si-v2 backup writer"
  description = "Create, read and list backup objects and their multipart uploads, without delete permission"
  permissions = [
    "storage.objects.create",
    "storage.objects.get",
    "storage.objects.list",
    "storage.multipartUploads.create",
    "storage.multipartUploads.abort",
    "storage.multipartUploads.list",
    "storage.multipartUploads.listParts",
  ]
}

resource "google_service_account" "storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_backup" {
  for_each     = local.si_v2_backup_writers
  account_id   = "si-devnet2-si-v2-backup-${each.key}"
  display_name = "Storage Integrity devnet2-si-v2 backup writer ${each.value}"
}

# One managed folder per writer prefix (Plan S3-C1 K25). GCS checks a list on
# the bucket, and an IAM Condition of a bucket binding may test only the
# resource name, the resource type and the time: Cloud Storage's API
# attributes, the list prefix among them, work only in Credential Access
# Boundaries. A role granted on a managed folder covers every object whose name
# starts with the folder's name and a list whose prefix lies in the folder, so
# the folder is what confines a writer's list. GCS refuses to delete a managed
# folder that holds objects, and Terraform does not force it.
resource "google_storage_managed_folder" "storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_backup" {
  for_each      = local.si_v2_backup_writers
  bucket        = google_storage_bucket.storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_replica.name
  name          = each.value
  force_destroy = false
}

# The writer role on the writer's own managed folder only, without a
# condition: it creates, reads and lists objects under that prefix, and no
# writer holds anything on the bucket itself (the lock remover below aside).
# The P1 runbook (§5) proves on GCS that each key lists its own prefix and is
# refused a list or read of another one.
resource "google_storage_managed_folder_iam_member" "storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_backup_writer" {
  for_each       = local.si_v2_backup_writers
  bucket         = google_storage_managed_folder.storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_backup[each.key].bucket
  managed_folder = google_storage_managed_folder.storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_backup[each.key].name
  role           = google_project_iam_custom_role.storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_backup_writer.name
  member         = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_backup[each.key].email}"
}

# Only when P1_BACKUP_DELETE is lock (K24, after the user's amendment of spec
# §16 P1): the delete of a .lock file under the writer's own prefix, and of
# nothing else. Its condition tests the object's resource name only, which a
# bucket binding supports.
resource "google_project_iam_custom_role" "storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_backup_lock_remover" {
  count       = local.si_v2_backup_delete_right == "lock" ? 1 : 0
  role_id     = "siDevnet2SiV2BackupLockRemover"
  title       = "Storage Integrity devnet2-si-v2 backup lock remover"
  description = "Delete the .lock file a ClickHouse BACKUP leaves under its own prefix"
  permissions = [
    "storage.objects.delete",
  ]
}

resource "google_storage_bucket_iam_member" "storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_backup_lock_remover" {
  for_each = local.si_v2_backup_delete_right == "lock" ? local.si_v2_backup_writers : {}
  bucket   = google_storage_bucket.storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_replica.name
  role     = google_project_iam_custom_role.storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_backup_lock_remover[0].name
  member   = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_backup[each.key].email}"

  condition {
    title       = "si-v2-backup-${each.key}-lock"
    description = "The .lock files under ${each.value} only"
    expression  = "resource.name.startsWith(\"projects/_/buckets/${local.si_v2_replica_bucket}/objects/${each.value}\") && resource.name.endsWith(\"/.lock\")"
  }
}

resource "google_service_account" "storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_restore" {
  for_each     = toset(local.si_v2_restore_readers)
  account_id   = "si-devnet2-si-v2-restore-${each.key}"
  display_name = "Storage Integrity devnet2-si-v2 restore reader ${each.key}"
}

# Read-only on the whole bucket: get and list, never create or delete.
resource "google_storage_bucket_iam_member" "storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_restore_viewer" {
  for_each = toset(local.si_v2_restore_readers)
  bucket   = google_storage_bucket.storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_replica.name
  role     = "roles/storage.objectViewer"
  member   = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_restore[each.key].email}"
}
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Creates the HMAC key of one service account of devnet2-si-v2's replica bucket
# (stage 3 P1 of housegate spec 2026-10-14 §16;
# docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p1-backups.md §3), after
# terraform/storage_integrity_devnet2_si_v2_replica.tf is applied. Run it in your
# own terminal (from fish too):
#
#   bash scripts/storage-integrity/make-si-backup-keys.sh <account>
#
# <account> is backup-<owner id> (backup-0, backup-1 and indexer-c's
# backup-<INDEXER_C_ID>), backup-mech, restore-a, restore-b, restore-c or
# restore-drill: the service account
# si-devnet2-si-v2-<account>@sentio-352722.iam.gserviceaccount.com. It creates
# one HMAC key with gcloud storage hmac create, stores its access id and secret
# only in the Kubernetes Secret storage-integrity-si-v2-<account> (keys
# access-id and secret; context sentio-sea, namespace sentio-network-devnet2),
# and writes the access id, which is not a secret, to
# $HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p1-logins/hmac-<account>.access-id for its rotation.
# That directory must exist (mode 700). It never prints the secret and never
# passes it on a command line; the secret exists only in a mode-700 temporary
# directory that it removes on exit. It refuses to overwrite an existing Secret
# or access-id file: a key is replaced by a new key and a new Secret, never in
# place (runbook §15.3).
set -euo pipefail
umask 077

readonly project=sentio-352722
readonly context=sentio-sea
readonly namespace=sentio-network-devnet2

usage() {
  echo "usage: bash scripts/storage-integrity/make-si-backup-keys.sh backup-<owner id>|backup-mech|restore-a|restore-b|restore-c|restore-drill" >&2
  exit 2
}

[ "$#" -eq 1 ] || usage
account=$1
# Service account ids have at most 30 characters and si-devnet2-si-v2-backup- has
# 24, so an owner id has at most 6 digits.
[[ "$account" =~ ^(backup-(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,5})|backup-mech|restore-(a|b|c|drill))$ ]] || usage

readonly service_account="si-devnet2-si-v2-$account@$project.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
readonly secret_name="storage-integrity-si-v2-$account"
readonly logins_dir="$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p1-logins"
readonly id_file="$logins_dir/hmac-$account.access-id"

kube() {
  kubectl --context "$context" --namespace "$namespace" "$@"
}

for tool in gcloud kubectl python3; do
  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || { echo "make-si-backup-keys: $tool is required" >&2; exit 1; }
done
[ -d "$logins_dir" ] || { echo "make-si-backup-keys: $logins_dir does not exist; create it with mode 700 first" >&2; exit 1; }
if [ -e "$id_file" ]; then
  echo "make-si-backup-keys: $id_file exists; refusing to overwrite it (nothing was created)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
found=$(kube get secret "$secret_name" --ignore-not-found -o name)
if [ -n "$found" ]; then
  echo "make-si-backup-keys: Secret $secret_name exists in $namespace; refusing to overwrite it (nothing was created)" >&2
  exit 1
fi

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
chmod 700 "$tmp"
created=""
stored=""
cleanup() {
  status=$?
  rm -rf "$tmp"
  if [ "$status" -ne 0 ] && [ -n "$created" ] && [ -z "$stored" ]; then
    echo "make-si-backup-keys: failed after gcloud created an HMAC key of $service_account that no Secret holds; its secret is lost" >&2
    echo "make-si-backup-keys: find it with gcloud storage hmac list --service-account=$service_account --project=$project, deactivate it with gcloud storage hmac update <access id> --deactivate --project=$project, remove it with gcloud storage hmac delete <access id> --project=$project, and run the script again" >&2
  fi
  exit "$status"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT
trap 'exit 143' TERM

# The key, secret included, goes only into the temporary directory.
created=yes
gcloud storage hmac create "$service_account" --project="$project" --format=json > "$tmp/key.json"
python3 -I - "$tmp" "$service_account" <<'PY'
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

directory, account = Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2]
key = json.loads((directory / "key.json").read_text())
metadata = key.get("metadata") or {}
access_id, secret = str(metadata.get("accessId", "")), str(key.get("secret", ""))
if metadata.get("serviceAccountEmail") != account or metadata.get("state") != "ACTIVE":
    sys.exit(f"make-si-backup-keys: gcloud did not answer an active key of {account}")
```

```bash
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

directory = Path(sys.argv[1])
if (directory.stat().st_mode & 0o777) != 0o700:
    sys.exit(f"{directory} must have mode 700")
wanted = {"hashes-p1-staging.yaml": ["default", "si_backup", "si_gateway", "si_reader", "si_restore", "si_snode"]}
wanted.update({f"hashes-si_backup-{name}.yaml": ["si_backup"] for name in ("indexer-b", "indexer-c", "network")})
seen = []
for name, users in wanted.items():
    # BaseLoader keeps every scalar a string: a hash of digits only stays a hash.
    data = yaml.load((directory / name).read_text(), Loader=yaml.BaseLoader)
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or sorted(data) != ["passwordSha256"] or sorted(data["passwordSha256"]) != users:
        sys.exit(f"{name}: must hold passwordSha256 with exactly {users}")
    for user, value in data["passwordSha256"].items():
        if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", value):
            sys.exit(f"{name}: {user} is not 64 lowercase hex characters")
        seen.append(value)
if len(set(seen)) != len(seen):
    sys.exit("two logins share a password hash")
taken = "\n".join(path.read_text() for path in sorted(Path("k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2").rglob("*.yaml")))
if any(value in taken for value in seen):
    sys.exit("a P1 hash appears in a devnet2 file already: one password per user and installation")
print(f"hashes ok: {len(seen)} distinct, in {len(wanted)} files")

for secret in storage-integrity-si-v2-p1-staging-logins storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-backup-indexer-b storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-backup-indexer-c storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-backup-network; do
  printf '%s:' "$secret"
  kubectl --context sentio-sea -n sentio-network-devnet2 get secret "$secret" -o go-template='{{range $key, $value := .data}} {{$key}}{{end}}'
  echo
done
```

Create `docs/examples/storage-integrity-p1-staging-chi.yaml` (indexer-b's installation as Step 1 found it, renamed, under its own Keeper root, with 2Gi volumes and the P1 staging users; the six hashes are tokens that the fill tool replaces from the user's staging hashes file):

```yaml
# The P1 staging installation of stage 3 P1 (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §16;
# docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p1-backups.md): §4 applies it with
# kubectl under its own Keeper root and §13 deletes it with its PVCs. It is
# indexer-b's source installation (storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-b-source.yaml
# in k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2) renamed, with 2Gi volumes, so the
# devnet2-operator that reconciles every SI installation reconciles exactly
# its shape here. It is born locked (posture C): default with its own password
# and loopback only, indexer-b's user set, si_backup, and si_restore, the
# restore drill's login, which no other installation has (Plan S3-C1 contract
# §18). Its literal hashes are those scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh
# p1-staging wrote; the passwords live only in the Secret
# storage-integrity-si-v2-p1-staging-logins.
#
# The runbook runs on it what must never touch an owner's ClickHouse: the grant
# probe of every role (charts/storage-integrity/tests/clickhouse_grant_probe.tsv),
# the mechanics on GCS with the deployed image (§5, every key-bearing statement
# piped from a Secret into the pod), and one restore drill per owner into
# hg_rstage (§10). test_render.py keeps it equal to indexer-b's installation. No
# client of devnet2-si-v2 ever connects to it.
apiVersion: clickhouse.altinity.com/v1
kind: ClickHouseInstallation
metadata:
  name: storage-integrity-si-v2-p1-staging
  namespace: sentio-network-devnet2
spec:
  defaults:
    templates:
      podTemplate: clickhouse
      dataVolumeClaimTemplate: data-volume-claim
      logVolumeClaimTemplate: log-volume-claim
      clusterServiceTemplate: cluster-service
      replicaServiceTemplate: replica-service
    storageManagement:
      reclaimPolicy: Retain
  configuration:
    zookeeper:
      nodes:
        - host: clickhouse-keeper-extra-0.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local
          port: 2181
        - host: clickhouse-keeper-extra-1.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local
          port: 2181
        - host: clickhouse-keeper-extra-2.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local
          port: 2181

      operation_timeout_ms: 10000

    files:

          <background_fetches_pool_size>8</background_fetches_pool_size>
        </clickhouse>
      users.d/zz-si-default-loopback.xml: |
        <clickhouse><users><default><networks replace="replace"><ip>::1</ip><ip>127.0.0.1</ip></networks><access_management>0</access_management></default></users></clickhouse>
    # Born locked (posture C): default accepts loopback connections only, has
    # its own password and no access management (the users.d file above), and
    # is the runbook's administrator through kubectl exec. indexer-b's protocol
    # users keep exactly their grants (test_render.py SI_CLICKHOUSE_GRANTS), so
    # the grant probe runs them as on an owner; si_backup holds SI_BACKUP_GRANTS
    # and si_restore SI_RESTORE_GRANTS (hg_rstage: explicit rights, never ALL;
    # spec §8.2 as amended).

      - ::1
      si_snode/password_sha256_hex: "__SHA256_P1S_SI_SNODE__"
      si_snode/networks/ip:
      - ::/0
      si_snode/profile: default
      si_snode/grants/query:
      - GRANT CREATE DATABASE ON hg_unsafe.*
      - GRANT CREATE DATABASE ON hg_safe.*
      - GRANT CREATE DATABASE ON hg_promote.*
      - GRANT SELECT, INSERT, ALTER DELETE, CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE ON hg_unsafe.*
      - GRANT SELECT, INSERT, ALTER DELETE, CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE ON hg_safe.*
      - GRANT SELECT, INSERT, ALTER DELETE, CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE ON hg_promote.*
      - GRANT SYSTEM MERGES ON hg_unsafe.*
      - GRANT SYSTEM MERGES ON hg_safe.*
      - GRANT SYSTEM DROP REPLICA ON *.*
      - GRANT SELECT ON system.parts
      - GRANT SELECT ON system.detached_tables
      - GRANT SELECT ON system.replicas
      - GRANT SELECT ON system.zookeeper
      - GRANT SELECT ON system.merges
      si_gateway/password_sha256_hex: "__SHA256_P1S_SI_GATEWAY__"
      si_gateway/networks/ip:
      - ::/0
      si_gateway/profile: default
      si_gateway/grants/query:
      - GRANT SELECT, INSERT, ALTER, CREATE TABLE, CREATE VIEW, DROP TABLE, DROP VIEW, TRUNCATE, OPTIMIZE ON devnet2.*
      - GRANT CREATE DATABASE ON devnet2.*
      - GRANT SELECT ON hg_safe.*
      - GRANT SELECT ON hg_unsafe.*
      - GRANT READ ON REMOTE
      - GRANT CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ON *.*
      - GRANT SELECT ON system.processes
      si_reader/password_sha256_hex: "__SHA256_P1S_SI_READER__"
      si_reader/networks/ip:
      - ::/0
      si_reader/profile: default
      si_reader/grants/query:
      - GRANT SELECT ON hg_safe.*
      - GRANT SELECT ON hg_unsafe.*
      - GRANT SELECT(database, table, name, active, rows, partition_id, hash_of_all_files) ON system.parts
      si_backup/password_sha256_hex: "__SHA256_P1S_SI_BACKUP__"
      si_backup/networks/ip:
      - ::/0
      si_backup/profile: default
      si_backup/grants/query:
      - GRANT BACKUP ON hg_safe.*
      - GRANT READ, WRITE ON S3
      - GRANT CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ON *.*
      - GRANT SELECT ON system.parts
      - GRANT SELECT ON system.tables
      - GRANT SELECT ON system.backups
      si_restore/password_sha256_hex: "__SHA256_P1S_SI_RESTORE__"
      si_restore/networks/ip:
      - ::/0
      si_restore/profile: default
      si_restore/grants/query:
      - GRANT CREATE DATABASE ON hg_rstage.*
      - GRANT SELECT, INSERT, ALTER, CREATE TABLE, DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE, OPTIMIZE ON hg_rstage.*
      - GRANT READ ON S3
      - GRANT CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ON *.*
      - GRANT SELECT ON system.parts
      - GRANT SELECT ON system.tables
      - GRANT SELECT ON system.backups
    profiles:

      default/enable_json_type: "1"

    serviceTemplates:

          type: ClusterIP
```

```diff
+def sentio_node_release_documents(stdout):
+    """{(kind, name): exact text} of every document of a helm template output."""
+    found = {}
+    for chunk in re.split(r"^---\n", stdout, flags=re.M):
+        item = yaml.safe_load(chunk)
+        if item:
+            found[(item["kind"], item["metadata"]["name"])] = chunk
+    return found
+
+
+def render_sentio_node_release(name, namespace, values):
+    """helm template of one charts/sentio-node release from its statically merged values."""
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
+        path = Path(directory) / "values.yaml"
+        path.write_text(yaml.safe_dump(values))
+        return subprocess.run(
+            ["helm", "template", name, str(SENTIO_NODE_CHART), "--namespace", namespace, "-f", str(path)],
+            capture_output=True, text=True, check=False,
+        )

+    def test_backup_job_needs_a_reviewed_image(self):
+        # sentio-node has no storage-integrity backup before the P1 build: a values
+        # file may set siBackup only with an image of STAGE3_BACKUP_IMAGES, enabled
+        # or not. That build runs only in the backup and drill jobs, never as a
+        # host (Plan S3-C1 contract §16).
+        for image in STAGE3_BACKUP_IMAGES:
+            self.assertRegex(image, r"^ghcr\.io/sentioxyz/sentio-node:sha-[0-9a-f]{40}@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$")
+            self.assertNotIn(image, STAGE3_HOST_IMAGES)
+            self.assertNotIn(image, WRITER_AUTHORIZATION_IMAGES)
+        with_backup = []
+        referenced = set()
+        for helmfile in sentio_node_helmfiles():
+            for release in yaml.safe_load(helmfile.read_text())["releases"]:
+                if (helmfile.parent / release["chart"]).resolve() != SENTIO_NODE_CHART:
+                    continue
+                label = f"{helmfile.relative_to(ROOT)}:{release['name']}"
+                values, files = release_chart_values(helmfile, release, label)
+                referenced.update(files)
+                image = values["node"]["image"]
+                self.assertNotIn(f'{image["repository"]}:{image["tag"]}', STAGE3_BACKUP_IMAGES, f"{label}: a host runs the backup build")
+                sets = [entry for entry in release.get("values", []) if isinstance(entry, dict) and "siBackup" in entry]
+                sets += [path for path in files if "siBackup" in (yaml.safe_load(path.read_text()) or {})]
+                if sets:
+                    with_backup.append(label)
+                    self.assertIn(values["siBackup"]["image"], STAGE3_BACKUP_IMAGES, f"{label}: siBackup needs a reviewed backup image")
+        # Every SI host states its backup job from the P1 PR on (runbook §8 only enables it).
+        for name in DEVNET2_SI_RELEASES:
+            self.assertIn(f"{FRESH_HELMFILE.relative_to(ROOT)}:{name}", with_backup)
+        # No file outside those releases may set the key: dead configuration a
+        # later release could pick up unreviewed.
+        tracked = subprocess.run(
+            ["git", "-C", str(ROOT), "ls-files", "k8s-*"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
+        ).stdout.split()
+        for name in tracked:
+            path = ROOT / name
+            if path.suffix in (".yaml", ".yml") and path not in referenced and path.is_file():
+                self.assertNotIn("siBackup", path.read_text(errors="ignore"), f"{name} is not part of any sentio-node release")
+
+    def test_devnet2_backup_jobs_follow_the_rollout(self):
+        # Runbook §8 enables each host's job in a single-service commit that also
+        # flips DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP: indexer-b, indexer-c, then indexer-a, each only
+        # once its installation has si_backup (§6). Every overlay states the whole
+        # job from the PR on, so the commit changes enabled only.
+        self.require_every_si_host()
+        self.assertEqual(tuple(DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP), DEVNET2_SI_RELEASES)
+        self.assertEqual(tuple(DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP_SCHEDULES), DEVNET2_SI_RELEASES)
+        self.assertEqual(len(set(DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP_SCHEDULES.values())), len(DEVNET2_SI_RELEASES))
+        for name, docs in self.si_hosts.items():
+            with self.subTest(release=name):
+                release = self.releases[(LEGACY_NAMESPACE, name)]
+                overlay = yaml.safe_load((FRESH_HELMFILE.parent / release["values"][3]).read_text())
+                owner = DEVNET2_BACKUP_OWNERS[name]
+                chi, installation = DEVNET2_HOST_INSTALLATION[name]
+                self.assertEqual(overlay["siBackup"], {
+                    "enabled": DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP[name],
+                    "image": DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP_IMAGE,
+                    "schedule": DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP_SCHEDULES[name],
+                    "ownerIndexerID": owner,
+                    "bucketURL": f"https://storage.googleapis.com/{SI_BACKUP_BUCKET}",
+                    "clickhousePasswordSecret": {"name": f"storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-backup-{installation}"},
+                    "keySecret": {"name": f"storage-integrity-si-v2-backup-{owner}"},
+                })
+                cronjob = ("CronJob", f"{name}-si-backup")
+                self.assertIs(cronjob in docs, DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP[name])
+                if DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP[name]:
+                    self.assertTrue(DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP_USER[chi], f"{name} backs up as si_backup before {chi} has the user")
+                # Enabled, the overlay renders a job that backs up this host's own
+                # source ClickHouse, as si_backup, for this owner.
+                on = docs if DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP[name] else documents(self.render_with(release, {"siBackup": {"enabled": True}}))
+                config = yaml.safe_load(on[("ConfigMap", f"{name}-si-backup")]["data"]["config.yaml"])["storage_integrity"]
+                host = host_config(on)["storage_integrity"]

+                )
+                self.assertEqual(config["clickhouse_username"], "si_backup")
+                self.assertEqual(config["backup"], {

+                self.assertEqual(on[cronjob]["spec"]["schedule"], DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP_SCHEDULES[name])
+                (container,) = on[cronjob]["spec"]["jobTemplate"]["spec"]["template"]["spec"]["containers"]
+                self.assertEqual(container["image"], DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP_IMAGE)
+                if not DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP[name]:

+                    self.assertEqual({key for key in on if key not in docs}, {cronjob, ("ConfigMap", f"{name}-si-backup")})
+                    self.assertEqual({key: on[key] for key in docs}, docs)
```

```yaml
{{- /*
The daily backup of this SI host's hg_safe (stage 3 P1 of housegate spec
2026-10-14 §16; docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p1-backups.md §8): a
CronJob running sentio-node storage-integrity backup, which logs in to this
host's own source ClickHouse as siBackup.clickhouseUsername and lets ClickHouse
write BACKUP DATABASE hg_safe TO S3(...) under the owner's prefix of the
replica bucket, then its index object. Its config names no secret: the
ClickHouse password and the HMAC key reach the container only as three Secret
environment variables.

siBackup is a top-level block, never under storageIntegrity, housegate or
housegateSidecar, so the host's checksum/config never sees it: turning the job
on or off, or changing it, restarts no host pod. Its pods carry
app.kubernetes.io/component si-backup, so no Service of this chart selects
them. Nothing here renders unless siBackup.enabled.
*/ -}}
{{- if .Values.siBackup.enabled }}
{{- $backup := .Values.siBackup -}}
{{- $fullname := include "sentio-node.fullname" . -}}
{{- if not .Values.storageIntegrity.enabled -}}
{{- fail "siBackup.enabled requires storageIntegrity.enabled: the backup job reads the SI arbiter peers and the source ClickHouse" -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- if not (regexMatch "^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._/-]*[a-z0-9])?(:[0-9]+/[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._/-]*[a-z0-9])?)?:[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,127}@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$" (toString $backup.image)) -}}
{{- fail "siBackup.image must be a pinned image (<repository>:<tag>@sha256:<64 hex>)" -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- $owner := $backup.ownerIndexerID -}}
{{- if kindIs "invalid" $owner -}}
{{- fail "siBackup.ownerIndexerID is required" -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- if not (and (or (kindIs "float64" $owner) (kindIs "int64" $owner) (kindIs "int" $owner)) (ge (float64 $owner) 0.0) (eq (float64 $owner) (float64 (int64 $owner)))) -}}
{{- fail "siBackup.ownerIndexerID must be the owner's SI indexer id: a whole number of at least 0" -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- if not (regexMatch "^https://storage\\.googleapis\\.com/[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{1,61}[a-z0-9]$" (toString $backup.bucketURL)) -}}
{{- fail "siBackup.bucketURL must be https://storage.googleapis.com/<bucket>" -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- if not (and (kindIs "string" $backup.schedule) $backup.schedule) -}}
{{- fail "siBackup.schedule is required" -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- $links := $backup.maxChainLinks -}}
{{- if not (and (or (kindIs "float64" $links) (kindIs "int64" $links) (kindIs "int" $links)) (ge (float64 $links) 1.0) (le (float64 $links) 30.0) (eq (float64 $links) (float64 (int64 $links)))) -}}
{{- fail "siBackup.maxChainLinks must be between 1 and 30" -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- if not (and (kindIs "string" $backup.clickhouseUsername) (regexMatch "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$" $backup.clickhouseUsername)) -}}
{{- fail "siBackup.clickhouseUsername must be one ClickHouse user name ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)" -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- if empty $backup.clickhousePasswordSecret.name -}}
{{- fail "siBackup.clickhousePasswordSecret.name is required" -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- if empty $backup.clickhousePasswordSecret.key -}}
{{- fail "siBackup.clickhousePasswordSecret.key is required" -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- if empty $backup.keySecret.name -}}
{{- fail "siBackup.keySecret.name is required" -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- if or (empty $backup.keySecret.accessKeyIDKey) (empty $backup.keySecret.secretAccessKeyKey) -}}
{{- fail "siBackup.keySecret.accessKeyIDKey and secretAccessKeyKey are required" -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- $deadline := $backup.activeDeadlineSeconds -}}
{{- if not (and (or (kindIs "float64" $deadline) (kindIs "int64" $deadline) (kindIs "int" $deadline)) (ge (float64 $deadline) 1.0) (eq (float64 $deadline) (float64 (int64 $deadline)))) -}}
{{- fail "siBackup.activeDeadlineSeconds must be a whole number of seconds of at least 1" -}}
{{- end }}
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: {{ $fullname }}-si-backup
  labels:
    {{- include "sentio-node.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/component: si-backup
data:
  # sentio-node storage-integrity backup's job config: no node block, no
  # password and no key (sentio-node refuses a key or password in the file).
  config.yaml: |
    storage_integrity:
      arbiter_peers:
        {{- range .Values.storageIntegrity.arbiterPeers }}
        - id: {{ .id | quote }}
          addr: {{ .addr | quote }}
        {{- end }}
      clickhouse_dsn: {{ .Values.storageIntegrity.clickhouseDSN | quote }}
      clickhouse_username: {{ $backup.clickhouseUsername | quote }}
      snode:
        network_id: {{ .Values.storageIntegrity.snode.networkID | quote }}
      backup:
        bucket_url: {{ $backup.bucketURL | quote }}
        owner_indexer_id: {{ int64 $owner }}
        max_chain_links: {{ int64 $links }}
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: {{ $fullname }}-si-backup
  labels:
    {{- include "sentio-node.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/component: si-backup
spec:
  schedule: {{ $backup.schedule | quote }}
  timeZone: Etc/UTC
  # One backup at a time: the next name chains on the last finished one.
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 3600
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  jobTemplate:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ $fullname }}-si-backup
        app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
        app.kubernetes.io/component: si-backup
    spec:
      # A failed backup is never retried in place: the next run takes a new name.
      backoffLimit: 0
      activeDeadlineSeconds: {{ int64 $deadline }}
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app.kubernetes.io/name: {{ $fullname }}-si-backup
            app.kubernetes.io/instance: {{ .Release.Name }}
            app.kubernetes.io/component: si-backup
        spec:
          restartPolicy: Never
          automountServiceAccountToken: false
          {{- with .Values.imagePullSecrets }}
          imagePullSecrets:
            {{- toYaml . | nindent 12 }}
          {{- end }}
          {{- with .Values.nodeSelector }}
          nodeSelector:
            {{- toYaml . | nindent 12 }}
          {{- end }}
          containers:
            - name: si-backup
              image: {{ $backup.image | quote }}
              imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
              command: ["/sentio-node", "storage-integrity", "backup", "--config-path", "/etc/si-backup/config.yaml"]
              env:
                - name: STORAGE_INTEGRITY_CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD
                  valueFrom:
                    secretKeyRef:
                      name: {{ $backup.clickhousePasswordSecret.name | quote }}
                      key: {{ $backup.clickhousePasswordSecret.key | quote }}
                - name: STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID
                  valueFrom:
                    secretKeyRef:
                      name: {{ $backup.keySecret.name | quote }}
                      key: {{ $backup.keySecret.accessKeyIDKey | quote }}
                - name: STORAGE_INTEGRITY_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
                  valueFrom:
                    secretKeyRef:
                      name: {{ $backup.keySecret.name | quote }}
                      key: {{ $backup.keySecret.secretAccessKeyKey | quote }}
              volumeMounts:
                - name: config
                  mountPath: /etc/si-backup
                  readOnly: true
              {{- with $backup.resources }}
              resources:
                {{- toYaml . | nindent 16 }}
              {{- end }}
          volumes:
            - name: config
              configMap:
                name: {{ $fullname }}-si-backup
{{- end }}
```

```diff
+# -- Stage 3 P1 (housegate spec 2026-10-14 §16;
+# docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p1-backups.md §8): a CronJob that backs
+# up this SI host's hg_safe to its owner's prefix owner-<ownerIndexerID>/ of the
+# replica bucket, with sentio-node storage-integrity backup (templates/si-backup.yaml).
+# ClickHouse itself writes the backup (BACKUP DATABASE hg_safe TO S3(...)) as
+# clickhouseUsername, a full backup and then incremental ones on it, at most
+# maxChainLinks per chain. The job needs storageIntegrity.enabled (it reads
+# storageIntegrity.arbiterPeers, clickhouseDSN and snode.networkID) and takes
+# its ClickHouse password and its HMAC key from Secrets only. A top-level
+# block, outside the host's checksum/config: turning it on or off, or changing
+# it, restarts no host pod.
+siBackup:
+  enabled: false
+  # A pinned sentio-node build with storage-integrity backup:
+  # <repository>:<tag>@sha256:<64 hex>.
+  image: ""
+  # Cron, in UTC.
+  schedule: "17 3 * * *"
+  # The owner's contract-assigned SI indexer id (0 is a valid id).
+  ownerIndexerID: null
+  # https://storage.googleapis.com/<bucket>
+  bucketURL: ""
+  # Backups per chain: one full backup and at most maxChainLinks - 1
+  # incremental ones on it (1-30).
+  maxChainLinks: 7
+  # The installation-wide backup user of the host's source ClickHouse.
+  clickhouseUsername: si_backup
+  # The Secret holding that user's password (make-clickhouse-logins.sh --add-user).
+  clickhousePasswordSecret:
+    name: ""
+    key: password
+  # The Secret holding the owner's HMAC key (make-si-backup-keys.sh backup-<owner id>).
+  keySecret:
+    name: ""
+    accessKeyIDKey: access-id
+    secretAccessKeyKey: secret
+  # A backup that runs longer than this is stopped and fails.
+  activeDeadlineSeconds: 3600
+  resources: {}
```

```diff
+              max by (cluster, namespace, cronjob) (kube_cronjob_status_last_successful_time{namespace="{{ $namespace }}", cronjob=~"{{ $cronJobs }}"}))
+            {{- range $backups }}
+            or absent(kube_cronjob_created{namespace="{{ $namespace }}", cronjob="{{ . }}"})
+            {{- end }}
+          for: 30m
+          labels:
+            severity: critical
+            network: {{ $network | quote }}
+          annotations:
+            summary: "An SI owner has no successful hg_safe backup within monitoring.backups.maxAgeSeconds, or its listed backup CronJob is gone"
+            runbook_url: "{{ $backupRunbook }}#152-a-failed-or-stale-backup"
+        - alert: StorageIntegrityBackupFailed
+          expr: |-
+            (max by (cluster, namespace, job_name) (kube_job_status_failed{namespace="{{ $namespace }}"}) > 0)
+            and on (cluster, namespace, job_name)
+            max by (cluster, namespace, job_name) (kube_job_owner{namespace="{{ $namespace }}", owner_kind="CronJob", owner_name=~"{{ $cronJobs }}"})
+          for: 5m
+          labels:
+            severity: warning
+            network: {{ $network | quote }}
+          annotations:
+            summary: "A backup Job of a listed SI backup CronJob failed; only the next scheduled run tries again, under a new name"
+            runbook_url: "{{ $backupRunbook }}#152-a-failed-or-stale-backup"
+    {{- end }}
 {{- end }}
```

Notes (drafting decisions, Appendix B):
- **Sections, helpers and evidence are the contract's.** The headings are contract §18's list, the §0 helpers and evidence files contract §19's, each spelled as there; §5's four parts (backups and restore, versions, keys, masking) are run-in labels, not headings, because the contract lists no subsection of §5. §1, §2 and §3 hold no confirmed block (§2 and §3 are the user's fish blocks; their checks are read-only), which Task 28 relies on.
- **Every live change is a commit helper and an apply helper.** `si_p1_user_commit`, `si_p1_job_commit` and `si_p1_monitoring_commit` edit with `si_p1_py` (text insertions verified by a YAML round trip: exactly the intended keys change), run the render tests and commit locally; `si_p1_user_apply`, `si_p1_job_apply` and `si_p1_monitoring_apply` check HEAD (`si_head_is`) and the render (`si_render_diff`: exactly `changed ClickHouseInstallation/storage-integrity-si-v2`, `added ConfigMap/<cj>` and `added CronJob/<cj>`, or `changed VMRule/storage-integrity-si-v2`), push, apply or sync, and compare every pod with the §1.3 baseline. A helper replaces a block written out three times, so each owner's subsection is three short blocks; the conventions check treats each mutating helper as a write.
- **`si_s3_sql` completes and masks inside the pod (K23).** Default's password, the access id and the secret arrive as three stdin lines; awk replaces the placeholders from the environment (no regex, so `/`, `+`, `&` and `\` in a secret are literal) and pipes the SQL into `clickhouse-client --multiquery`; a second awk replaces the secret with `[HIDDEN]` in every output line, because `clickhouse-client` echoes a failing statement verbatim (measured on 26.3.51.7: `(query: … 'SECRETFAKE2' …)`), while the server logs and system tables show `[HIDDEN]` (measured); the client's exit status comes back as a trailer line. It runs only on the P1 staging installation and needs `awk` in that pod (checked in §4).
- **S3 retries are off for the probe and the staging queries.** Measured on 26.3.51.7: a `BACKUP` to `http://127.0.0.1:1/` was still retrying after ten minutes (`backup_restore_s3_retry_attempts` 1000, up to 5 s apart) and an `s3()` read after 60 s (`s3_retry_attempts` 500); with both at 0 they answer at once with 499, which the grant probe counts as `ok`. `si_s3_sql` keeps 10 retries for GCS.
- **ClickHouse removes each backup's `.lock`.** Measured on 26.3.51.7 against an S3 endpoint that models this plan's GCS rules (a writer without delete, an overwrite needing delete): `BACKUP … TO S3` heads `.backup` and `.lock`, puts `.lock`, writes the files and `.backup`, then deletes `.lock`; without a delete right it fails at that last step (`Access denied … while removing object with path …/.lock`) after writing everything, and its cleanup is refused too. Mechanics M13 decides `P1_BACKUP_DELETE`; on that image it would be `lock`. The runbook works for both: §2 adds the lock remover only for `lock`, and §5 measures the right on GCS from the full backup's status, the `.lock`'s live and noncurrent versions (`gcloud storage ls` and `ls -a` on the versioned bucket) and the mechanics key's bindings.
- **Every refusal row has a positive control.** A broken or wrong key answers 403 everywhere, so §5 reads a missing object in each owner key's own prefix (`missing`, 404) next to the refused read of another prefix (`denied`, 403), and lists the own prefix (`ok`); measured against the model endpoint. Writes are tried only where a wrong grant would land under `mechanics/`.
- **The mechanics table pins merges off.** `RESTORE` recreates a table with the backup's settings, and measured on 26.3.51.7 a restored copy without the pin merged its three parts within seconds; `hg_safe.p1_mech` therefore carries `max_bytes_to_merge_at_max_space_in_pool = 0`, as `ddl.SafeSettings` pins every `hg_safe` table, so the drill's scratch tables keep their parts the same way.
- **`system.grants` is compared row by row.** Measured on 26.3.51.7: `SI_BACKUP_GRANTS` expands to 7 rows (`GRANT READ, WRITE ON S3` is two, `access_object` `S3`) and `SI_RESTORE_GRANTS` to 13 (`ON hg_rstage.*` one row per right); `si_p1_py grants-check` holds those rows.
- **The backup checks are relative to the latest index before each run.** `si_backup_run` records it (`backup-<x>-<n>.prev`), so a scheduled run that comes between §8 and §9 makes the next link instead of failing a check; the sync of §8 and every manual run refuse to start from 90 minutes before to 70 minutes after the owner's schedule, so the first run is the manual one in practice.
- **The drill is the CronJob's sibling.** `si_drill` derives its config from the owner's deployed CronJob config (arbiter peers, network id, bucket) with only the staging address, `si_restore` and the scratch prefix changed, and its pod spec from the CronJob's (pull secrets, node selector, resources); the verdict line is taken from `kubectl logs` by its `format`, since the logs interleave sentio-node's stdout and stderr.
- **The drill restores the backup this runbook made and checked (review fix).** `si_drill` passes `--backup <name>` (Task 25's optional flag) with the name of the owner's newest `backup-<x>-<n>.json`, and refuses unless `si_p1_backup_check` wrote its check: the owner's CronJob runs every day, so a drill that took "the latest backup" in a later window would restore a scheduled backup that no check of §8 or §9 read, and `si_p1_drill_check` (which compares the verdict with that file) would stop a healthy run.
- **The registry comparison reads the hosts, not the voters.** The P0 runbook's partstates tool would have to be copied into the voters again (a write in §1) and reads P0's evidence names; `si_p1_active` instead lists each `hg_safe` table of the owner's source ClickHouse with the host's `sentio_getStorageIntegrityTableStatus`, which the host derives from the registry it follows, and §10 requires the verified tables to be exactly the `active` ones and the owner's known table among them.
- **No secret reaches a disk or argv.** `si_secret_hits` and `si_p1_hits_all` read secrets through file descriptors (fixed descriptors 3 to 10, so bash 3.2 runs them too); a Job's log is saved only when it holds none; the masking samples stay in a shell variable.

````markdown
# Storage integrity devnet2: stage-3 P1, verified object-store backups

This runbook gives each SI owner of devnet2-si-v2 (indexer-a, indexer-b, indexer-c) verified, incremental backups of its `hg_safe` in the versioned GCS bucket `sentio-352722-si-devnet2-si-v2-replica`, written by ClickHouse `BACKUP DATABASE hg_safe TO S3(...)` as the installation-wide user `si_backup` with an HMAC key that is confined to the owner's prefix `owner-<indexer id>/` (a managed folder of the bucket, the only GCS IAM scope that confines a list) and cannot delete, and proves every owner's latest backup with a restore drill on a throwaway staging installation that gates each restored partition against the published manifest the backup's index object names. Design: housegate `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-multi-source-si-stage3-database-groups-design.md` §16 row P1 and its exit criterion, §8.4 to §8.6, §13.1 and §14, as clarified by Plan S3-C1 (housegate `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-15-multi-source-si-s3c1-p1-backups.md`, clarifications K23 to K28, on top of Plans S3-A and S3-B). It continues [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md) (every SI ClickHouse locked) and [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-indexer-c.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-indexer-c.md) (indexer-c enrolled), both done. P1 pauses no track: nothing here restarts an SI ClickHouse, a host pod, a verifier or a voter, and nothing changes consensus state except the drill table and its two INSERTs.

| Stage | Change | Way back |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | PR: the replica bucket and its service accounts in Terraform, the `si_backup` user (chart value, grant-probe rows), the P1 staging installation file with the staging-only `si_restore`, the `siBackup` CronJob of `charts/sentio-node` (off on every host), the backup alerts (off), the key and login scripts, render tests, this runbook; inert until applied, synced or turned on | Revert the PR |
| 1 | The bucket and the service accounts, the user's Terraform apply (§2) | The bucket stays (`prevent_destroy`); service accounts only through a reviewed Terraform change |
| 2 | Eight HMAC keys and their Secrets, the user's terminal (§3) | Deactivate the keys and delete the Secrets (§15.3) |
| 3 | The P1 staging installation, born locked, and its grant probe (§4) | Staging cleanup (§13) |
| 4 | Mechanics on GCS with the deployed ClickHouse image: objects under `mechanics/` (§5) | None: no key deletes an object |
| 5 | `si_backup` on indexer-b's, indexer-c's, then the network installation (§6) | Revert (§14) |
| 6 | The drill table `devuser1.s3_p1`, rows `5101` to `5104` (§7) | None: on chain for good |
| 7 | The backup CronJobs of indexer-b, indexer-c and indexer-a, each with a first, full backup run by hand (§8) | Revert (§14); the objects stay |
| 8 | A second, incremental backup per owner (§9) | The objects stay |
| 9 | One restore drill per owner (§10) | None needed |
| 10 | The backup alerts (§11) | Revert (§14) |
| 11 | End record (§12); staging cleanup (§13) | None needed |

Every command block is bash, except the user's own fish blocks of §2, §3 and §15.3. Run the bash blocks from the root of a production checkout at `origin/main` (the live worktree, held at a detached, freshly fetched `origin/main`), in order, in one dedicated `bash` session started with `set -eo pipefail` (from fish, run `bash` first), each block from a file of its own after §0 is defined. Every value a later block needs is written under `$si_backup`, so a block also runs in a new session once §0 is defined. Never run two stages in one window, never change more than one installation or one host per window, and from §6 to §12 change `storage-integrity-si-v2`, the three host releases and the three SI ClickHouse installations only through this runbook.

Every block that pushes to production `main`, syncs a release, applies, creates or deletes a resource, writes Keeper, runs DDL or writes data, writes to the bucket or runs a Job needs explicit user confirmation in chat before it runs; each such block is preceded by the line `Confirm before running.`. Never re-run a confirmed block only to see its output: its read-only checks are in separate blocks, or `tee` their output into `$si_backup`; read that file instead. Objects written to the bucket (§5, §8, §9) and the drill table's writes (§7) are irreversible, and each of those blocks says so.

Keys and passwords (K23, Plan S3-B K16): only the user's terminal creates them (`scripts/storage-integrity/make-si-backup-keys.sh` for the HMAC keys, `scripts/storage-integrity/make-clickhouse-logins.sh` for the ClickHouse logins, both before or during this runbook as §1.2 and §3 say); git and the CHIs carry only SHA-256 hashes, and each plaintext lives only in its Kubernetes Secret. This runbook never prints, echoes, logs or passes a key or a password on argv, and never copies one into `$si_backup`. The flows that touch one are a Secret read piped straight into `kubectl exec -i` stdin (`si_ch_admin`, `si_p1s_as`, `si_p1_backup_login`, `si_s3_sql`), the key-bearing SQL that `si_s3_sql` completes inside the P1 staging pod from that stdin, and `si_secret_hits`, which reads a secret through a file descriptor only to count the lines of a log that contain it. A ClickHouse server shows the secret argument of `S3(...)` and `s3(...)` as `[HIDDEN]` in its logs and system tables (mechanics M14, re-proven on GCS in §5), but `clickhouse-client` echoes a failing statement verbatim, so `si_s3_sql` masks the secret in every line before it leaves the pod. No live owner ClickHouse ever receives a key from this runbook: only the backup CronJobs send their own key, in their own query text, to their own owner's ClickHouse. Never paste a key or a password into chat.

Writes in this runbook: the bucket's objects under `mechanics/<stamp>-*` (§5), `owner-<id>/<name>/` and `owner-<id>/<name>.index.json` (§8, §9), never deleted or overwritten by any key here; the P1 staging installation's tables (`hg_safe.p1_mech`, `hg_safe.p1_mech_bulk`, `hg_rstage.p1mech_restore`, the grant probe's objects and the drill scratch tables `hg_rstage.p1drill_<x>_<n>`), gone with it in §13; the `devuser1` owner's drill table `devuser1.s3_p1` (two partitions) with rows `5101` to `5104` in two INSERTs, through its own local agent in the user's terminal (§7), kept for stage 3 P2; and the single-service commits of §6, §8 and §11. These values are disjoint from every earlier runbook's: the stage-3 P0 runbook's `3001` to `3004`, the lockdown runbook's `4101` to `4104`, the indexer-c runbook's `3101` and `3102` and its `s3e_e2e` rows `1` to `3`. P1 writes nothing into `devnet101.swap_new2`.

## 0. Session helpers

Define the helpers of §0 of [storage-integrity-devnet2-dynamic-table-set.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-dynamic-table-set.md), [storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source.md), [storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source-tracks.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-multi-source-tracks.md), [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p0.md), [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-lockdown.md) and [storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-indexer-c.md](storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-indexer-c.md), unchanged and in that order (each runbook's first bash block of §0, extracted by parsing fences), then these. They replace `si_backup`, so every earlier runbook's evidence stays where it is (the lockdown runbook's lock records stay in `$si_lockdown_dir`, which `si_ch_admin` reads; the P0 runbook's partstates tool stays in `$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p0`). From the earlier runbooks this runbook uses, among others, `si_kubectl`, `si_arbiter`, `si_show`, `si_leader`, `si_images`, `si_tracks`, `si_track`, `si_wait_track`, `si_status` and `si_info` (both take `c` since the indexer-c runbook), `si_agent_start`, `si_agent_stop`, `si_agent_ch`, `si_vm_query`, `si_vmalert_groups`, `si_head_is`, `si_revert_stage3`, `si_ch_admin`, `si_ch_pod`, `si_installation`, `si_inpod_client`, `si_keeper`, `si_stamp`, `si_chi_state`, `si_wait_chi`, `si_runtime_uids`, `si_secret_keys`, `si_render_diff` and `si_source_ch` (`a`, `b` or `c`, as `default` over loopback with the installation's admin password).

The helpers below fall into five groups. Names and identities: `si_p1_pin` reads `$si_backup/pins` (§1.1), `si_p1_image` prints the backup and drill image, and `si_p1_owner`, `si_p1_installation`, `si_p1_chi`, `si_p1_rpc_url`, `si_p1_cronjob` and `si_p1_account` map an owner (`a`, `b`, `c`) or a key account to its names. The P1 staging installation: `si_p1s_as` and `si_p1s_ch` run one query as one of its users over loopback, with S3 retries off so that a probe of an unreachable endpoint answers at once (ClickHouse 26.3 retries such a `BACKUP` up to 1000 times and an `s3()` read up to 500 times by default; measured: both still running after ten minutes), and `si_p1s_grant_probe` runs the committed grant-probe corpus there as the lockdown runbook's `si_grant_probe` runs it, skipping the `si_verifier` rows (that role has no login there; the lockdown runbook's staging probe ran them). The bucket: `si_s3_sql` runs a SQL file as `default` on the P1 staging installation only, after the pod has replaced `@@S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID@@` and `@@S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY@@` with the key the account's Secret holds (awk, from the environment; never argv), and masks that secret in every output line; `si_p1_sql`, `si_p1_status`, `si_p1_probe` and `si_s3_outcome` build on it, `si_index` and `si_indexes` read index objects with the read-only `restore-drill` key, and `si_secret_hits` and `si_p1_hits_all` count lines that hold a secret. Changes: each live change is a pair, a local commit (`si_p1_user_commit`, `si_p1_job_commit`, `si_p1_monitoring_commit`, which edit through `si_p1_py`, run the render tests and commit) and a mutating apply (`si_p1_user_apply`, `si_p1_job_apply`, `si_p1_monitoring_apply`, which check HEAD and the render, push, apply or sync, and prove that nothing restarted with `si_p1_pods_check` against the §1.3 baseline); `si_backup_run`, `si_drill`, the `si_p1_mech_*` helpers of §5 and `si_p1_revert_chi` are mutating too and run only in confirmed blocks. Checks: `si_host_pods`, `si_p1_wait_backup_user`, `si_p1_grants`, `si_p1_backup_login`, `si_p1_backup_check`, `si_p1_active`, `si_p1_drill_check`, `si_p1_budget_left` and the local `si_p1_py`.

```bash
si_backup="$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p1"
si_p1_logins_dir="$HOME/si-devnet2-stage3-p1-logins"
si_p1_bucket=sentio-352722-si-devnet2-si-v2-replica
si_p1_bucket_url="https://storage.googleapis.com/$si_p1_bucket"
si_p1s_chi=storage-integrity-si-v2-p1-staging
si_p1s_pod=storage-integrity-si-v2-p1-staging-source-0-0-0
si_p1s_logins=storage-integrity-si-v2-p1-staging-logins
si_p1_trailer='Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>'
si_p1_pin() { # $1 HG_TAG_P1|CORE_TAG_P1|SN_COMMIT_P1|SN_DIGEST_P1|P1_BACKUP_DELETE|INDEXER_C_ID: that line of $si_backup/pins (§1.1)
  local n v
  case "$1" in
    HG_TAG_P1) n=1 ;; CORE_TAG_P1) n=2 ;; SN_COMMIT_P1) n=3 ;; SN_DIGEST_P1) n=4 ;; P1_BACKUP_DELETE) n=5 ;; INDEXER_C_ID) n=6 ;;
    *) echo "si_p1_pin: unknown pin $1" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
  v="$(sed -n "${n}p" "$si_backup/pins" 2>/dev/null)"
  [ -n "$v" ] || { echo "si_p1_pin: $1 is not in $si_backup/pins: run §1.1 first" >&2; return 1; }
  printf '%s\n' "$v"
}
si_p1_image() { # the backup and drill image, ghcr.io/sentioxyz/sentio-node:sha-<commit>@<digest> with SN_COMMIT_P1 and SN_DIGEST_P1 from $si_backup/pins
  local c d
  c="$(si_p1_pin SN_COMMIT_P1)" && d="$(si_p1_pin SN_DIGEST_P1)" || return 1
  printf 'ghcr.io/sentioxyz/sentio-node:sha-%s@%s\n' "$c" "$d"
}
si_p1_owner() { # $1 a|b|c: that owner's SI indexer id (indexer-c's from the pins)
  case "$1" in
    a) echo 0 ;; b) echo 1 ;; c) si_p1_pin INDEXER_C_ID ;;
    *) echo "si_p1_owner: the owner is a, b or c, not '$1'" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
}
si_p1_installation() { # $1 a|b|c: the SI ClickHouse installation that owner's source belongs to
  case "$1" in
    a) echo network ;; b|c) echo "indexer-$1" ;;
    *) echo "si_p1_installation: the owner is a, b or c, not '$1'" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
}
si_p1_chi() { # $1 a|b|c: the CHI of that owner's installation
  case "$1" in
    a) echo storage-integrity-si-v2 ;; b|c) echo "storage-integrity-si-v2-indexer-$1" ;;
    *) echo "si_p1_chi: the owner is a, b or c, not '$1'" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
}
si_p1_rpc_url() { # $1 a|b|c: that owner host's storage RPC inside the namespace (restore-drill --owner-rpc)
  case "$1" in
    a) echo http://sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-a:32003 ;; b) echo http://sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-b:33003 ;; c) echo http://sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-c:34003 ;;
    *) echo "si_p1_rpc_url: the owner is a, b or c, not '$1'" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
}
si_p1_cronjob() { # $1 a|b|c: that owner's backup CronJob
  case "$1" in
    a|b|c) echo "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$1-si-backup" ;;
    *) echo "si_p1_cronjob: the owner is a, b or c, not '$1'" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
}
si_p1_account() { # $1 key account: prints it when it is one of the eight of §3
  local c

  case "$1" in
    backup-0|backup-1|"backup-$c"|backup-mech|restore-a|restore-b|restore-c|restore-drill) echo "$1" ;;
    *) echo "si_p1_account: $1 is not a key account of §3" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
}
# Runs inside a ClickHouse pod: $1 user, $2 query; the password arrives on stdin and leaves only through CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD; S3 retries are off, so a statement that names an unreachable endpoint answers at once.
# shellcheck disable=SC2016
si_p1_inpod_client='
user=$1 query=$2
IFS= read -r CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD || [ -n "$CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD" ] || { echo "no password on stdin for $user" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -n "$CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD" ] || { echo "empty password for $user" >&2; exit 2; }
export CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD
exec clickhouse-client --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9000 --user "$user" --backup_restore_s3_retry_attempts 0 --s3_retry_attempts 0 --query "$query"
'
si_p1s_as() { # $1 user of the P1 staging installation, $2 query: one query as that user over loopback in the staging pod; the password goes from the staging logins Secret straight into kubectl exec stdin
  case "$1" in
    default|si_snode|si_gateway|si_reader|si_backup|si_restore) ;;
    *) echo "si_p1s_as: the P1 staging installation has no user '$1'" >&2; return 2 ;;
  esac
  si_kubectl get secret "$si_p1s_logins" -o "go-template={{index .data \"$1\"}}" | base64 -d |
    si_kubectl exec -i "$si_p1s_pod" -c clickhouse -- sh -c "$si_p1_inpod_client" sh "$1" "$2"
}
si_p1s_ch() { si_p1s_as default "$1"; } # $1 query: as default over loopback on the P1 staging installation

si_s3_inpod="$(cat <<'INPOD'
IFS= read -r CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD || exit 2
IFS= read -r SI_S3_ID || exit 2
IFS= read -r SI_S3_SECRET || exit 2
[ -n "$CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD" ] && [ -n "$SI_S3_ID" ] && [ -n "$SI_S3_SECRET" ] || { echo "si_s3_sql: a password, an access id or a secret arrived empty" >&2; exit 2; }
export CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD SI_S3_ID SI_S3_SECRET
command -v awk > /dev/null || { echo "si_s3_sql: this pod has no awk" >&2; exit 2; }
rep='function rep(s, pat, val,   out, i) { out = ""; while ((i = index(s, pat)) > 0) { out = out substr(s, 1, i - 1) val; s = substr(s, i + length(pat)) } return out s }'
{ awk "$rep"' { print rep(rep($0, "@@S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID@@", ENVIRON["SI_S3_ID"]), "@@S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY@@", ENVIRON["SI_S3_SECRET"]) }' |
  clickhouse-client --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9000 --user default --multiquery --backup_restore_s3_retry_attempts 10 --s3_retry_attempts 10 2>&1
  echo "si_s3_sql_exit=$?"; } | awk "$rep"' { print rep($0, ENVIRON["SI_S3_SECRET"], "[HIDDEN]") }'
INPOD
)"
si_s3_sql() { # $1 key account, $2 SQL file: the file's statements as default on the P1 staging installation only, with @@S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID@@ and @@S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY@@ replaced inside the pod by the access id and secret of Secret storage-integrity-si-v2-<account>; both, and default's password, travel on stdin only, the output has the secret masked, and the return status is clickhouse-client's
  local out rc
  si_p1_account "$1" > /dev/null || return 2
  [ -s "$2" ] || { echo "si_s3_sql: $2 is missing or empty" >&2; return 2; }
  out="$( {
    si_kubectl get secret "$si_p1s_logins" -o 'go-template={{index .data "default"}}' | base64 -d | tr -d '\n'; printf '\n'
    si_kubectl get secret "storage-integrity-si-v2-$1" -o 'go-template={{index .data "access-id"}}' | base64 -d | tr -d '\n'; printf '\n'
    si_kubectl get secret "storage-integrity-si-v2-$1" -o 'go-template={{index .data "secret"}}' | base64 -d | tr -d '\n'; printf '\n'
    cat "$2"
  } | si_kubectl exec -i "$si_p1s_pod" -c clickhouse -- sh -c "$si_s3_inpod")" || { printf '%s\n' "$out"; echo "si_s3_sql: the staging pod refused the run" >&2; return 1; }
  rc="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^si_s3_sql_exit=\([0-9][0-9]*\)$/\1/p' | tail -n 1)"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -v '^si_s3_sql_exit=' || true
  [ -n "$rc" ] || { echo "si_s3_sql: the pod reported no exit status" >&2; return 1; }
  return "$rc"
}
si_secret_hits() { # $1 key account: reads text on stdin and prints how many of its lines contain that account's secret; the secret comes from its Secret through file descriptor 3, never argv, and is never printed
  si_p1_account "$1" > /dev/null || return 2
  python3 -I -c 'import sys
with open(3) as f:
    secret = f.read().strip()
if len(secret) < 16:
    sys.exit("si_secret_hits: the secret of this account is missing or too short")
print(sum(1 for line in sys.stdin if secret in line))' 3< <(si_kubectl get secret "storage-integrity-si-v2-$1" -o 'go-template={{index .data "secret"}}' | base64 -d)
}
si_s3_outcome() { # $1 si_s3_sql's return status, stdin its output: ok, denied (403 or AccessDenied), missing (404 or NoSuchKey), exists (598 or an existing object) or error
  if [ "$1" = 0 ]; then cat > /dev/null; echo ok; return 0; fi
  python3 -I -c 'import re, sys
t = sys.stdin.read()
if re.search(r"AccessDenied|Access denied|ACCESS_DENIED|response code: 403|Forbidden", t, re.I):
    print("denied")
elif re.search(r"NoSuchKey|response code: 404|The specified key does not exist", t):
    print("missing")
elif re.search(r"Code: 598\.|BACKUP_ALREADY_EXISTS|Code: 36\..*already exists", t):
    print("exists")
else:
    print("error")'
}
si_p1_check() { # $1 check, $2 expect, $3 got: appends one row to $si_backup/mechanics-gcs.tsv and prints PASS or FAIL
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$2" "$3" >> "$si_backup/mechanics-gcs.tsv"
  if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then echo "PASS $1: $3"; else echo "FAIL $1: expected $2, got $3"; fi
}
si_p1_probe() { # $1 check, $2 expect, $3 key account, $4 one SQL statement with the @@ placeholders: runs it with si_s3_sql on the staging installation and records its outcome (si_s3_outcome); its masked output goes to mechanics-gcs.log
  local f out rc=0 got
  f="$(mktemp "$si_backup/sql/probe.XXXXXX")" || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$4" > "$f"
  out="$(si_s3_sql "$3" "$f" 2>&1)" || rc=$?
  got="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | si_s3_outcome "$rc")"
  printf '== %s (%s, exit %s)\n%s\n' "$1" "$3" "$rc" "$out" >> "$si_backup/mechanics-gcs.log"
  si_p1_check "$1" "$2" "$got"
}
si_p1s_grant_probe() { # the committed grant-probe corpus on the P1 staging installation, in file order, each row as its role (si_p1s_as); rows of si_verifier, which the P1 staging installation does not have (the lockdown runbook's staging probe ran them), print as skipped; fails on a row whose outcome differs from its expect column and on a default row that does not succeed outright
  local corpus=charts/storage-integrity/tests/clickhouse_grant_probe.tsv role expect stmt out code got n=0 bad=0 skipped=0
  [ -s "$corpus" ] || { echo "$corpus is missing" >&2; return 2; }
  printf 'row\trole\texpect\tgot\tcode\tstatement\n'
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r role expect stmt <&3 || [ -n "$role" ]; do
    case "$role" in ''|'#'*|role) continue ;; esac
    n=$((n + 1))
    case "$role" in
      default|si_snode|si_gateway|si_reader|si_backup|si_restore) ;;
      *) printf '%s\t%s\t%s\tskipped\t-\t%s\n' "$n" "$role" "$expect" "$stmt"; skipped=$((skipped + 1)); continue ;;
    esac
    if out="$(si_p1s_as "$role" "$stmt" 2>&1)"; then code=0; else code=""; fi
    if [ -z "$code" ]; then
      code="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*Code: \([0-9][0-9]*\)\..*/\1/p' | head -n 1)"
      code="${code:-unknown}"
    fi
    case "$code" in
      0) got=ok ;;
      497) got=denied ;;
      209|210|unknown) got=error ;;
      # 516 is an error when this row's own login failed; a remote() leg that cannot log in answers 516 after the access check passed.
      516) if [ "$role" != default ] && ! printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q " $role: Authentication failed"; then got=ok; else got=error; fi ;;
      *) if [ "$role" = default ]; then got=error; else got=ok; fi ;;
    esac
    [ "$got" = "$expect" ] || bad=$((bad + 1))
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$n" "$role" "$expect" "$got" "$code" "$stmt"
  done 3< "$corpus"
  [ "$n" -gt "$skipped" ] || { echo "the corpus has no row the P1 staging installation can run" >&2; return 2; }
  [ "$bad" = 0 ] || { echo "$bad of $((n - skipped)) rows differ from their expect column" >&2; return 1; }
  echo "every row of $((n - skipped)) is as expected; $skipped rows of roles without a P1 staging login skipped" >&2
}
si_index() { # $1 a|b|c, $2 backup name: that owner's index object <name>.index.json, read on the P1 staging installation with the restore-drill key, as one JSON line
  local owner f
  owner="$(si_p1_owner "$1")" || return 2
  [[ "$2" =~ ^[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z-(full|incr)$ ]] || { echo "si_index: '$2' is not a backup name" >&2; return 2; }
  f="$(mktemp "$si_backup/sql/index.XXXXXX")" || return 1
  printf "SELECT raw_blob FROM s3('%s/owner-%s/%s.index.json', '@@S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID@@', '@@S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY@@', 'RawBLOB', 'raw_blob String') FORMAT TSVRaw\n" "$si_p1_bucket_url" "$owner" "$2" > "$f"
  si_s3_sql restore-drill "$f" | python3 -I -c 'import json, sys
print(json.dumps(json.loads(sys.stdin.read()), separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True))'
}
si_indexes() { # $1 a|b|c: the names of that owner's backups (its index objects), sorted, read on the P1 staging installation with the restore-drill key; nothing for an owner without a backup
  local owner f
  owner="$(si_p1_owner "$1")" || return 2
  f="$(mktemp "$si_backup/sql/indexes.XXXXXX")" || return 1
  printf "SELECT substring(_file, 1, length(_file) - 11) AS name FROM s3('%s/owner-%s/*.index.json', '@@S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID@@', '@@S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY@@', 'RawBLOB', 'raw_blob String') ORDER BY name FORMAT TSV\n" "$si_p1_bucket_url" "$owner" > "$f"
  si_s3_sql restore-drill "$f"
}
si_host_pods() { # $1 a|b|c: uid, start time and every container's restart count of that owner's host pod and of its source ClickHouse pod, one line each
  local p
  si_p1_owner "$1" > /dev/null || return 2
  for p in "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$1-0" "$(si_ch_pod "$1")"; do
    si_kubectl get pod "$p" -o jsonpath='{.metadata.name} uid={.metadata.uid} started={.status.startTime} restarts={range .status.containerStatuses[*]}{.name}:{.restartCount} {end}{"\n"}' || return 1
  done
}
si_p1_pods_check() { # $1 a|b|c, $2 label: writes host-pods-<x>-<label>.txt and fails unless it equals host-pods-<x>-before.txt of §1.3, the StatefulSet of the host keeps its revisions, and, for a, no arbiter or verifier pod was replaced
  local f="$si_backup/host-pods-$1-$2.txt"
  [ -s "$si_backup/host-pods-$1-before.txt" ] || { echo "no host-pods-$1-before.txt: run §1.3 first" >&2; return 1; }
  si_host_pods "$1" > "$f" || return 1
  if ! diff "$si_backup/host-pods-$1-before.txt" "$f" >&2; then echo "indexer-$1: a host or source ClickHouse pod changed or restarted since §1.3: stop (§14)" >&2; return 1; fi
  si_kubectl get statefulset "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$1" -o jsonpath='{.metadata.generation} {.status.currentRevision} {.status.updateRevision}{"\n"}' | diff "$si_backup/sts-$1-before.txt" - >&2 || { echo "indexer-$1: its StatefulSet changed since §1.3: stop (§14)" >&2; return 1; }
  if [ "$1" = a ]; then si_runtime_uids | diff "$si_backup/runtime-uids-before.txt" - >&2 || { echo "an arbiter or verifier pod was replaced since §1.3: stop (§14)" >&2; return 1; }; fi
  echo "indexer-$1: host and source ClickHouse pods unchanged since §1.3 ($2)"
}
si_p1_wait_backup_user() { # $1 a|b|c|v1|v2|v3: waits up to 5 minutes until system.users of that server lists si_backup with a SHA-256 password from any address; never waits on the CHI status
  local n got=""
  for n in $(seq 1 30); do
    got="$(si_ch_admin "$1" "SELECT name, auth_type, host_ip FROM system.users WHERE name = 'si_backup' FORMAT JSONEachRow" 2>/dev/null)" || got=""
    [ "$got" = '{"name":"si_backup","auth_type":["sha256_password"],"host_ip":["::\/0"]}' ] && { echo "host $1: si_backup is in system.users"; return 0; }
    sleep 10
  done
  echo "host $1: si_backup did not reach system.users within 5 minutes (last answer: ${got:-none})" >&2
  return 1
}
si_p1_grants() { # $1 a|b|c|v1|v2|v3, $2 si_backup|si_restore: that user's system.grants rows on that server (si_ch_admin), or on the P1 staging installation for $1 = staging, one JSON line each
  local q="SELECT user_name, access_type, access_object, database, table, column, is_partial_revoke, grant_option FROM system.grants WHERE user_name = '$2' ORDER BY access_type, access_object, database, table FORMAT JSONEachRow"
  case "$2" in si_backup|si_restore) ;; *) echo "si_p1_grants: si_backup or si_restore, not '$2'" >&2; return 2 ;; esac
  if [ "$1" = staging ]; then si_p1s_ch "$q"; else si_ch_admin "$1" "$q"; fi
}
si_p1_backup_login() { # $1 a|b|c|v1|v2|v3: logs in as si_backup over loopback with the installation's backup Secret and prints "host <h>: si_backup ok" when the server names si_backup
  local pod inst got
  pod="$(si_ch_pod "$1")" && inst="$(si_installation "$1")" || return 2
  got="$(si_kubectl get secret "storage-integrity-si-v2-clickhouse-backup-$inst" -o 'go-template={{index .data "password"}}' | base64 -d |
    si_kubectl exec -i "$pod" -c clickhouse -- sh -c "$si_inpod_client" sh raw si_backup "SELECT currentUser()")" || { echo "host $1: si_backup cannot log in" >&2; return 1; }
  [ "$got" = si_backup ] || { echo "host $1: si_backup logged in as $got" >&2; return 1; }
  echo "host $1: si_backup ok"
}
si_p1_servers() { # $1 a|b|c: the ClickHouse servers of that owner's installation (users are installation-wide)
  case "$1" in a) echo a v1 v2 v3 ;; b|c) echo "$1" ;; *) echo "si_p1_servers: the owner is a, b or c, not '$1'" >&2; return 2 ;; esac
}
si_p1_fresh_main() { # fails unless the checkout is at a freshly fetched origin/main with no uncommitted change
  git fetch -q origin main || return 1
  local git_read_1 git_read_2
  git_read_1="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" || return 1
  git_read_2="$(git rev-parse origin/main)" || return 1
  [[ "$git_read_1" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ && "$git_read_2" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || return 1
  [ "$git_read_1" = "$git_read_2" ] || { echo "the checkout is not at origin/main: git checkout --detach origin/main first" >&2; return 1; }
  local git_read_3
  git_read_3="$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no)" || return 1
  [ -z "$git_read_3" ] || { echo "the checkout has uncommitted changes" >&2; return 1; }
}
si_p1_tests() { # $1 log name: runs the render tests into $si_backup/tests-<name>.txt and fails unless they pass
  python3 -B charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py > "$si_backup/tests-$1.txt" 2>&1 || { tail -n 30 "$si_backup/tests-$1.txt" >&2; echo "the render tests fail: git reset --hard origin/main and stop" >&2; return 1; }
  tail -n 3 "$si_backup/tests-$1.txt"
}
si_p1_user_commit() { # $1 a|b|c, local only: the single-service commit that adds si_backup to that owner's installation from its hashes file, with the DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP_USER mirror; prints the commit
  local workflow_commit_before workflow_commit_after workflow_identity
  local inst chi file hashes subject
  case "$1" in a) subject="the network ClickHouse installation" ;; b|c) subject="indexer-$1's ClickHouse" ;; *) return 2 ;; esac
  inst="$(si_p1_installation "$1")" && chi="$(si_p1_chi "$1")" || return 2
  si_p1_fresh_main || return 1
  hashes="$si_p1_logins_dir/hashes-si_backup-$inst.yaml"
  if [ "$1" = a ]; then
    file=k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.yaml
    si_p1_py values-add-user "$file" "$hashes" || return 1
  else
    file="k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2-$inst-source.yaml"
    si_p1_py chi-add-user "$file" "$hashes" || return 1
  fi
  si_p1_py mirror charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP_USER "$chi" True || return 1
  si_p1_tests "si-backup-user-$inst" || return 1
  git add -- "$file" charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py || return 1
  git config --worktree commit.gpgsign true || return 1
  workflow_commit_before="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" || return 1
  git commit -q -m "chore(devnet2): si_backup on $subject (stage-3 P1)" -m "Adds the installation-wide backup user si_backup (literal SHA-256 hash, exactly SI_BACKUP_GRANTS) to $chi as a users reload, and its DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP_USER mirror (docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p1-backups.md §6)." -m "$si_p1_trailer" || { echo "commit/signing failed; preserve staged work and ask the user to unlock this repository actual signing key; no unsigned fallback" >&2; return 1; }
  workflow_commit_after="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" || return 1
  [ "$workflow_commit_after" != "$workflow_commit_before" ] || { echo "commit produced no new HEAD; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  workflow_identity="$(git log -1 --format='%an <%ae> %G?')" || return 1
  [ "$workflow_identity" = 'poetry <chen@sentio.xyz> G' ] || { echo "new HEAD must be poetry <chen@sentio.xyz> G; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  git verify-commit HEAD || return 1
  git show --stat --oneline HEAD | cat
}
si_p1_user_apply() { # $1 a|b|c, mutating (only in a confirmed block): pushes si_p1_user_commit's commit to main, applies the CHI file (b, c) or syncs storage-integrity-si-v2 (a), waits for si_backup on every server of the installation and proves it: grants, login, nothing restarted
  local inst chi file h servers
  inst="$(si_p1_installation "$1")" && chi="$(si_p1_chi "$1")" && servers="$(si_p1_servers "$1")" || return 2
  [ ! -e "$si_backup/si-backup-user-$inst-commit" ] || { echo "si-backup-user-$inst-commit exists: this step ran; never re-run it" >&2; return 1; }
  if [ "$1" = a ]; then file=k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.yaml; else file="k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2-$inst-source.yaml"; fi
  si_head_is charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py "$file" || return 1
  si_p1_tests "si-backup-user-$inst-apply" || return 1
  if [ "$1" = a ]; then
    si_render_diff storage-integrity-si-v2 > "$si_backup/render-si-backup-user-network.txt" || return 1
    [ "$(cat "$si_backup/render-si-backup-user-network.txt")" = "changed ClickHouseInstallation/storage-integrity-si-v2" ] || { cat "$si_backup/render-si-backup-user-network.txt" >&2; echo "the commit renders more than the network CHI differently: stop" >&2; return 1; }
  else
    si_kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f "$file" -o json |
      jq -e '.spec.configuration.users | has("si_backup/password_sha256_hex") and has("si_backup/grants/query") and (has("si_restore/password_sha256_hex") | not)' > /dev/null || { echo "the server dry run does not show si_backup: stop" >&2; return 1; }
  fi
  git rev-parse HEAD > "$si_backup/si-backup-user-$inst-commit" || return 1
  git push origin HEAD:main || return 1
  if [ "$1" = a ]; then
    helmfile -f k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/storage-integrity-si-v2.helmfile.yaml sync --selector name=storage-integrity-si-v2 || return 1
  else
    si_kubectl apply -f "$file" || return 1
  fi
  for h in $servers; do si_p1_wait_backup_user "$h" || return 1; done
  si_wait_chi "$chi" || return 1
  si_chi_state "$chi" > "$si_backup/chi-$inst-after-si-backup-user.txt" || return 1
  diff "$si_backup/chi-$inst-before.txt" "$si_backup/chi-$inst-after-si-backup-user.txt" >&2 || { echo "a pod or StatefulSet of $chi changed: stop (§14)" >&2; return 1; }
  for h in $servers; do
    si_p1_grants "$h" si_backup > "$si_backup/grants-si_backup-$h.jsonl" || return 1
    si_p1_py grants-check si_backup "$si_backup/grants-si_backup-$h.jsonl" || return 1
    si_p1_backup_login "$h" || return 1
  done
  if [ "$1" = a ]; then
    [ "$(si_kubectl get job storage-integrity-si-v2-bootstrap-source -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}')" = 1 ] || { echo "the bootstrap-source hook did not succeed" >&2; return 1; }
  fi
  si_p1_pods_check "$1" si-backup-user || return 1
  si_stamp > "$si_backup/si-backup-user-$inst-done"
}
si_p1_schedule_clear() { # $1 a|b|c: fails from 90 minutes before to 70 minutes after that owner's daily scheduled backup (its CronJob's schedule, or DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP_SCHEDULES before the CronJob exists; UTC), so a manual run or the first sync never meets a scheduled run
  local sched min hour now s d
  sched="$(si_kubectl get cronjob "$(si_p1_cronjob "$1")" --ignore-not-found -o jsonpath='{.spec.schedule}')" || return 1
  if [ -z "$sched" ]; then
    sched="$(python3 -I -B -c 'import os, sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("charts/storage-integrity/tests"))
import test_render
print(test_render.DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP_SCHEDULES["sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-" + sys.argv[1]])' "$1")" || return 1
  fi
  read -r min hour _ <<< "$sched"
  [[ "$min" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$hour" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || { echo "unexpected schedule '$sched'" >&2; return 1; }
  now=$((10#$(date -u +%H) * 60 + 10#$(date -u +%M)))
  s=$((hour * 60 + min))
  d=$(( (s - now + 1440) % 1440 ))
  if [ "$d" -le 90 ] || [ "$d" -ge 1370 ]; then
    printf "indexer-%s's backup is scheduled at %02d:%02d UTC: run this block from 70 minutes after it until 90 minutes before the next one\n" "$1" "$hour" "$min" >&2
    return 1
  fi
}
si_p1_job_commit() { # $1 a|b|c, local only: the single-service commit that turns that owner's backup CronJob on (siBackup.enabled) with its DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP mirror; prints the commit
  local workflow_commit_before workflow_commit_after workflow_identity
  local file="k8s-sea/sentio-network-devnet2/sentio-node-indexer-$1-storage-integrity-si-v2.yaml"
  si_p1_owner "$1" > /dev/null || return 2
  si_p1_fresh_main || return 1
  si_p1_py enable-backup "$file" || return 1
  si_p1_py mirror charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP "sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$1" True || return 1
  si_p1_tests "si-backup-$1" || return 1
  git add -- "$file" charts/storage-integrity/tests/test_render.py || return 1
  git config --worktree commit.gpgsign true || return 1
  workflow_commit_before="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" || return 1
  git commit -q -m "chore(devnet2): indexer-$1's stage-3 P1 backup CronJob" -m "Turns on sentio-node-devnet2-indexer-$1's siBackup CronJob (a ConfigMap and a CronJob outside the host checksum; the host StatefulSet renders unchanged) and its DEVNET2_SI_BACKUP mirror (docs/storage-integrity-devnet2-stage3-p1-backups.md §8)." -m "$si_p1_trailer" || { echo "commit/signing failed; preserve staged work and ask the user to unlock this repository actual signing key; no unsigned fallback" >&2; return 1; }
  workflow_commit_after="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" || return 1
  [ "$workflow_commit_after" != "$workflow_commit_before" ] || { echo "commit produced no new HEAD; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  workflow_identity="$(git log -1 --format='%an <%ae> %G?')" || return 1
  [ "$workflow_identity" = 'poetry <chen@sentio.xyz> G' ] || { echo "new HEAD must be poetry <chen@sentio.xyz> G; stop" >&2; return 1; }
  git verify-commit HEAD || return 1
  git show --stat --oneline HEAD | cat
}
si_p1_job_apply() { # $1 a|b|c, mutating (only in a confirmed block): pushes si_p1_job_commit's commit to main and syncs that host's release only; the render adds exactly the CronJob and its ConfigMap, the CronJob runs si_p1_image with exactly three Secret env vars, and no pod restarts
````
